en: ART Enabled by micro-TESE in Bosma Arhinia Microphthalmia Syndrome
ja: Bosma無鼻小眼球症候群におけるmicro-TESEによるART
abs: Background: Bosma arhinia microphthalmia syndrome is a rare congenital disorder caused by SMCHD1 mutations and characterized by hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Male reproductive potential in this condition remains largely unknown, and reports on sperm retrieval are extremely limited. Case: A 38-year-old man with congenital arhinia and a history of bilateral cryptorchidism was diagnosed with BAMS based on a pathogenic SMCHD1 variant (c.1568C>A). He had been treated with gonadotropins for hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Semen analysis revealed azoospermia, and testicular volumes were approximately 3 mL bilaterally. Intervention and Outcome: Microdissection testicular sperm extraction (micro-TESE) was performed on the right testis under ongoing hormonal therapy. Five immotile, morphologically abnormal sperm were successfully retrieved and cryopreserved. Histopathological findings demonstrated maturation arrest with a Johnsen score of 3. Discussion and Future Perspective: Despite severe spermatogenic impairment, sperm retrieval was achieved, suggesting the presence of focal spermatogenesis. Hormonal therapy may have contributed to this outcome. Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) is planned using the cryopreserved sperm. The patient has expressed interest in preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic disorders (PGT-M); genetic counseling will be provided, and submission will be considered. Continued hormonal therapy and contralateral micro- TESE may be considered if necessary.

en: Cases of three women with Xq microdeletions and diminished ovarian reserve who performed PGT-SR
ja: Xq微小欠失と卵巣予備能低下を有しPGT-SRを行った女性3例
abs: Background: The long arm of the X-chromosome (Xq) contains several genes essential for maintaining ovarian function. Deletions in this region are associated to diminished ovarian reserve (DOR). Here, we report on three couples who underwent PGT-SR due to maternal carriage of an Xq microdeletion. Case1: The couple was a 43-year-old woman (G0P0) with karyotype 46,X,del(X)(q27)[28]/45,X[2] and a 50-year-old man with normal karyotype. Her AMH was 0.186 (the median for her age was 1.13). She underwent egg retrieval with PGT- SR once, but was unable to obtain any eggs. Case2: The couple was a 33-year-old woman (G2P0SA2) with karyotype 46,X,del(X) (q22.3q24) and a 35-year-old man with normal karyotype. Her AMH was 0.524 (median 2.91). She underwent egg retrieval once, but the fertilized eggs did not develop to blastocyst, so PGT-SR could not be done. Case3: The couple was a 33-year-old woman (G1P0SA1) with karyotype 46,X,del(X)(q26) and a 33-year-old man with normal karyotype. Her AMH was 0.339 (median 2.91). Although egg retrievals were performed five times with PGT-SR, only three aneuploid blastocysts were obtained: one with an Xq microdeletion and two without. Conclusion: It has been suggested that Xq microdeletions are significant contributor to DOR independent of maternal age, and that female carriers of these deletions are predisposed to poor IVF outcomes. In cases where PGT-SR identifies an Xq microdeletion, a cautious approach to embryo transfer is recommended, given that X-chromosome inactivation complicates phenotype prediction.

en: DD twin pregnancy after double blastocyst transfer in a de novo X-chromosome deletion carrier: A case report
ja: de novo X染色体欠失保因者における2個胚盤胞移植後のDD双胎妊娠：症例報告
abs: [Background] X-chromosome structural abnormalities pose psychosocial challenges regarding offspring health and future fertility. We report the decision-making process toward double blastocyst transfer (DBT) in a de novo X-chromosome interstitial deletion carrier, supported by genomic analyses and serial genetic counseling (GC). [Case] A 30-year-old female had a karyotype of 46,X,del(X)(q23q25). G-banding identified POF1 region deletion, yet she exhibited a normal phenotype. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) on a parent-proband trio confirmed the de novo status; no pathogenic variants in infertility-related genes were found. Highly skewed X-inactivation (98.6%) was observed, indicating near-complete inactivation of the deleted X chromosome, explaining her normal phenotype. [Clinical Course] Five GC sessions addressed the risk of a female offspring inheriting the deletion and the ethical dilemmas of a discordant-outcome twin pregnancy. Confirmation of de novo status alleviated maternal self-blame and concerns about the patient's sisters. These insights supported her autonomous decision to proceed with DBT. Post-transfer amniotic fluid chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA) confirmed that neither twin inherited the deletion. [Conclusion] Genomic insights -including de novo confirmation and X-inactivation patterns - alleviate familial concerns and maternal self-blame, supporting autonomous reproductive decisions amid persistent uncertainty. Consent for publication was obtained.

en: Reproductive Genetics Across Generations: A Case of Carrier Testing in an Adult Born Following PGT-M
ja: 世代を越える生殖遺伝：PGT-Mを経て出生した成人の保因者検査の1例
abs: Background: Preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic disorders (PGT-M) is performed to prevent transmission of serious hereditary diseases. In Japan, PGT-M mainly aims to avoid affected offspring, while disclosure and management of carrier status remain unclear. We report a woman born following PGT-M who sought genetic counseling regarding carrier status and reproductive planning. Case: A 20-year-old woman visited our genetic counseling clinic with her mother. Her mother was diagnosed as a Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) carrier after her first son was diagnosed with DMD. PGT-M was subsequently performed, and the client was born following transfer of a non-affected embryo, although carrier status and sex selection had not been disclosed at that time. Prenatal diagnosis was not performed. The client had understood that DMD existed in her family and later learned that she had been born following PGT-M. After the death of her elder brother, she became interested in her genetic background. Although unmarried, she expressed a desire to have children in the future and stated that, if she were a carrier, she would consider reproductive options including PGT-M. During counseling, limitations of carrier testing were explained. Genetic testing was performed based on her decision. Conclusion: This case highlights transgenerational issues in reproductive genetics as individuals born following PGT-M begin making reproductive decisions themselves. Further discussion is needed regarding the management of carrier embryos and long-term disclosure of genetic information.

en: PGT-SR for a couple with paracentric inversion: suspected reunitant chromosome based on U-loop exchange
ja: 腕内逆位カップルへのPGT-SR：Uループ交換による再結合染色体の疑い
abs: Backbround: Paracentric inversion is generally considered to be a structural chromosome rearrangement that is unlikely to affect reproduction. In theory, phenotypically normal carriers of paracentric inversion will only produce offspring with a normal karyotype or the same balanced inversion. They cannot produce viable unbalanced progeny, since recombinant gametes would either have an acentric or dicentric chromosome. However exceptionally, a crossover within the inversion loop can reverse along the chromatid as a U-loop. This results in reuninant chromosomes with a duplication of part of the inversion loop and a deletion of the rest. Here, we present a couple with a paracentric inversion who obtained a blastocyst with U-loop reunitant suspective based on the results of preimplantation genetic testing for structural rearrangements (PGT-SR). Case report: This report presents a case of balanced paracentric inversion 46,inv(12)(p13.3p11.2) with a history of two spontaneous miscarriages, one healthy child, and one ectopic pregnancy. PGT-SR was initiated for a 39-year-old woman and a 43-year-old man. Out of 2 PGT-SR cycles, a total of 9 blastocysts were biopsied for array comparative genomic hybridization(aCGH) resulting in 2 euploid, 5 aneuploid, one mosaic, and one reuninant based on U-loop exchange. Conclusion: Pericentric inversions are generally not considered eligible for PGT-SR. However, based on this experience, close monitoring of PGT results is recommended for carriers of paracentric inversions, as well as those of other structural chromosomal rearrangements.

en: A Decade of Preimplantation Genetic Testing for Monogenic Disorders -Retrospective study at a Private Clinic-
ja: 単一遺伝子疾患に対する着床前遺伝学的検査の10年：民間クリニックでの後方視的研究
abs: Introduction: PGT-M at our clinic began in 2016 after approval by the JSOG for ALD. We retrospectively reviewed the backgrounds, application status, and outcomes of PGT-M cases over the past 10 years. Materials and Methods: The study participants comprised 137 couples who visited our clinic for genetic counseling regarding PGT- M between 2014 and April 2026. Results: Female age at first visit ranged from 23 to 45 years. Fifty two couples lived in Osaka Prefecture, and most were from the Kinki region, while others resided across 16 prefectures throughout Japan. Among 137 cases, 98 wished to apply for PGT-M, including 10 preparing applications. Of 88 completed applications, 64 were approved and 10 rejected; 14 remained under review or awaiting announcement. Three cases were undecided and 36 did not proceed to application. Of 64 approved cases, 57 underwent treatment. Transferable embryos were obtained in 55 cases, and embryo transfer was performed in 54. Live birth was achieved in 36 cases and 4 pregnancies were ongoing. The pregnancy rate per transfer cycle was 55.0%, with a miscarriage rate of 21.7%. Among 11 cases without live birth, 8 involved women aged over 38 years and 3 had DM1. Conclusion: Female age at first visit ranged widely, and couples resided throughout Japan. Ratio of couples who did not proceed to application is increasing because of procedural complexity, review duration, financial burden, and treatment logistics. Outcomes were generally favorable but influenced by maternal age and underlying disease.

en: A case of suspected mosaic trisomy 21 involving NIPT through the after giving birth
ja: 出生後にNIPTが関与したモザイク21トリソミー疑いの1例
abs: Background: We have experienced a case where mosaic trisomy21(T21) was suspected after two consecutive NIPT results indicated Non-reportable T21. Case: A 31y multiparous woman. Her partner is of the same sex, and she conceived through assisted reproductive technology, receiving sperm donation just like with her first child. During her first pregnancy, after gender-sensitive NIPT counseling, she took the test, and the result was negative. For this pregnancy as well, she took the test after similar consideration NIPT counseling. The initial result was Non-reportable T21, and a re-examination also resulted in Non-reportable T21. At this point, mosaic T21 was suspected. Amniocentesis revealed T21 in 3 out of 80 cells using the FISH , and in 3 out of 20 cells using G-banding. However, a fetal screening at another facility at 19 weeks showed no findings suggestive of T21. At 20 weeks, she met with a Board Certified Pediatrician for Prenatal Consultation, who explained the limitations of interpreting mosaicism ratios in amniocentesis, provided information on mosaic T21, and informed her that the baby would receive health management at our hospital after birth. She came to the realization that her child would likely be able to become independent in the future, and chose to continue the pregnancy, which led to the birth. After birth, the baby did not show T21 using G-banding or FISH. Discussion: This case highlighted the importance of gender-sensitive information provision at each stage, collaboration with Board Certified Pediatrician, and information sharing with another facility.

en: Two Cases of Prenatal Diagnosis in Pregnancies Complicated by Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1 at Different Stages of Diagnosis
ja: 診断時期の異なる筋強直性ジストロフィー1型合併妊娠の出生前診断2例
abs: In pregnancies complicated by myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1), prenatal genetic testing and preimplantation genetic testing are important clinical issues. We report two cases of prenatal genetic testing in DM1-complicated pregnancies with different diagnostic backgrounds. Case 1 was a 29-year-old woman referred after pregnancy was established because DM1 was suspected from her family history and myotonic symptoms. Genetic testing in the Department of Neurology confirmed DM1. While awaiting the result, she requested prenatal genetic testing, and amniotic fluid testing was performed at 16 weeks of gestation. No CTG repeat expansion was detected in either allele. Post-test genetic counseling was provided, and the pregnancy is ongoing. Case 2 was a 19-year-old woman diagnosed with DM1 at age 15 and followed at a local neurology clinic. After pregnancy was confirmed, she requested prenatal genetic testing and was referred to our hospital. Amniotic fluid testing at 16 weeks revealed CTG repeat expansion in one allele. During the waiting period, fetal ventriculomegaly was detected by ultrasonography. After post-test genetic counseling, the client and her partner decided to terminate the pregnancy. In both cases, prenatal genetic testing was requested only after pregnancy had been established, and sufficient information had not been provided by the primary specialty. For patients with monogenic disorders, a seamless transitional care model connecting adult care specialties with clinical genetics services should be established when they reach reproductive age or plan pregnancy.

en: Current Status After the Introduction of Non-Invasive Prenatal Testing (NIPT) at Our Hospital
ja: 当院におけるNIPT導入後の現状
abs: [Introduction] Before accreditation as NIPT facility, our hospital referred patients requesting NIPT to institutions within and outside the prefecture. We are also an NIPT-accredited facility that has been offering NIPT since April 2025, and we would like to report on the current status following its implementation. [Methods] We retrospectively analyzed 124 patients who requested NIPT between April 2025 and March 2026. Reasons for consultation were classified as advanced maternal age (A), previous pregnancy with chromosomal aneuploidy (B), Robertsonian translocation (C), abnormal ultrasound findings (D), family history (E), and maternal anxiety (F). Mean maternal age was 35.0 years. 82 patients (66.1%) were referred from surrounding clinics/hospitals, while 42 (33.9%) received prenatal care at our hospital. Conception methods were spontaneous conception in 67 cases (69.1%), artificial insemination in 5 (5.2%), and assisted reproductive technology (ART) in 25 (25.8%). [Results] Reasons for consultation by conception method (%) were : spontaneous conception, A 50.7, B 1.5, D 9.0, E 3.0, F 35.7; artificial insemination, A 40.0, E 20.0, F 40.0; ART, A 64.0, B 20.0, C 4.0, D 4.0, F 8.0. The positive rate was 1.6% (2/123). [Conclusion] Since the introduction of NIPT, 66.1% of patients were referred from nearby facilities, suggesting improved accessibility. In addition, as the population of women undergoing ART is aging, NIPT was requested not only because of advanced maternal age but also because of previous pregnancies affected by chromosomal aneuploidy.

en: Postnatal course of fetal-onset renal anomaly in Zhu-Tokita-Takenouchi-Kim syndrome with a novel SON variant
ja: 新規SONバリアントによるZhu-Tokita-Takenouchi-Kim症候群の胎児期発症腎異常の出生後経過
abs: Zhu-Tokita-Takenouchi-Kim (ZTTK) syndrome is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder caused by de novo loss-of-function variants in the SON gene. Renal anomalies are reported in 38-42% of postnatal cases; however, fetal-onset renal involvement and its long-term outcome have not been previously documented. A 39-year-old woman (G2P1) conceived spontaneously. At 21 weeks of gestation, ultrasound demonstrated oligohydramnios and right multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK), indicating early-onset renal involvement, along with enlarged cisterna magna. Cerebellar hypoplasia was detected at 25 weeks and confirmed by fetal MRI. Fetal growth restriction became evident at 28 weeks, and the renal findings persisted. Emergency cesarean section was performed at 34 weeks due to non-reassuring fetal status; a male infant weighing 1678 g was delivered. Postnatal ultrasonography confirmed the prenatal findings, showing left renal hypoplasia and right MCDK. Trio exome sequencing identified a novel de novo heterozygous frameshift variant in SON (NM_138927.4:c.1391del), confirmed by Sanger sequencing, establishing the diagnosis. On day 2 of life, idiopathic gastric perforation occurred and was treated surgically. The patient has subsequently required repeated hospitalisations due to late dumping syndrome. Renal function, already compromised by bilateral congenital anomalies, has progressively deteriorated, and dialysis is now under consideration. This is the first report of ZTTK syndrome with renal involvement detected in the fetal period, which led to postnatal impaired renal function.

en: A Case of Mosaic Trisomy 2 Detected by Amniocentesis with a Normal Karyotype After Birth
ja: 羊水検査でモザイク2トリソミーを検出し出生後核型正常であった1例
abs: Mosaic trisomy 2 is a rare chromosomal abnormality and has been reported to be associated with craniofacial anomalies and fetal growth restriction . Here, we report a case in which fetal growth restriction was evident from first trimester, amniocentesis revealed mosaic trisomy2, while a normal karyotype was confirmed postnatally. Case: A late forties woman conceived following the transfer of an embryo confirmed as euploid by PGT-A. At 10 weeks of gestation, the crown rump length corresponded to 9 weeks. Due to persistent fetal growth restriction, a chromosomal abnormality was suspected, and amniocentesis was performed. Cytogenetic analysis revealed mosaic trisomy 2 (47,XX,+2[5]/46,XX[10]). In the absence of apparent structural anomalies, the pregnancy was managed expectantly. Although growth restriction persisted, no abnormalities in fetal doppler studies or amniotic fluid volume were observed. At 38 weeks and 6 days of gestation, a female infant weighting 2118 g was delivered. Postnatal cytogenetic analysis demonstrated mosaic trisomy 2 in the placenta, whereas the neonatal peripheral blood karyotype was normal. Discussion: Previous studies have reported that mosaic trisomy 2 is associated with fetal growth restriction, oligohydramnios, and craniofacial abnormalities. In addition, cases similar to ours have been described, in which mosaicism detected by amniocentesis was not confirmed postnatally. Owing to the variable clinical outcomes of mosaic trisomy 2, meticulous longitudinal evaluation using ultrasound is essential for appropriate perinatal management.

en: Fetal Bilateral Multicystic Kidneys Leading to Potter Sequence in Two Siblings with TMEM67 Variants
ja: TMEM67バリアントを有する同胞2例の胎児両側多嚢胞腎によるPotter sequence
abs: TMEM67 is a gene associated with ciliopathies, including Meckel and Joubert syndromes, which frequently involve renal abnormalities. Severe fetal renal dysfunction can lead to oligohydramnios and subsequent Potter sequence, characterized by pulmonary hypoplasia due to oligohydramnios. A 32-year-old woman was referred to our hospital for fetal renal abnormalities at 17 weeks of gestation. She had one healthy son, and the family history was otherwise unremarkable. Ultrasonography revealed enlarged hyperechoic kidneys with bilateral cysts of varying sizes, suggestive of multicystic dysplastic kidneys, without other anomalies. Although amniotic fluid was initially preserved, severe oligohydramnios subsequently developed, leading to Potter sequence. The infant was delivered at 34 weeks and died shortly after birth from respiratory failure. No genetic testing was performed at that time. Three years later, the subsequent fetus showed similar ultrasonographic findings of bilateral multicystic kidneys at 17 weeks of gestation. The patient chose termination of pregnancy. Chromosomal analysis showed a normal karyotype. Whole-exome sequencing using samples from both affected siblings and their parents identified compound heterozygous TMEM67 pathogenic variants in both fetuses, while each parent carried each one of those pathogenic variants. Although whole-exome sequencing is not routinely performed for fetal disease, it may help clarify the etiology and guide genetic counseling for future pregnancies.

en: A Case of Mosaic Trisomy 12 Diagnosed by Amniocentesis
ja: 羊水検査で診断されたモザイク12トリソミーの1例
abs: (Background) Mosaic trisomy 12 is a rare mosaic aneuploidies showing diverse phenotypes which range from normal patients to severe congenital anomalies. (Case) A 41-year-old woman underwent a quadruple test at 15 weeks because of advanced maternal age, the result was positive for trisomy 21. She was referred to our department of genetic counseling for prenatal diagnosis, and amniocentesis was performed to evaluate for trisomy21 at 17weeks. Chromosome analysis of cultured amniocytes revealed 47,XX,+12[5]/46,XX[10], leading to a diagnosis of mosaic trisomy 12. Although we explained that additional testing by FISH analysis and array CGH was also available, the patient declined these options. For mosaic trisomy 12, additional analysis may not be necessary because the severity of phenotype does not correlate with the mosaic ratio, we explained that careful fetal ultrasonographic follow-up would be important. After thorough genetic counseling, the patient decided to continue the pregnancy. Ultrasonography of the fetus had revealed no anomalies at 17weeks and 20weeks and is scheduled at 27weeks of gestation. Reported clinical features include developmental delay, dysmorphic face, skin pigmentation abnormalities, congenital heart disease, hypotonia because the severity does not correlate with the mosaic ratio, prediction of the postnatal phenotype is considered extremely difficult. This point should be carefully explained during genetic counseling.

en: Changes in Testing Performance and Maternal Characteristics According to Shifts in Indications for NIPT.
ja: NIPT適応の変化に伴う検査性能と母体特性の変化
abs: NIPT has rapidly expanded worldwide and has influenced prenatal screening practices in Japan. However, there is limited longitudinal evidence describing how user characteristics and decision-making patterns have changed over time. The Japanese Association of Medical Sciences (JAMS) revised its view on NIPT in February 2022, largely eliminating age restrictions. We conducted an 11-year retrospective analysis of 10,582 women who underwent NIPT at a university hospital between April 2013 and March 2024, comparing maternal demographics, test indications, results, and post-test outcomes before and after the expansion of the eligibility criteria. A shift toward younger maternal age was observed throughout the study period. After the expansion, both maternal and paternal ages were significantly younger, and the proportion of low-risk, whereas advanced maternal age) AMA) declined as an indication for testing. The distribution of outcomes after a positive NIPT result differed significantly between the two periods; specifically, the proportion of cases that did not undergo confirmatory invasive testing increased in the post-expansion group. Positive predictive values were 96.6% for trisomy 21, 92.6% for trisomy 18, and 47.1% for trisomy 13, and no false-negative trisomy cases were identified. These findings indicate that the expansion of the eligibility criteria broadened the user population and diversified motivations and decision-making processes. As NIPT continues to expand, individualized value-sensitive genetic counseling is essential to support informed choices.

en: Repeated Inconclusive Noninvasive Prenatal Testing (NIPT) Results Associated With Large Uterine Fibroids
ja: 巨大子宮筋腫に関連したNIPTの反復判定保留
abs: [Introduction] NIPT is a highly accurate prenatal screening test, although inconclusive results occasionally occur. Uterine fibroids are a known maternal factor associated with NIPT failure. We report a case of repeated inconclusive NIPT results associated with large uterine fibroids. [Case Report] A 43-year-old gravida 3, para 0 woman with uterine fibroids was referred to our department. Before pregnancy, she had two large fibroids measuring 12 cm and 8 cm. At 14 weeks and 3 days of gestation, she underwent NIPT. The result was inconclusive because a trimodal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) size distribution interfered with analysis. Repeat testing at 15 weeks and 3 days yielded the same result. After genetic counseling (GC) regarding the inconclusive findings and management options, the patient chose expectant management. She delivered by elective cesarean section at 38 weeks of gestation because of uterine fibroids, and the neonate showed no apparent abnormalities. [Discussion] Low fetal fraction is a well-recognized cause of inconclusive NIPT results. In contrast, repeated test failure in this case appeared to result from a trimodal cfDNA size distribution, which generated analytical noise and may also have affected fetal fraction estimation. The finding suggests a possible association between uterine fibroids and abnormal cfDNA size distribution. [Conclusion] Inconclusive NIPT results may cause substantial psychological burden. Awareness of this possibility in pregnancies complicated by uterine fibroids may facilitate appropriate GC and informed decision-making.

en: Retrospective study of NIPT with fetal fraction in twin pregnancies and vanishing twin cases at our institution
ja: 当院における双胎妊娠・バニシングツインのNIPTと胎児分画の後方視的検討
abs: As a core facility, our institution performs approximately 340 NIPT cases annually. We conducted a retrospective study of maternal background, chorionicity, NIPT results, and fetal fraction in women with twin pregnancies or vanishing twin pregnancies who underwent genetic counseling and NIPT at our institution between April 2020 and December 2025. A total of 1,928 cases underwent NIPT at our institution, of which 35 cases (1.8%) were included in this study. The mean maternal age was 37.2 years. The NIPT results were negative in 33 cases, positive in 1 case (trisomy 13 on NIPT, but normal karyotype on amniocentesis), and inconclusive in 1 case (fetal fraction <8% on NIPT, but normal karyotype on amniocentesis). The chorionicity distribution was as follows: 1 case of monochorionic monoamniotic twins (MM group), 8 cases of monochorionic diamniotic twins (MD group), and 12 cases of dichorionic diamniotic twins (DD group). In addition, there were 14 cases in the vanishing twin (VT group). The fetal fraction according to gestational age was as follows: 10 weeks, 15-19%; 11 weeks, 9-21%; 12 weeks, 7-21%; 13 weeks, 9-23%; 14 weeks, 9%; 15 weeks, 11%; 16 weeks, 12%; and 17 weeks, 13-16%. The fetal fraction by group was as follows: MD group, 7-19%; DD group, 9-23%; and VT group, 9-21%. These findings suggest that NIPT can be appropriately performed in twin pregnancies and vanishing twin cases when adequate genetic counseling is provided regarding the possibility of false-positive or inconclusive results and the difficulty of selective fetal reduction.

en: A case of atypical Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome associated with CREBBP mosaic deletion and EP300 variant.
ja: CREBBPモザイク欠失とEP300バリアントを伴う非定型Rubinstein-Taybi症候群の1例
abs: [Background] Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome (RTS) is a congenital disorder caused by pathogenic variants in CREBBP or EP300 and characterized by typical facial features, broad thumbs, and developmental delay. RTS shows a wide phenotypic spectrum, sometimes making diagnosis difficult. [Case] A Japanese female infant was born at 35 weeks of gestation with a birth weight of 1,421 g (small for gestational age) and admitted to our NICU. She showed feeding difficulties, laryngomalacia, and atrial septal defect. G-banded karyotyping revealed 45,X[7]/46,XX[23], leading to a diagnosis of mosaic Turner syndrome. However, she later developed severe developmental delay that could not be fully explained by mosaic Turner syndrome. Chromosomal microarray analysis identified a copy number variant in 16p13.3 (log2 ratio -0.254), suggesting mosaic deletion of CREBBP. Although some of her manifestations were compatible with RTS, she lacked the cardinal features of RTS, namely typical facial features and broad thumbs. Subsequent genetic testing revealed a pathogenic EP300 variant (c.5355A>G). Finally, she was diagnosed as having RTS with coexisting CREBBP mosaic deletion and EP300 variant. [Discussion] To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of RTS with coexisting CREBBP mosaic deletion and EP300 variant. Although each alterations has been reported to be associated with relatively mild phenotypes, their coexistence may have contributed to the severe phenotype. In addition, the absence of the cardinal features of RTS may provide novel insight into the genotype-phenotype correlation of RTS.

en: Clinical significance of whole-genome sequencing in fatal infant cases
ja: 乳児死亡例における全ゲノム解析の臨床的意義
abs: Background Investigating the causes of unexpected death is critically important for bereaved families. When hereditary disorders underlie infant mortality, genetic diagnosis can be important for parents and other family members. However, the genomic landscape of infant mortality remains unclear. We present four cases with fatal conditions analyzed by whole-genome sequencing (WGS) at our institution. Results Clinically relevant genomic findings were identified in all four cases, none of which had been suspected during the clinical course: trisomy 21, an interstitial deletion of chromosome 10p, a novel de novo KMT2A variant associated with Wiedemann-Steiner syndrome, and NC_012920.1(MT-RNR1):m.1555A>G. The results were returned to parents approximately one year after testing. Discussion WGS identified diverse findings encompassing chromosomal abnormalities, a nuclear single-nucleotide variant, and a mitochondrial variant, all of which had potentially actionable implications. The mitochondrial m.1555A>G variant, although not directly causative of death, was also identified in the mother, providing actionable information regarding aminoglycoside ototoxicity risk. Conclusion WGS can reveal unrecognized or novel genetic variants, improve understanding of underlying conditions, and thereby support genetic counseling, recurrence-risk assessment, and family-centered postmortem care. In neonatal and infant deaths, where the window for ante-mortem genetic testing is narrow, WGS offers valuable diagnostic and actionable information, even when a definitive cause of death cannot be established.

en: A case of 1q deletion and 5q duplication with refractory atopic dermatitis and eosinophilic gastroenteritis
ja: 難治性アトピー性皮膚炎と好酸球性胃腸炎を伴う1q欠失・5q重複の1例
abs: Background: Numerous genes involved in regulation of the immune response have been identified; however, there have been few reports of patients with chromosomal duplications presenting with immune dysregulation. We encountered a patient with 5q duplication who exhibited multiple allergic manifestations. Case: The patient was the first son of healthy parents and was born at 38 weeks of gestation with a birth weight of 2334 g. By 15 years of age, the following features had become evident: nasal stenosis, microcephaly, partial agenesis of the corpus callosum, severe short stature (-5 SD), and severe intellectual disability (DQ 26). G-banding performed at 2 months of age revealed 46,XY,add(1)(q44), but further characterization was not performed. Atopic dermatitis and food allergies had been present since infancy. At 13 years of age, he developed abdominal pain and vomiting and was diagnosed with eosinophilic gastroenteritis, which was difficult to control. Chromosomal microarray analysis performed at 15 years of age revealed a 0.58 Mb deletion on 1q and a 26.9 Mb duplication on 5q, leading to the final karyotype of 46,XY,der(1;5) (q44;q33.2). Discussion: The duplicated 5q region included NSD1 and LTC4S at 5q35.3, as well as the immune-related genes IL12B, HAVCR1/2, and ITK at 5q33.3. Activation of IL12B and LTC4S has been reported to be associated with inflammatory bowel disease and eosinophil recruitment, respectively. In this patient, duplication extending to 5q33 may have contributed to refractory immune dysregulation in addition to the phenotype of reversed Sotos syndrome.

en: Clinical features and disease course of a Japanese boy with GEMIN5-related neurodevelopmental disorder
ja: GEMIN5関連神経発達症の日本人男児の臨床像と経過
abs: GEMIN5-related neurodevelopmental disorder is a rare autosomal recessive condition characterized by hypotonia, motor developmental delay, and cerebellar atrophy. However, the clinical spectrum associated with missense variants remains incompletely understood. We report a 4-year-old Japanese boy with hypotonia and motor-predominant developmental delay. He achieved independent walking at 12 months but developed gait instability after 1 year of age. Brain MRI at 1 year 8 months demonstrated cerebellar atrophy or hypoplasia. Follow-up imaging showed mild progression at 2 years 8 months, followed by relative radiological stability at 3 years 8 months. Extensive metabolic and neuromuscular investigations were unremarkable. Trio-based exome sequencing identified compound heterozygous novel missense variants in GEMIN5 (NM_015465.5): c.519T>G (p.Asp173Glu) and c.212C>A (p.Thr71Lys), inherited from his father and mother, respectively. Both variants were absent from population databases, predicted to be deleterious by multiple in silico tools, and located within the WD40 repeat region, a functional domain involved in RNA recognition. These findings were considered consistent with GEMIN5-related disorder. The relatively mild clinical course with limited radiological progression suggests that certain missense variants may retain partial protein function. This case expands the clinical and genetic spectrum of GEMIN5-related disorder and highlights the importance of considering this condition in patients with cerebellar atrophy and progressive motor dysfunction.

en: Whole-genome sequencing analysis of complex structural variants in 9p deletion and duplication syndrome
ja: 9p欠失・重複症候群の複雑構造多型の全ゲノム解析
abs: In this study, we investigated complex structural variants (SVs) involving copy number alterations in the 9p region identified by short-read whole-genome sequencing (srWGS).srWGS was performed for a 2-year-old boy with midface hypoplasia, a thin upper lip, microcephaly, and autism spectrum disorder-like features including hand-flapping movements. Genomic DNA libraries were sequenced on the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform using 2 × 150 bp paired-end reads, and variants were analyzed using Illumina Emedgene. Analysis identified a ~12 Mb deletion and a ~2 Mb duplication in the 9p terminal, suggesting 9p deletion/duplication syndrome. However, Integrative Genomics Viewer (IGV) inspection revealed abnormal read coverage and paired-end orientations adjacent to these copy number variants (CNVs), indicating additional structural alterations. Complex read configurations suggestive of inversion and deletion events involving multiple breakpoints were observed near the duplicated region, consistent with complex genomic rearrangements including chromothripsis-like events. While most reported cases of 9p deletion/duplication syndrome have been characterized using cytogenetic or chromosomal microarray approaches, this case additionally harbored multiple smaller SVs ranging from several tens to hundreds of kilobases. These findings suggest that distal 9p rearrangements may be more structurally complex than previously recognized and highlight the utility of srWGS and read-level analysis. Further analysis is progressing.

en: A Case of a Novel TUBB3 Gene Variant Associated with Spastic Quadriplegia, EEG Abnormalities, and Cortical Dysplasia
ja: 痙性四肢麻痺・脳波異常・皮質形成異常を伴う新規TUBB3バリアントの1例
abs: The β-tubulin class III (TUBB3) gene is located on chromosome 16q24 and is one of the genes encoding tubulin, a protein that constitutes microtubules. It is associated with a very rare neurological disorder known to cause complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations 1 (CDCBM1,#614039) and congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles type 3 (CFEOM3,#600638) both of which follow an autosomal dominant inheritance pattern. Although we reported on this condition in 2016, the number of case reports on Malformations of Cortical Development (MCD) has not increased since then. We report here on a 4-year-old boy with spastic quadriplegia, a history of febrile seizures, and characteristic head imaging findings, in whom we detected a novel de novo TUBB3 variant.

en: Identification of a hemizygous IRS4 pathogenic variant in a Japanese patient with central congenital hypothyroidism
ja: 中枢性先天性甲状腺機能低下症の日本人患者におけるヘミ接合IRS4病的バリアントの同定
abs: Background: Central congenital hypothyroidism (CeH) is caused by hypothalamic or pituitary dysfunction. Pathogenic variants in IGSF1, TBL1X, IRS4, TSHB, and TRHR are rare causes of isolated CeH. Objective: To report the first Japanese case of IRS4-related CeH and characterize its clinical features. Case Report: A 10-year-3-month-old boy with normal TSH-based neonatal screening and normal development was referred for short stature. His height was 125.7 cm (-2.03 SD) with delayed bone age. Endocrinological evaluation showed low free T4 without TSH elevation and a blunted TSH response to thyrotropin-releasing hormone stimulation. Other pituitary hormone tests and brain MRI were normal. He was diagnosed with isolated CeH and treated with levothyroxine. Although growth velocity did not markedly improve, gradual catch-up growth occurred with delayed puberty, reaching 164.5 cm (-0.71 SD) at 15 years. Genetic Analysis: Trio whole-exome sequencing identified a known hemizygous nonsense variant in IRS4 (c.643G>C, p.Gly215*). His asymptomatic mother was a heterozygous carrier. Discussion: Previously reported cases suggest that IRS4-related CeH is characterized by isolated TSH deficiency, failure of detection by TSH-based neonatal screening, diagnosis later in childhood during evaluation for short stature or incidentally, and normal neurodevelopment without severe hypothyroid manifestations. Conclusion: IRS4-related CeH is a mild and potentially underdiagnosed disorder that may be overlooked among patients with idiopathic short stature.

en: A mild form of RORA-related neurodevelopmental disorder in a Japanese patient with hypotonia and cerebellar ataxia
ja: 筋緊張低下と小脳失調を呈した日本人患者のRORA関連神経発達症の軽症型
abs: Introduction: RORA encodes a nuclear receptor involved in cerebellar neurodevelopment. Heterozygous pathogenic RORA variants cause neurodevelopmental disorders with developmental delay, cerebellar ataxia, and epilepsy, however, genotype phenotype correlations remain incompletely understood. Case Report: A 2-year-old girl was referred for developmental delay, hypotonia, and truncal ataxia. She walked independently at 1 year and 8 months. Brain MRI showed no cerebellar abnormalities. Nerve conduction studies and muscle biopsy showed no significant abnormalities. Language development improved, and at 3 years she showed relatively preserved cognitive function despite persistent motor impairment (DQ 91). Genetic Analysis: Trio whole-exome sequencing identified a novel heterozygous de novo RORA variant (c.1519T>A, p.Tyr507Asn) in the ligand-binding domain of RORα. According to ACMG/AMP guidelines, the variant was classified as likely pathogenic (PS2, PM2, PP3). Discussion: Previous studies suggest that missense variants affecting the DNA-binding domain are associated with severe cerebellar phenotypes, whereas ligand-binding domain variants may be associated with milder phenotypes. The mild phenotype, including preserved cognitive function and absence of epilepsy or cerebellar atrophy, is consistent with this proposed genotype phenotype correlation. Conclusion: Our case expands the clinical and molecular spectrum of RORA-related disorders and supports genotype phenotype correlations. RORA-related disorders should be considered in developmental delay with hypotonia and ataxia.

en: Unexpected Death with Autopsy Findings of Right Heart Failure in PCGF2-Related Disorder: Expanding Phenotypic Spectrum
ja: PCGF2関連疾患における右心不全の剖検所見を伴う予期せぬ死亡：表現型スペクトラムの拡大
abs: PCGF2 is a component of Polycomb repressive complex 1 and regulates gene expression during development. PCGF2-related syndrome has recently been associated with growth impairment, congenital anomalies, neurodevelopmental disorders, and cardiac defects. We report an infant with a broader phenotype who died of right heart failure. The patient was born at 31 weeks of gestation with a birth weight of 1,073 g and was small for gestational age. Prenatal findings included intraventricular hemorrhage, ventriculomegaly, and absence of the septum pellucidum. After birth, patent ductus arteriosus was surgically ligated, while atrial septal defect was managed medically. Additional findings included distinctive facial features, congenital glaucoma, and congenital hypothyroidism. The glaucoma improved spontaneously. The patient was discharged at a corrected age of 3 months, but poor feeding and poor weight gain persisted. Genetic testing identified a de novo heterozygous PCGF2 variant causing substitution of proline 65 with leucine. At 8 months of age, the patient was found unresponsive in the prone position and died. Autopsy indicated right heart failure rather than asphyxia as the cause of death. The patient presented with small for gestational age, congenital heart disease, facial dysmorphism, central nervous system anomalies, ophthalmologic abnormalities, and endocrine abnormalities, suggesting expansion of the PCGF2-related phenotypic spectrum. The fatal course highlights the importance of multidisciplinary management, particularly for cardiac complications.

en: A case of Activated PI3Kδ Syndrome Type 1 with Thyroid Autoimmunity and Renal Involvement
ja: 甲状腺自己免疫と腎病変を伴う活性化PI3Kδ症候群1型の1例
abs: Background: Activated PI3K-delta; syndrome (APDS) is a primary immunodeficiency caused by gain-of-function variants in PIK3CD, leading to dysregulated PI3K signaling and a broad spectrum of clinical manifestations. Early diagnosis remains challenging because symptoms overlap with common pediatric respiratory diseases. Case presentation: We report a 14-year-old boy with a long history of recurrent lower respiratory tract infections, chronic productive cough, and persistent rhinorrhea. Since infancy, he experienced repeated episodes of pneumonia and wheezing, requiring 19 hospitalizations by age 9. He also had recurrent otitis media with effusion requiring multiple tympanostomies, mild hepatosplenomegaly, and bronchiectasis. Laboratory findings over the past decade revealed intermittent lymphopenia, mild thrombocytopenia, minimally reduced IgA, elevated β2-microglobulin, and persistently high anti-TPO and anti-thyroglobulin antibodies with normal thyroid hormone levels. Whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous gain-of-function variant in PIK3CD, c.3061G>A (p.Glu1021Lys), confirming the diagnosis of APDS. Conclusion: This case highlights the diagnostic difficulty of APDS, which may present with chronic airway disease, recurrent otitis media, subtle immunologic abnormalities, and thyroid autoimmunity. Careful longitudinal assessment, detailed history-taking, and comprehensive immunologic and genetic evaluation are essential for early recognition of APDS, particularly in children with refractory or atypical respiratory disease.

en: Valvular Heart Disease in Geleophysic Dysplasia: Surgical and Perioperative Challenges in Three Pediatric Cases
ja: Geleophysic dysplasiaの弁膜症：小児3例の外科・周術期の課題
abs: Geleophysic dysplasia (GD), associated with mutations in ADAMTSL2, FBN1, and LTBP3, is a progressive disorder characterized by short stature, thickened skin, and cardiac involvement. We present three pediatric GD patients with valvular heart disease. Two developed severe mitral stenosis (MS) requiring mechanical mitral valve replacement (MVR), while one has been followed for mild supraaortic and pulmonary valve stenosis without surgery. A de novo FBN1 variant in one case and compound heterozygous ADAMTSL2 variants were identified in others. In the first surgical case, cardiac issues progressed after 3 years of age. MVR was performed at school age, and difficult airway was noted. Both mitral leaflets were thickened, the commissure was fused with subvalvular tissue. The second patient developed severe MS during infancy. Because of the tiny annulus, implantation of the smallest available mechanical valve(16mm) caused coronary artery compression. The patient also had tricuspid valve dysplasia requiring repeated surgery. Despite preserved prosthetic valve function, respiratory failure and pulmonary hypertension persist with tracheostomy and respiratory support. The third case was initially suspected of Williams syndrome and later diagnosed with ADMTSL2-related GD. Cardiac involvement remained mild despite similar extracardiac manifestations. In both surgical cases, small annuli, rigid valvular tissue, restrictive thoracic anatomy and difficult airway complicated management. These cases highlight the need for individualized care in GD-associated valvular disease.

en: Compound heterozygous B3GALT6 variants in an infant with severe short stature and achondroplasia- like features
ja: 重度低身長と軟骨無形成症様所見を呈した乳児のB3GALT6複合ヘテロ接合バリアント
abs: A 6-month-old boy was referred for severe short stature with an achondroplasia-like phenotype. Femoral shortening had been noted prenatally, and he was born at 39 weeks with a length of 43.5 cm (-2.6 SD) and weight of 2604 g. At presentation, his height was 56.9 cm (-4.63 SD). He had mild frontal bossing and depressed nasal bridge, without skin hyperextensibility, dislocation, or fracture. Skeletal radiographs showed metaphyseal widening of long bones, hypoplastic ilia, narrowed sciatic notches, ovoid vertebral bodies, and anterior vertebral beaking. FGFR3 genetic testing showed no pathogenic variant. B3GALT6 analysis identified compound heterozygous variants: maternally inherited c.1A>G and paternally inherited c.694C>T (p.Arg232Cys), both known pathogenic variants. He was diagnosed with B3GALT6-related skeletal dysplasia, corresponding to spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia with joint laxity (Beighton type) or Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, spondylodysplastic type 2. This rare disorder has been reported in only approximately 70 cases worldwide. Midface hypoplasia, frontal bossing, short stature, and metaphyseal changes may overlap with achondroplasia, whereas ovoid vertebrae, anterior vertebral beaking, and iliac hypoplasia can suggest B3GALT6-related disorder. Early diagnosis is important for skeletal and cardiovascular follow-up. In conclusion, in infants with an achondroplasia-like phenotype and negative FGFR3 testing, reassessment of radiographs can prompt genetic testing and diagnosis of B3GALT6-related disorder, enabling follow-up and genetic counseling.

en: Interpretation of 3q29 Copy Number Loss: A Diagnostic Pitfall in Chromosomal Microarray Analysis
ja: 3q29コピー数減少の解釈：染色体マイクロアレイ解析の診断上の落とし穴
abs: Background: Chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA) is a first-tiet test for children with developmental delay and congenital anomalies because of its high sensitivity for detecting copy number variants (CNVs). However, technical artifacts may lead to false-positive findings. We encountered four pediatric cases in which CMA suggested 3q29 copy number loss, but subsequent investigations did not support a pathogenic deletion. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed four unrelated pediatric patients with developmental delay, congenital anomalies, or growth failure. CMA findings, clinical phenotypes, genomic mapping, and confirmatory test results were analyzed. Results: All four cases showed apparent copy number loss overlapping the canonical 3q29 microdeletion critical region, with estimated sizes of 1.3-2.8 Mb. Clinical phenotypes were heterogeneous and not strongly consistent with 3q29 microdeletion syndrome. Detailed review showed that neither comparative genomic hybridization nor SNP probe patterns clearly supported heterozygous deletion. Subtelomeric fluorescence in situ hybridization performed in three cases failed to confirm the suspected deletion. The 3q29 region contains abundant segmental duplications, which may predispose to probe cross-hybridization and false-positive CNV calls. Conclusion: Apparent CNVs should not be considered diagnostic solely based on automated CMA output or overlap with known pathogenic regions. Careful review of raw array data, genotype-phenotype correlation, and confirmatory testing are essential, especially in regions such as 3q29.

en: Retrospective Study of Foramen Magnum Development in Patients With Achondroplasia Starting Vosoritide Before Age Three
ja: 3歳未満でボソリチドを開始した軟骨無形成症患者の大後頭孔発達の後方視的検討
abs: Purpose: Achondroplasia (ACH) is a monogenic skeletal dysplasia caused by gain-of-function variants in FGFR3, leading to impaired endochondral ossification that results in growth disturbance and foramen magnum stenosis. Foramen magnum stenosis is one of the most serious complications in infancy and may cause brainstem compression or sudden death. Although vosoritide promotes endochondral ossification and improves linear growth, its effects on foramen magnum development remain unclear. We evaluated the impact of early vosoritide administration on foramen magnum development in infants and young children with ACH using longitudinal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Methods: This retrospective single-center case series included nine patients who initiated vosoritide before age 3. Serial head MRI scans were analyzed. Anteroposterior and transverse diameters of the foramen magnum were measured and compared with reference curves from untreated ACH cohorts. Results: Vosoritide was initiated at a median age of 4 months, with a mean treatment duration of 2.5 years. Compared with untreated cohorts, steeper growth rates were observed in eight of nine patients for the anteroposterior and in all for the transverse diameter. Except for one patient, all patients remained at Achondroplasia Foramen Magnum Score 1 or 2 during follow-up. Conclusion: Early initiation of vosoritide may promote foramen magnum enlargement in infants and young children with achondroplasia.

en: BRCA deleterious alterations in advanced prostate cancer: insights from the nationwide cancer genomic database
ja: 進行前立腺がんにおけるBRCA有害変化：全国がんゲノムデータベースからの知見
abs: Background The clinicopathological distribution of BRCA1 and BRCA2 (BRCA) deleterious alterations in advanced prostate cancer patients undergoing tumor-only panel testing remains insufficiently understood. Materials & Methods We analyzed 2,815 patients who underwent comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) testing using a tumor-only panel for advanced prostate cancer between December 2020 and November 2024. Data were obtained from the Center for Cancer Genomics and Advanced Therapeutics, a nationwide database for CGP test. Results The median age at CGP testing was 72 years (range, 23-93). Deleterious gene alterations in BRCA1 and BRCA2 were identified in 33 (1.2%) and 398 patients (14.1%), respectively, with an overlap of three patients (0.1%). The frequency of BRCA deleterious alteration decreased with aging, being 24.2% in <50 years, 25.4% in 50-59 years, 16.3% in 60-69 years, 14.3% in 70-79 years, and 9.3% in >=80 years. A family history of breast and ovarian cancers were independently predicted to detect BRCA deleterious alterations (odds ratio 1.901 and 3.016, both P<.001). Stratification of the interval from initial diagnosis to CGP testing into one-year increments showed a consistent BRCA deleterious alteration rate of approximately 10-20%, including 17.3% (97/560) in the first year and 18.0% (7/39) in the tenth year. Conclusions Among patients with advanced prostate cancer, BRCA deleterious alterations were detected more frequently in patients younger than 60 years and in those with a family history of breast or ovarian cancer, even when using a tumor-only panel.

en: Expanded HBOC coverage, but disrupted cascade testing: multi-layered barriers revealed by CGP.
ja: HBOC保険適用拡大とカスケード検査の断絶：CGPが明らかにした多層的障壁
abs: Hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (HBOC) is increasingly identified through comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) across diverse malignancies. In Japan, insurance coverage for cascade testing and preventive interventions has recently been expanded to first-degree relatives. However, whether expanded access alone ensures clinical uptake remains unclear. We retrospectively reviewed CGP tests performed at our institution between January and December 2025 (n = 212) and identified 10 patients (4.7%) with suspected HBOC as secondary findings, including breast (n = 5), prostate (n = 1), neuroendocrine (n = 1), biliary (n = 1), histiocytic sarcoma (n = 1), and cervical cancer (n = 1). Genetic findings were disclosed to all patients. Of the seven female patients, three had already been diagnosed with HBOC. Among the remaining four, three underwent confirmatory germline testing (3/4). Among the three male patients with solid tumors, none proceeded to confirmatory testing (0/3) despite appropriate genetic counseling: two declined and one cancelled. In addition, one BRCA pathogenic variant identified in a hematologic malignancy was disclosed within hematology, and referral to genetic counseling was not achieved. These findings highlight multi-layered barriers to cascade testing, including behavioral, structural, contextual, and regulatory factors. Expanded access alone may not ensure uptake, and coordinated strategies are required to translate genetic findings into clinical action.

en: Distribution of BRCA1/2 Pathogenic Variants Identified by BRACAnalysis at a Single Japanese Center
ja: 国内単一施設でBRACAnalysisにより同定されたBRCA1/2病的バリアントの分布
abs: Background: Germline pathogenic variants in BRCA1 and BRCA2 are key drivers of hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome (HBOC). Large-scale studies in Japanese populations have shown that these variants are predominantly truncating and widely distributed, with several recurrent variants. However, real-world single-center data remain limited. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed patients who underwent BRACAnalysis at Teikyo University Hospital between July 2019 and March 2026. Clinical data including age, sex, and cancer type were collected. Pathogenic variants were evaluated and visualized using lollipop plots. Variant classification was based on clinical interpretation. Results: A total of 42 patients were included (mean age 51.4 years; 41 females, 1 male). Breast cancer was the most common (n=28), followed by ovarian cancer (n=7) and bilateral breast cancer (n=5). Most variants were truncating mutations. In BRCA1, recurrent variants included p.Leu63* and p.Gln934*. In BRCA2, p.Ile1859Lysfs*3, p.Arg2318*, and p.Ile2675Val were identified. Variants were widely distributed, although a limited number accounted for multiple cases. These recurrent variants may reflect population-specific founder effects in the Japanese population. The distribution pattern was consistent with previous large-scale genomic studies. Conclusions:BRCA1/2 variants were predominantly truncating and broadly distributed, with recurrent variants contributing disproportionately. As a single-center study, regional or referral bias cannot be excluded.

en: BRCA1/2 Pathogenic Variant Characteristics in HBOC Care at Our Hospital and Their Implications for Nursing Care
ja: 当院HBOC診療におけるBRCA1/2病的バリアントの特徴と看護への示唆
abs: Our hospital established a Department of Clinical Genetics in 2022, primarily providing care for clients related to hereditary tumors. Most clients are those with BRCA1 or BRCA2 variants , and their understanding of and emotional reactions to genetic test results including pathogenic variants, variants of uncertain significance or even no variants, as well as their levels of anxiety, vary widely. At the same time, there are situations in which clients confront complicated feelings such as how to tell the results and related matters, which is a characteristic of hereditary tumors to their relatives. In the Department of Clinical Genetics, we often face challenges in providing not only genetic counseling but also nursing support to clients and their relatives from diverse backgrounds. This study reviewed genetic counseling record and medical records of clients who underwent germline testing of BRCA1 and BRCA2 at our hospital from 2018 to 2025. The aim was to review the characteristics of pathogenic variants in BRCA1 or BRCA2 and to investigate the significant relationships of those variants with the level of anxiety experienced by clients . This study might provide us with insights for the future direction of nursing support for HBOC clients in the Department of Clinical Genetics.

en: Secondary Findings Identified Through Comprehensive Genomic Profiling: A Single-Institution Analysis of 100 Cases
ja: 包括的がんゲノムプロファイリングで同定された二次的所見：単一施設100例の解析
abs: Background: Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) is primarily performed to identify therapeutic targets; however, it can also reveal clinically significant secondary findings (SFs) suggestive of germline variants. In Hokkaido, where medical resources are geographically dispersed, regional core hospitals play an important role in genomic medicine through collaboration with tertiary care centers. Objective: To investigate the frequency, genetic spectrum, and clinical management of SFs identified through CGP at a regional core hospital. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 100 patients who underwent CGP at our institution between April 2024 and March 2026. We evaluated the frequency and spectrum of SFs, variant allele frequency (VAF), and subsequent genetic counseling. Results: Primary tumor sites included lung (30 cases), breast (19), uterus/ovary (14), gastrointestinal tract (12), hepatobiliary tract/pancreas (11), prostate (2), and others (12). The CGP platforms used were FoundationOne (F1) in 46 cases, F1 Liquid in 41 cases, GenMineTOP in 7 cases, and Guardant360 in 6 cases. SFs were identified in 11 patients (11%), with BRCA gene alterations being the most frequent. The VAF ranged from 29% to 93%, suggesting germline origin. Among the 8 patients newly suspected of having hereditary cancer, genetic counseling was provided to 4 patients. Discussion: The frequency of SFs was consistent with previous reports. CGP serves not only as a tool for therapeutic decision-making but also as an entry point into genomic medicine and hereditary cancer care in regional healthcare settings.

en: Universal tumor screening for Lynch syndrome and real-world MGPT candidates in colorectal cancer
ja: 大腸がんにおけるLynch症候群ユニバーサル腫瘍スクリーニングと実臨床のMGPT候補
abs: Background: Universal tumor screening (UTS) for Lynch syndrome (LS) is recommended for colorectal cancer (CRC), while multigene panel testing (MGPT) is increasingly considered. However, real-world data on MGPT candidates remain limited. We evaluated UTS outcomes and explored MGPT candidates in CRC. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 1,008 CRC surgical cases undergoing UTS between May 2022 and March 2026. UTS outcomes, recommendations for genetic counseling (GC), and LS diagnoses were assessed. MGPT candidates were evaluated based on age at CRC surgery, prior malignancy, and synchronous multiple CRC. Results: Among 1,008 CRC cases (median age 74 years), MSI-H/dMMR was identified in 104 (10.3%), and GC was recommended in 47 (4.7%). Germline testing confirmed LS in 11 patients (1.1%); 7 relatives were additionally diagnosed. CRC surgery before age 50 occurred in 50 patients (5.0%). Seventeen patients developed malignancy or metachronous CRC before age 50 despite CRC surgery after age 50, resulting in 67 patients (6.6%) with malignancy onset before age 50. In contrast, 260 patients (25.8%) had CRC surgery before age 50, prior malignancy, or synchronous multiple CRC. Among the remaining 748 patients (74.2%) without these features, 32 (4.3%) were still recommended for GC through UTS. Conclusions: UTS was feasible and enabled cascade LS identification. Because LS was not limited to early-onset cases, UTS should remain the basis of LS detection. MGPT may be added to UTS, beginning with early-onset CRC and exploratory inclusion of patients with malignancy onset before age 50.

en: Real-World Barriers to Confirmatory and Cascade Testing Following Germline Findings from Comprehensive Genomic Profiling
ja: CGPの生殖細胞系列所見後の確認検査・カスケード検査における実臨床の障壁
abs: Background: Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) occasionally identifies germline pathogenic variants (GPVs) or presumed germline pathogenic variants (PGPVs). We investigated clinical outcomes after disclosure of germline findings identified through CGP at our institution. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 441 patients who underwent CGP between April 2025 and March 2026. Frequencies of GPVs/PGPVs, genetic counseling, confirmatory germline testing, and cascade testing in relatives were evaluated. Results: Disclosure-eligible GPVs/PGPVs were identified in 34 patients (7.7%), including 28 PGPVs and 6 GPVs. All patients requesting disclosure received genetic counseling. Confirmatory germline testing was performed in 8 of 28 patients (28.6%) with PGPVs. Cascade testing in relatives was performed in only one family. This case involved a 76-year-old woman with cholangiocarcinoma carrying a PALB2 GPV. Her two daughters underwent testing, and one carried the familial variant. Surveillance based on NCCN guidelines was introduced. Discussion: Despite universal genetic counseling among disclosure-requesting patients, confirmatory- and cascade testing rates remained low. Possible contributing factors included advanced cancer status, absence of informative relatives, low likelihood of germline origin in some PGPVs, and financial burden. These findings highlight substantial real-world barriers in translating CGP-derived germline findings into familial risk assessment and preventive care. Improved systems for family communication, surveillance, and long-term follow-up are needed.

en: Current Practice of Reproductive and Preventive Care Support for BRCA1 and BRCA2 Variant Carriers
ja: BRCA1/2バリアント保持者への生殖・予防ケア支援の現状
abs: Background BRCA1 and BRCA2 pathogenic variant carriers require support for cancer risk management fertility preservation family planning and timing of risk reducing salpingo oophorectomy. We evaluated reproductive care and counseling issues. Methods We reviewed patients under forty nine years tested for hereditary breast and ovarian cancer between 2016 and 2025 who carried pathogenic BRCA1 and BRCA2 variants. Clinical data included cancer history marital status childbearing desire fertility referral pregnancy outcome and risk reducing salpingo oophorectomy. Results Forty two patients were included with fifteen BRCA1 and twenty seven BRCA2 variants. Median age was thirty nine years. Eleven were unaffected, twenty nine had breast cancer, and two had ovarian cancer. Eight breast cancer patients with childbearing desire visited oncofertility services. Three underwent embryo cryopreservation and one achieved pregnancy. Risk reducing salpingo oophorectomy was performed in eighteen patients. Median age was forty two years and sixteen had prior childbirth. Ten were unmarried and had no childbirth history including seven unaffected carriers and three with breast cancer. Median age was twenty nine years. Only one accessed oncofertility services and none received fertility preservation. Conclusions Reproductive and cancer risk decisions were linked in BRCA carriers. Young unmarried carriers rarely accessed reproductive support. Continuous life stage based genetic counseling is needed.

en: One Case with Two Pathogenic Variants in the BRCA2 Gene
ja: BRCA2遺伝子に2つの病的バリアントを有した1例
abs: Background: BRCA1/2 genetic testing is widely used for the diagnosis of hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (HBOC) and as a companion diagnostic for PARP inhibitors. As testing becomes more common, cases with two BRCA2 pathogenic variants are occasionally identified. Because BRCA2 is also a causative gene for autosomal recessive Fanconi anemia, careful interpretation is required. When two variants are detected, they may be located in cis (on the same allele) or in trans (on different alleles); the latter configuration is associated with Fanconi anemia. Case: A 69-year-old nulliparous woman developed bilateral synchronous breast cancer at age 50 and underwent breast-conserving surgery. At age 68, she developed right breast cancer again and underwent germline testing using BRACAnalysis. Two BRCA2 frameshift variants were identified: c.1278del (p.Asp427Thrfs*3) and c.1888dup (p.Thr630Asnfs*6), leading to a diagnosis of HBOC. Based on detailed evaluation of her family history and clinical findings, these variants were determined to be in cis. She was therefore managed as a typical HBOC patient with a single pathogenic variant and received counseling regarding risk-reducing surgery and appropriate surveillance. Discussion: With the increasing use of BRCA1/2 testing, rare variant patterns and unexpected findings related to Fanconi anemia may be encountered. Accurate interpretation requires careful assessment of clinical features and family history, as well as consideration of additional genetic analyses when necessary.

en: Genetic counseling following identification of EGFR T790M by comprehensive genomic profiling in lung cancer
ja: 肺がんのCGPでEGFR T790Mが同定された後の遺伝カウンセリング
abs: Background: EGFR T790M is recognized as a resistance mutation associated with epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors in lung cancer. In contrast, germline EGFR T790M mutations(gEGFRm) associated with hereditary lung cancer have rarely been reported. We report a case of suspected gEGFRm identified through comprehensive genetic profiling (CGP). Case presentation: A woman in her 70s was diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma. Following treatment with Osimertinib, an EGFR T790M mutation was identified through CGP. She was a non-smoker and had no family history of lung cancer. Although the mutation was considered most likely associated with acquired resistance, gEGFRm could not be completely excluded. The patient was referred for genetic counseling, and the possible hereditary implications were discussed. After genetic counseling, she decided to take confirmatory germline testing. Discussion: EGFR T790M is most commonly detected as an acquired resistance mutation after TKI therapy; however, rare germline cases have also been described. Previous reports suggest incomplete penetrance and variable clinical presentation. Recent advances in CGP have increased opportunities to identify variants suggestive of germline alterations during routine genomic testing. Appropriate interpretation of such findings is important because misclassification of somatic and germline variants may affect both patient management and familial risk assessment. This case highlights the importance of collaboration between oncology and clinical genetics in the era of precision medicine.

en: A case of juvenile gastric polyposis with germline SMAD4 mutation
ja: 生殖細胞系列SMAD4変異を有する若年性胃ポリポーシスの1例
abs: SMAD4 is a transcription regulator gene in TGF-β signaling pathway and acts as a tumor suppressor. Germline mutation of SMAD4 causes hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) and juvenile polyposis in autosomal dominant inheritance. A 35-year-old female complained anemic symptom and visited nearby hospital. Blood test showed Hb=4.5 and fecal occult blood test was positive and therefore transferred to our university hospital. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy revealed gastric multiple polyposis without teleangiectasia. CT scan exhibited no systemic vascular malformation and HHT was excluded. Because her mother, grandmother and aunt had gastric polyposis and gastric cancer she was suspected of juvenile gastric polyposis (JGP). After genetic counseling, peripheral blood test suspected that she had large heterozygous deletion from intron 7 to exon 10 (c.904+309_1227) of SMAD4 by short-read next-generation sequencing but not definitive diagnosis. She undergoes esophagogastroduodenoscopy and total colonoscopy every 12 months and whenever large polyps are found, we have removed them endoscopically. Almost all of them had been benign lesions but only one polyp contained well differentiated adenocarcinoma with curative resection. JGP case with SMAD4 mutation tends to have more aggressive gastric lesions and often needs total gastrectomy due to advanced cancer, extensive hemorrhage and hypoproteinemia. Our case has succeeded in escaping from surgical treatment by frequent endoscopic therapy based on patient's wishes.

en: A Case of Peritoneal Cancer in which Comprehensive Cancer Genome Profiling Testing Was Useful for Diagnosis
ja: 包括的がんゲノムプロファイリング検査が診断に有用であった腹膜がんの1例
abs: [Background] Primary peritoneal cancer (PPC) often shows no apparent uterine or adnexal mass on imaging and is therefore frequently classified as cancer of unknown primary ,which complicates treatment selection. We report a case in which comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) enabled a diagnosis of primary peritoneal cancer. [CASE] A 73 year old woman with a history of breast cancer surgery at age 50 presented lower abdominal pain. Computed tomography showed a 10cm pelvic mass, liver tumors, peritoneal dissemination and she was referred with suspected ovarian cancer. She underwent hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and sigmoid colostomy. Histopathology revealed no adnexal abnormalities, and lesions of the small intestine, uterine serosa, rectum were interpreted as metastases of an epithelial malignancy. Then she was diagnosed as cancer of unknown primary and received nivolumab therapy, but it showed no efficacy. CGP detected a pathogenic BRCA1 variant, and an expert panel concluded PPC. She received chemotherapy and maintenance poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor (PARPi) therapy , resulting in shrinkage of liver and peritoneal lesions 4 years postoperatively. Additionally she performed germline BRCA1/2 testing and confirmed hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome(HBOC). Also her daughter was diagnosed HBOC. [CONCLUTION] We were able to establish a definitive diagnosis and determine an appropriate treatment strategy through CGP. And this also enabled implementation of HBOC surveillance for the patient and appropriate management of at risk relatives.

en: A case of Lynch syndrome with advanced adrenal sarcoma
ja: 進行副腎肉腫を合併したLynch症候群の1例
abs: Background: Adrenal sarcomas are rare tumors. The precise incidence is unknown, and no standardized treatment protocol has been established. Although there are some reports of adrenocortical carcinomas associated with Lynch syndrome, this is the first report of adrenal sarcoma associated with Lynch syndrome. Case report: A Japanese man in his 30s underwent adrenalectomy for left adrenal tumor. After surgery, peritoneal dissemination showed rapid increase and he was treated with doxorubicin under the diagnosis of unclassifiable adrenal sarcoma. The pathological findings showed the possibility of undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma or pleomorphic liposarcoma. The cancer genomic profiling test was performed. The analysis revealed MSI-high and tumor mutation burden was 21Muts/Mb. As the secondary findings, MLH1 E13 pathogenic variant (Variant Allele Frequency(VAF) 65.6%) and TP53 R273H(VAF 23.2%) was detected. Based on this result, we switched to pembrolizumab monotherapy and the tumor dramatically reduced. After genetic counseling for hereditary tumors, multi-gene panel testing was performed, and the test revealed MLH1 c.37G>T leading to the diagnosis of Lynch syndrome. Conclusion: We report a case of Lynch syndrome with advanced adrenal sarcoma which showed remarkable sensitivity for immune checkpoint inhibitor. This case suggests the association between adrenal sarcomas and Lynch syndrome, and the utility of cancer genomic profiling tests for rare tumors from the perspective of therapeutic benefits and the patient's future health management.

en: Spatial transcriptomics reveals the molecular pathological features of ERBB2-amplified colorectal cancer
ja: 空間トランスクリプトミクスが明らかにするERBB2増幅大腸がんの分子病理学的特徴
abs: Recent advances in high-resolution, probe-based whole-transcriptome technologies for formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissues have enabled detailed molecular analyses of archival specimens. ERBB2 amplification, resulting in HER2 overexpression, is identified in approximately 2% - 5% of metastatic colorectal cancers (CRC). Although ERBB2-amplified CRC represents a relatively small molecular subtype, its clinical significance has increased with the development of HER2-targeted therapies. However, the spatial architecture and transcriptional heterogeneity of ERBB2-amplified CRC remain poorly understood. We aimed to characterize the spatial distribution and molecular features of tumor cell populations in ERBB2-amplified CRC using spatial transcriptomics. Spatial transcriptomic analysis was performed on an ERBB2-amplified CRC specimen to evaluate intratumoral cellular organization and transcriptional heterogeneity. Three distinct tumor cell clusters were identified: T1, a differentiated cell cluster; T2, an invasive-state cell cluster; and T3, a proliferative cell cluster. Tumor cells in T2 were spatially localized between T1 and T3, suggesting a transitional state associated with tumor invasion and differentiation. These spatially distinct clusters demonstrated differential gene expression profiles, including variable ERBB2 expression levels. Our findings provide novel insights into the spatial heterogeneity and molecular pathology of ERBB2-amplified CRC and may contribute to the development of more precise therapeutic strategies.

en: A review of the cases detected germline pathogenic variants through cancer genome panel testing in our institute.
ja: 当院のがんゲノムパネル検査で生殖細胞系列病的バリアントが検出された症例の検討
abs: Background Cancer genome panel testing (CGP) is submitted with a view to detect the druggable variants. The germline pathogenic variant (GPV) or presumed GPV (PGPV) leads to necessity of appropriate genetic counseling for at risk relatives. Case and Methods We detected the cases submitted CGP with solid tumor from May 2020 to April 2026 in our institute. The GPV / PGPV available for disclose through expert panel (EP) were extracted. Result The 218 cases were detected. The 75 cases of T-only panel and 112 cases of Liquid Bx, 35 cases of matched pair panel were included. The 7 cases with GPV / PGPV includes the 2 cases of TP53, a case of ATM, BARD1, MEN1, RAD51C. A case of undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma, gastric, pancreas, rectum, and ampullary cancer consisted the primary disease. The relatives of the 4 clients were disclosed the germline findings and received genetic counseling. No relatives requested the confirmatory testing and surveillance. Discussion The BRCA1/2 variants were acknowledged with highest frequency with malignant disease in Japan and 80% of them were GPV3. In this report, various genetic findings other than BRCA1/2 were detected. The germline conversion rate (GCR) of detected variants were reported about 10% with T-only panel in Japan. The variants of RAD51C and BARD1 with high GCR were detected in our report, appropriate confirmatory genetic testing should be considered. Conclusion The PGV / PGPV detected as secondary findings through CGP were disclosed appropriately for the clients and their relatives.

en: Experience of Multigene Panel Testing for At-Risk Relatives from Lynch Syndrome Families; its benefits and issues
ja: Lynch症候群家系のリスク保有血縁者への多遺伝子パネル検査の経験：利点と課題
abs: Introduction Recent advances in genomic medicine for hereditary cancer have been remarkable. In hereditary breast and ovarian cancer care, insurance coverage for BRCA1/BRCA2 genetic testing (GT) has expanded from probands to first-degree relatives. In contrast, for many other hereditary cancer syndromes, including Lynch syndrome, GT is not covered by insurance in Japan, and multigene panel testing (MGPT) is useful. Case A 55-year-old woman with no history of malignancy visited for genetic counseling after her paternal cousin was diagnosed with Lynch syndrome. She requested GT for health management. Because her cousin's results could not be confirmed, MGPT was performed. No pathogenic variants were detected. Family history Paternal cousin: 65y. Small bowel cancer in her 40s, renal cancer at 50y, and colorectal cancer at 62y; diagnosed with Lynch syndrome by genetic testing. Father: d.68y. Rectal cancer at 30y; gastric cancer at 56y. Brother: d.55y. Colorectal cancer at 45y; gastric cancer at 55y. Paternal uncle: d.29y. Colorectal cancer. Discussion When a pathogenic variant is identified in a proband, single-site analysis is often used for familial testing. However, even when no variant is detected, other hereditary cancer syndromes cannot be excluded. In this case, comprehensive evaluation using MGPT contributed to the patient's health management and reduced anxiety. Conclusion While MGPT may therefore be beneficial for individuals seeking information for health management, many problems still present, such as the fact that it is not covered by insurance.

en: Validating Germline Structural Variants from Short-Read WGS Using Nanopore Target Adaptive Sampling Long-Read Sequencing
ja: ナノポア・ターゲットアダプティブサンプリングによるショートリードWGS由来生殖細胞系列構造多型の検証
abs: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) is expected to show higher accuracy than target-capture sequencing to detect structural variants (SVs) by identifying breakpoints (BPs) in non-coding regions. However, short-read WGS (SR-WGS) pipelines often suffer from insufficient accuracy and discrepancies between analytical tools, posing challenges for clinical interpretation. We evaluated 7 germline SVs previously detected by SR-WGS using target adaptive sampling long-read sequencing (TAS-LRS). The target region spanned 13 Mb (approximately 0.4% of the genome), covering 147 hereditary tumor-related genes and 20 kb flanking each SV. Alignment was performed using minimap2, followed by SV analysis with nanomonsv. TAS-LRS achieved an average on-target coverage of 28.5x and a 7.0-fold enrichment. Consistent BPs were confirmed for 6 out of 7 variants. The single discrepant case involved a suspected PMS2 translocation in SR- WGS, which TAS-LRS identified as a false positive due to a 174-bp insertion of a PMS2-homologous sequence insertion in a distinct region on chromosome 4. Furthermore, TAS-LRS enabled nucleotide-level evaluation of all BPs and clarified complex rearrangements, such as SVA retrotransposon insertions in BRCA2, which were previously misclassified or unclear in SR-WGS. While SR-WGS is effective for detecting various SVs, it remains prone to false positives and misinterpretations of complex genomic structures. Integrating TAS- LRS into the diagnostic workflow significantly enhances the accuracy of germline SV detection, providing a robust framework for precise genomic medicine.

en: Hereditary breast and ovarian cancer diagnosed through comprehensive genomic profiling in a young lung cancer patient
ja: 若年肺がん患者のCGPを契機に診断された遺伝性乳がん卵巣がん
abs: Background: Although comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) is widely used in lung cancer (LC), germline pathogenic variants (GPVs) identified through CGP are rarely reported.
