Results: Universal screening was explained to 175 patients (84.5%), consent was obtained from 171 (82.6%), and screening was performed in 168 (81.2%). dMMR was identified in 43 cases (25.6%); PMS2 loss in 34, MSH6 loss in 6, and combined PMS2/MSH6 loss in 3. Genetic counseling was recommended for 40 of 43 dMMR patients, of whom 29 (67.4%) completed counseling and 4 (9.3%) had scheduled appointments. Germline testing was performed in 13 patients (multigene panel in 10, MMR genes only in 3), and pathogenic germline variants were identified in 4 (30.8%). Including one case previously diagnosed at another institution, LS was diagnosed in 5 of 168 screened patients (3.0%), with pathogenic variants in MLH1 (n=3), MSH2 (n=1), and MSH6 (n=1). Of the 5 LS cases, 2 met Amsterdam II criteria. Conclusions: Universal screening using PMS2 and MSH6 immunohistochemistry effectively identified dMMR and LS in EC patients. Closer collaboration with genetic medicine specialists is needed to improve LS diagnosis.

en: Initial Experience with Comprehensive Genomic Profiling in Renal Cell Carcinoma
ja: 腎細胞がんにおける包括的がんゲノムプロファイリングの初期経験
abs: Background The relationship between genomic findings and treatment response in renal cell carcinoma (RCC) has not been fully understood. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 9 patients with RCC who underwent Comprehensive Genomic Profiling (CGP) at our institution. Results Our cohort included 8 male and 1 female patients, 7 de novo metastatic and 2 recurrent metastatic RCC, and clear cell/ chromophobe/FH-deficient subtypes in 7/1/1 cases. CGP specimens, collected after systemic therapy, were from the primary tumor/ metastatic lesions/blood in 3/3/3 cases. TMB ranged from 1 to 8.4. All tumors were microsatellite stable (MSS). Three patients have died during the observation period (median 915 days) after CGP. Pathogenic variants of VHL/PBRM1 were detected in 5 (56%)/3 (33%) cases. TP53/PTEN/MTOR pathogenic variants were identified in 3/2/1 cases, respectively. All patients received immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. Two ICI-responders had low TMB. Discussion High frequency of VHL pathogenic variants was confirmed. RCC is one of the tumor types in which ICI efficacy has been observed regardless of molecular profile. Our findings suggest that mechanisms distinct from those in other cancers may underlie ICI response in RCC. To be noted, potentially actionable pathogenic variants, including those in PTEN, were identified. These findings suggest that CGP may play an important role in the management of RCC.

en: A case of bladder cancer in which BRCA1 was identified by PGPV in cancer gene panel testing
ja: がん遺伝子パネル検査のPGPVでBRCA1が同定された膀胱がんの1例
abs: Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer Syndrome (HBOC) is an autosomal dominant inherited disorder characterized by pathogenic variants in the tumor suppressor genes BRCA1 or BRCA2, leading to the development of breast cancer, ovarian cancer, and other cancers. We report a case in which HBOC was definitively diagnosed following a cancer gene panel test for bladder cancer, and relatedness analysis was performed on two family members. The proband is an 82-year-old male who was diagnosed with bladder cancer at our hospital in 2024. Curative resection was planned after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, but was cancelled due to renal dysfunction. In 2025, he was referred to the cancer genome medicine outpatient clinic, and a bladder tumor sample was submitted for Foundation One CDx cancer genome profiling test (F1-T). The F1-T results detected a pathogenic variant in BRCA1, identified as PGPV (presumed germline pathogenic variant). The genetic testing results led to a diagnosis of germline variant, confirming the diagnosis of HBOC. Genetic counseling was also provided to the two daughters, and single-site testing for each yielded negative results. We have instructed other family members who wish to receive genetic counseling to contact the genetic counseling department. With the introduction of insurance coverage for cancer gene panel testing in 2019, opportunities to diagnose hereditary disorders from secondary findings are increasing. Building a robust genetic medicine department will become even more crucial in the future.

en: Retrospective analysis of BRCA domains and PARP inhibitor efficacy in BRCA1/2 pathogenic variant- positive ovarian cancer
ja: BRCA1/2病的バリアント陽性卵巣がんにおけるBRCAドメインとPARP阻害薬有効性の後方視的解析
abs: Background: BRCA1/2 pathogenic variants (PV) confer sensitivity to platinum and PARP inhibitors (PARPi), although clinical outcomes vary among patients. Emerging evidence suggests that the functional consequences of BRCA1/2 PV may depend on their localization within domains involved in homologous recombination repair. Objective: This study aimed to clarify the significance of domain-specific BRCA1/2 PV in ovarian cancer, focusing on treatment response and outcomes. Methods: We conducted a retrospective study of ovarian cancer patients harboring BRCA1/2 PV. Variants were stratified according to localization within the BRCA1 RING/BRCT domains and the BRCA2 RAD51-binding domain. Results: Among 261 patients with newly diagnosed ovarian cancer treated between 2020 and 2025, 27 had BRCA1/2 PV. Median age was 55 years. High-grade serous carcinoma was observed in 24 (89%), and 22 (81%) had stage III/IV disease. All patients received platinum-based chemotherapy, and 20 (74%) received PARPi maintenance therapy. Among PARPi-treated patients, 7 had variants localized to these domains and 13 had other variants. Median progression-free survival (PFS) was 33.2 vs 21.5 months, and median time to next treatment (TTNT) was 32.0 vs 22.6 months, respectively. In first-line maintenance cases, median PFS was 30.3 vs 28.1 months, whereas in recurrent cases, median PFS was 47.7 vs 8.4 months. Conclusion: Functional domain-based analysis of BRCA1/2 may provide prognostic and therapeutic insights beyond conventional BRCA classification in ovarian cancer.

en: Status of cascade testing for first-degree relatives of hereditary breast and ovarian cancer patients at our hospital
ja: 当院における遺伝性乳がん卵巣がん患者の第一度近親者へのカスケード検査の現状
abs: [Background] Diagnosing hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (HBOC) is crucial for early cancer detection and preventive intervention in probands and relatives. While Japan's cascade testing uptake rate is approximately 20%, the data from regional core hospitals such as our hospital remain insufficient. This study aimed to investigate the cascade testing uptake rate and evaluate clinical challenges at our hospital. [Methods] We included probands with BRCA1/2 pathogenic variants identified between April 2023 and January 2026. The primary endpoint was the cascade testing uptake rate among first-degree relatives (FDRs) by April 2026. [Results] Among 15 probands, 65 FDRs (including seven young relatives under the age of 18 years) were identified. Only five FDRs (7.7%) attended genetic counseling. Three individuals (all daughters of probands) underwent cascade testing, resulting in an overall uptake rate of 4.6%. [Conclusions] Our hospital's uptake rate (4.6%) is significantly lower than the previously reported national average of 20%. Although the presence of young relatives among FDRs may have contributed to this lower rate, the rate remains low at 5.1% even after excluding them. The low attendance rate for genetic counseling is a major contributing factor. The strengthening of genetic counseling systems and the establishing of mechanisms to support family information-sharing are urgent priorities. The proactive communication from healthcare providers and educational activities are essential to lower psychological barriers and promote regional genetic medicine.

en: Lynch Syndrome Identified After Endometrial Cancer in a Patient with Prior Rectal and Subsequent Sigmoid Cancer
ja: 直腸がん・S状結腸がんの既往後に子宮体がんを契機に同定されたLynch症候群
abs: [Introduction] Lynch syndrome (LS) is an autosomal dominant hereditary disorder caused by pathogenic variants in DNA mismatch repair (MMR) genes, significantly increasing the risk for colorectal (CRC) and endometrial cancers (EC). We report a case of LS diagnosed via genetic testing after EC treatment in a patient with early-onset CRC, which subsequently led to detecting metachronous sigmoid colon cancer. [Case Report] A 50-year-old female with a history of rectal cancer at age 29 had undergone regular colonoscopies and multiple endoscopic resections for polyps. Her father was diagnosed with CRC at age 34 and died of gastric cancer at age 45. At age 48, she was diagnosed with EC and underwent hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and pelvic/para-aortic lymphadenectomy. Pathology showed Grade 2 endometrioid carcinoma, Stage IB (pT1bN0M0). Postoperatively, she received six cycles of adjuvant chemotherapy with paclitaxel and carboplatin. Given her clinical history, MMR protein immunohistochemistry (IHC) showed a loss of MLH1 and PMS2 expression. Following genetic counseling, a pathogenic variant in the MLH1 gene was identified, confirming LS. Subsequent surveillance colonoscopy detected sigmoid colon cancer, which was treated with laparoscopic total colectomy. [Conclusion] In gynecology, EC and ovarian cancer are key sentinel indicators for LS diagnosis. Clinicians must prioritize not only proband treatment and surveillance but also strategies for the early detection and prevention of cancer in at-risk relatives.

en: Gynecologic Surveillance in Lynch Syndrome: Three Cases Illustrating Benefits and Limitations
ja: Lynch症候群の婦人科サーベイランス：利点と限界を示す3例
abs: Background/Aim: Lynch syndrome (LS) confers a high risk of endometrial (EC) and ovarian cancers. Patient education and gynecologic surveillance with transvaginal ultrasound and endometrial cytology/biopsy are recommended. Risk-reducing hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (RRH-BSO) is offered in Western guidelines but implemented cautiously in Japan. We report three cases of endometrial atypical hyperplasia (AH) or EC diagnosed during LS surveillance. Case 1: A woman in her late 40s, an MSH2 carrier with two prior colorectal cancers, experienced anxiety with serial biopsies. An endometrial polyp with hyperplasia prompted hysterectomy and BSO. She expressed relief from surveillance. Case 2: A cancer-free woman in her 50s, an MSH2 carrier, developed abnormal bleeding in surveillance year 2. Stage IA EC was diagnosed, but positive peritoneal cytology required adjuvant chemotherapy. Case 3: A woman in her 50s, an MSH2 carrier with prior colorectal cancer, had AH confirmed on surveillance endometrial sampling and underwent hysterectomy and BSO at the precancerous stage, which she viewed favorably. Discussion/Conclusion: Surveillance enabled detection of precancerous lesions and prompt response to symptoms but did not preclude adverse features in one case. RRH-BSO may offer both oncologic and psychological benefit. Individualized, lifelong management-considering life stage, fertility, prior cancers, causative gene, and patient values-together with ongoing genetic counseling, is essential to support informed decisions.

en: Six-Year Report on Risk-Reducing Surgery and Decision-Making in Pathogenic BRCA1/2 Variant Carriers at Our Institution
ja: 当院のBRCA1/2病的バリアント保持者におけるリスク低減手術と意思決定の6年間の報告
abs: Background: Risk-reducing surgery is important for carriers of pathogenic BRCA1/2 variants, but decision-making is influenced by clinical and personal factors. We reviewed our 6-year experience to clarify implementation and factors. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 20 individuals with pathogenic BRCA1/2 variants. Primary disease, BRCA1/2 status, surgery, pathology, follow-up, and reasons for non-implementation were reviewed. Results: The cohort included 17 women and 3 men; 7 carried BRCA1 variants and 13 carried BRCA2 variants. Risk-reducing surgery was performed in 8 women; 8 underwent risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy and 4 underwent contralateral risk-reducing mastectomy. Time from result disclosure to surgical decision ranged from the same day to 1 year; 7 of 8 decisions were confirmed within 34 days. Serous tubal intraepithelial lesions were detected in 2 patients: a BRCA2 carrier with breast cancer and an unaffected BRCA1 carrier identified through cascade testing. Surgery was not performed in several patients due to treatment, poor condition, other malignancies, advanced disease, or uncertain follow-up. Conclusions: Risk-reducing surgery after identification of pathogenic BRCA1/2 variants was influenced not only by genetic risk but also by primary disease, prognosis, treatment status, age, follow-up pathways, and family testing. Occult tubal lesions highlight the importance of timely gynecologic referral and multidisciplinary genetic care. Decision-making support may help connect carriers and at-risk relatives to surveillance and preventive interventions.

en: Nonsense-Associated Altered Splicing Observed in a Lynch Syndrome Family with an MSH2 Nonsense Variant
ja: MSH2ナンセンスバリアントを有するLynch症候群家系で観察されたナンセンス関連スプライシング変化
abs: Introduction: Nonsense variants are known to trigger nonsense-mediated mRNA decay. In addition, an aberrant splicing mechanism called nonsense-associated altered splicing (NAS) has also been reported, in which the exon harboring a premature termination codon is skipped. The mechanism underlying NAS remains poorly understood, and to the best of our knowledge, reports of NAS in individuals with Lynch syndrome (LS) are limited. Case: A 63-year-old female presented for genetic counseling regarding cascade testing of her son. She developed skin and endometrial cancers in her 30s, and subsequent genetic testing revealed a pathogenic variant in MSH2, NM_000251.3 :c.2038C>T p.(Arg680*), leading to the diagnosis of LS. As part of cascade testing, she underwent repeated genetic testing, which confirmed the identical nonsense variant in the MSH2 gene. RNA analysis showed two distinct transcripts expressed at approximately comparable levels; one containing the nonsense variant at codon 680, and the other lacking exon 13, the exon harboring the premature termination codon, resulting in a frameshift. These findings indicated that the variant induced NAS. The same variant and RNA analysis findings were also confirmed in her son. Conclusion: RNA analysis in these cases suggested that this variant not only generates a premature termination codon at codon 680 but also induces NAS. Because this variant is not predicted by ESEfinder 3.0 to affect an exonic splicing enhancer (ESE) motif, the observed exon skipping may occur through an unknown mechanism other than ESE disruption.

en: Young-onset metachronous bilateral breast cancer with a germline TP53 pathogenic variant in a BRCA1/2-negative patient
ja: BRCA1/2陰性患者における生殖細胞系列TP53病的バリアントを有する若年発症異時性両側乳がん
abs: Li-Fraumeni syndrome (LFS) is a hereditary cancer syndrome caused by TP53 pathogenic variants and is associated with early-onset malignancies, including breast cancer. Identification of TP53 variants is important because it may influence treatment and surveillance strategies. A 46-year-old woman developed right breast cancer 18 years after treatment for left breast cancer at age 27. The initial cancer was Stage IIA, hormone receptor (HR)-positive, HER2-positive disease treated with breast-conserving surgery, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, and endocrine therapy. She remained recurrence-free. The second cancer was Stage IIB, HR-negative, HER2-positive breast cancer, and neoadjuvant chemotherapy was initiated. Because of metachronous bilateral breast cancer, BRCA1/2 testing revealed no pathogenic variants. However, the young age at onset and bilateral HER2-positive phenotype raised suspicion of a hereditary cancer syndrome, particularly LFS. Following genetic counseling, TP53 testing identifieIdentification of a germline TP53 pathogenic variant during neoadjuvant chemotherapy enabled preoperative treatment planning, including consideration of mastectomy to avoid radiation exposure. This case underscores that TP53 pathogenic variants can be overlooked when reliance is placed solely on BRCA1/2 testing, particularly in patients lacking classic LFS features. Genetic counseling and TP53 testing should be considered in young-onset or bilateral breast cancer because results may substantially affect local treatment decisions.

en: Implementation of TCGA Molecular Classification Panel in Endometrial Cancer Care Centered on Radiotherapy
ja: 放射線治療を中心とした子宮体がん診療へのTCGA分子分類パネルの導入
abs: Background: Molecular classification of endometrial cancer (EC)-including POLE mutation, mismatch repair deficiency (dMMR), and p53 abnormality-is valuable for prognostication and treatment individualization. We established a system integrating the TCGA classification (POLEmut/dMMR/p53abn/NSMP) into routine clinical care centered on radiotherapy to optimize treatment intensity and identify hereditary tumor syndromes. Methods: Consecutive EC cases after panel introduction were included. Molecular classification was performed using POLE sequencing, MMR immunohistochemistry (MLH1/MSH2/MSH6/ PMS2), and p53 immunohistochemistry. Treatment decisions were retrospectively reviewed. The study was conducted under institutional opt-out consent. Results: Molecular classification directly informed adjuvant therapy selection. POLEmut cases provided rationale for de-escalation, including omission of chemotherapy. p53abn cases supported treatment intensification by adding chemotherapy to radiotherapy. For dMMR cases, the panel prompted development of a systematic referral pathway for Lynch syndrome screening, particularly given the limited availability of MLH1 methylation testing in Japan. NSMP cases were managed based on conventional pathological risk factors within the radiotherapy-centered framework. Conclusions: Molecular classification panels are feasible in radiotherapy-centered EC care and proved useful for optimizing treatment intensity, standardizing clinical workflows, and identifying Lynch syndrome candidates.

en: Current Status and Challenges of Genetic Testing in Cancer-Unaffected Individuals After Genetic Counseling for HBOC
ja: HBOC遺伝カウンセリング後の未発症者における遺伝学的検査の現状と課題
abs: Background: In hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (HBOC), sharing pathogenic variant information with relatives and linking unaffected relatives to genetic testing and risk-reducing care are important. As testing for first-degree relatives is expected to be covered by health insurance in Japan, we assessed the current status and issues at our hospital. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 55 unaffected individuals among 179 who received HBOC-related genetic counseling from January 2016 to December 2025. Age, sex, relationship to the proband, test uptake and results, risk-reducing surgery (RRSO/RRM), and cancer development after diagnosis were analyzed. Results: Median age was 38 years (range, 5-71); 44 were female and 11 male. Fifty were first-degree relatives and 5 were second-degree or more distant relatives. After counseling, 34 individuals (61.8%) underwent genetic testing. Uptake was 59% in women, 73% in men, 62% in first-degree relatives, and 60% in more distant relatives. Eleven were diagnosed with HBOC (BRCA1, n=5; BRCA2, n=6). Two underwent RRSO, and none underwent RRM. One developed breast cancer during follow-up. Test uptake tended to increase after 2020. Discussion: About 60% of counseled unaffected relatives underwent genetic testing, with a similar rate among first-degree relatives, whereas nearly 40% did not. With expanded insurance coverage, stronger genetic counseling systems and support for family information sharing are needed to ensure testing opportunities for unaffected relatives, especially first-degree relatives.

en: Current Status of Colorectal Surveillance and Metachronous Colorectal Cancer in Lynch Syndrome
ja: Lynch症候群における大腸サーベイランスと異時性大腸がんの現状
abs: Background: Lynch syndrome (LS) is associated with a high risk of colorectal and other cancers caused by mismatch repair gene alterations. Current guidelines recommend regular colonoscopic surveillance, but real-world data remain limited. Objective: To evaluate adherence to colorectal surveillance and the occurrence of metachronous colorectal cancer (mCRC) in patients with LS at our hospital. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 12 patients diagnosed with LS in Clinical Genetics between April 2019 and May 2026. Age, sex, causative gene, primary cancer, surveillance status, and mCRC development were analyzed. Results: Median age at diagnosis was 51 years (range, 33-66), and 5 patients were male. Pathogenic variants were identified inMLH1/MSH2/MSH6/PMS2 in 2/8/1/1 patients, respectively. Primary cancers included colorectal cancer in 6 patients (right-sided colon, n=4; left-sided colon, n=1; rectum, n=1), endometrial cancer in 5, and no cancer in 1. All patients underwent annual colonoscopy according to guideline recommendations. Median surveillance duration was 39 months (range, 11-84). mCRC developed in 2 patients (16.7%), both were early-stage cancers. No new LS-related extracolonic cancers developed. Conclusions: Complete adherence was achieved through collaboration among gastroenterology, surgery, and clinical genetics departments. Nevertheless, early-stage mCRC developed despite annual surveillance, suggesting rapid development of some LS-associated colorectal cancers. High-quality colonoscopy and proactive adenoma removal may reduce mCRC risk.

en: A Case of Li-Fraumeni Syndrome Difficult to Diagnose Genetically
ja: 遺伝学的診断が困難であったLi-Fraumeni症候群の1例
abs: [Background] Li-Fraumeni syndrome (LFS) is a hereditary tumor syndrome caused by germline pathogenic variants (GPVs) in TP53, characterized by early-onset and multiple cancers. We report a case in which hereditary tumor syndrome was strongly suspected based on the phenotype, but genetic diagnosis was difficult. [Case Report] A woman in her 20s developed synchronous bilateral HER2-positive breast cancer. Her mother had lung cancer in her 20s, and her maternal grandmother had lung cancer in her 30s. Suspecting hereditary cancer syndrome, we first performed insurance-covered BRCA1/2 testing, which was negative. Because the patient met the Chompret criteria, LFS was suspected and multi-gene panel testing (MGPT) including TP53 was performed. However, no pathogenic variants were detected. This MGPT analyzed only the coding region from exon 2 onward of TP53. Therefore, we repeated MGPT using a 146-gene panel including exon 1, which contains the TP53 transcription start site. This analysis identified a large deletion spanning exon 1 (TP53:g.7687016_7688272del), suspected to be a GPV, leading to the diagnosis of LFS. [Conclusion] Even when the phenotype strongly suggests a hereditary tumor syndrome, genetic diagnosis may fail because of: (1) variants outside the analysis range, (2) involvement of unanalyzed susceptibility genes, or (3) involvement of unknown genes. In this case, continued genetic evaluation based on the phenotype led to the diagnosis of LFS, highlighting the limitations of current testing strategies.

en: The impact of BRCA genetic testing for breast cancer-free individuals becoming covered by insurance.
ja: 乳がん未発症者へのBRCA遺伝学的検査の保険適用化の影響
abs: In April 2020, it was included in the national health insurance system for the purpose of diagnosing hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome (HBOC). Finally, in June 2026, BRCA genetic testing for individuals who have not yet developed breast cancer but whose family history includes a BRCA gene mutation will be covered by health insurance. Until now, asymptomatic individuals have been tested at their own expense, and single-site testing has been performed. This report will discuss the current state of breast clinics that provide genetic counseling. A risk assessment was conducted on 136 cases of primary breast cancer diagnosed and treated between April 2020 and April 2026. We selected 40 cases (29.4%) and performed BRCA1/2 genetic testing on 19 of those 40 cases (47.5%). We found pathogenic mutations in the BRCA gene in three cases. One reason why people may not undergo genetic testing is the financial burden on family members if a pathogenic mutation is found. Some breast cancer patients are now getting tested after learning about the insurance coverage for those who have not yet developed symptoms. HBOC treatment in Japan has undergone rapid changes since its inclusion in health insurance coverage. With this revision of medical fees, an increase in the number of people seeking testing among asymptomatic individuals is expected. However, as healthcare professionals providing genetic medicine, I believe it is necessary to carefully consider whether insurance coverage and treatment based on genetic risk can coexist in the future.

en: Reimbursement Gap for Unaffected Relatives in HBOC Families Identified by Tumor-Only CGP in Japan
ja: 本邦で腫瘍のみCGPにより同定されたHBOC家系の未発症血縁者における償還のギャップ
abs: Background: Following the 2026 revision of the Japanese medical reimbursement system, unaffected first-degree relatives of patients with hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (HBOC) became eligible for insurance-covered genetic testing and surveillance. However, this coverage applies primarily to families where a pathogenic BRCA1/2 variant was identified through insured germline testing. Families identified via tumor-only cancer genomic profiling (CGP) followed by self-pay germline confirmation may remain outside this framework. Case Presentation: A 61-year-old man with recurrent ampullary carcinoma underwent tumor-only CGP, which detected a BRCA2 c.9117G>A variant (VAF 64%) as a suspected secondary finding. His family history included ovarian cancer in his mother and breast cancer in his sister. This variant is classified as pathogenic/likely pathogenic in HBOC databases. After genetic counseling, its germline origin was confirmed via self-pay single-site testing. Although the patient sought care for his children, his unaffected relatives were ineligible for insurance-covered genetic testing or risk-reducing interventions because his confirmatory germline test was performed outside the insured system. Conclusion: The 2026 reimbursement revision represents important progress in hereditary cancer care in Japan. However, this case highlights a critical gap for families identified through tumor-only CGP followed by self-pay germline confirmation. Further discussion is needed to ensure equitable access to genetic testing and preventive care for these individuals.

en: Preliminary results for detection of secondary findings using CGP for hematological disorder
ja: 血液疾患に対するCGPを用いた二次的所見検出の予備的結果
abs: Background: CGP insurance was approved for hematological malignancies last year in Japan. Careful consideration is required because secondary findings suggestive of hereditary tumor syndromes can occur in hematological malignancies. In this study, we examined previous findings regarding secondary findings of CGP in patients with confirmed or suspected hematological malignancies at our institute. Patients and methods. A total 15 patients received CGP (HEM-SIGH) at our institute. We assessed the results of secondary findings and genetic testing following genetic counselling. Results: All 15 patients were able to evaluate the results of the CGP test. All patients wanted to know the results of the secondary findings. Matched normal DNA was derived from oral mucosal swabs in all patients. Three of these patients had pathogenic variants detected in matched specimens using oral mucosa. Of these, one case exhibited a KRAS G12D mutation in the matched normal sample, which was deemed to be contamination due to a clear discrepancy with the phenotype. In contrast, two cases (13.3%) exhibited pathogenic variants in BRCA2 and TP53 as secondary findings. Following genetic counselling, these variants were confirmed to be of germline origin through single-site testing of nail specimens conducted at our institution. Conclusion: Our results highlight the clinical necessity of establishing protocols for managing secondary findings and genetic counselling in hematological cancer genetic profiling (CGP), in line with current standards in solid tumor oncology.

en: Development of Photoimmunotherapy Targets for Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer-Associated Breast Cancer
ja: 遺伝性乳がん卵巣がん関連乳がんに対する光免疫療法標的の開発
abs: [Background] Women with hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (HBOC) have a high lifetime risk of developing breast cancer (BC) and are often diagnosed at a young age. Although risk-reducing mastectomy is recommended as a preventive strategy, it is not widely accepted because of its substantial physical and psychological burden. Therefore, we investigated near-infrared photoimmunotherapy (NIR- PIT) as a novel minimally invasive preventive approach. [Materials and Methods] Total RNA was extracted from FFPE specimens of normal mammary gland (MG) tissue and BC tissue obtained from women with pathogenic variants (PVs) in BRCA1 or BRCA2 (8 cases each) and from women without BRCA1/2 PVs (3 cases). Comprehensive gene expression analysis was performed using RNA-sequencing. We then conducted comparative analyses between normal MG tissue and BC tissue in each group, with a focus on cell surface molecules that could serve as potential NIR-PIT targets. In addition, immunohistochemical (IHC) staining was performed to assess the localization of the candidate molecules. [Results and Discussion] Several molecules were identified as significantly upregulated in BC tissue from women with HBOC. Among them, three candidate molecules -X, Y, and Z- showed potential BC-specific expression were selected for further evaluation. Furthermore, IHC analysis demonstrated that Molecule X was localized on the cell membrane, suggesting that it is a promising target for NIR-PIT. We plan to further evaluate its therapeutic potential by performing in vitro NIR-PIT using cell lines expressing Molecule X.

en: Clinical Characteristics and Genetic Counseling in BRCA-Positive Prostate Cancer at Our Institution
ja: 当院におけるBRCA陽性前立腺がんの臨床的特徴と遺伝カウンセリング
abs: Background: Prostate cancer (PC) with BRCA1/2 pathogenic variants, especially BRCA2 variants, is associated with aggressive disease and poor prognosis. Because of its close association with hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome (HBOC), it is an important hereditary tumor in urology. Methods: We retrospectively evaluated the clinical characteristics and genetic counseling interventions in five patients with BRCA1/2 pathogenic variants among 27 patients who underwent comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) for PC at our institution between January 2021 and March 2026. Results: The mean age was 73 years. All patients had BRCA2 pathogenic variants. Family histories of malignancy were observed in three cases, including pancreatic, gastric, thyroid, and liver cancers; however, all variants were somatic pathogenic variants. The mean initial PSA level was markedly elevated at 2,199 ng/ml. All cases were Grade Group 5, and intraductal carcinoma of the prostate (IDC-P) was observed in two cases. Two patients had Lymph node metastases, and all patients had bone metastases at diagnosis. Genetic counseling (GC) was explained to all patients and families at CGP result disclosure. Three families declined GC, while two were considering consultation. Conclusions: BRCA-positive PC showed highly aggressive clinical features in our cohort. Although BRCA-associated PC is often associated with germline pathogenic variants, all cases involved somatic variants. Nevertheless, family history assessment and appropriate information regarding GC remain important.

en: A Case of MEN1 in Which Expert Panel Discussion Prompted Reclassification of a VUS as Pathogenic
ja: エキスパートパネル討議によりVUSが病的へ再分類されたMEN1の1例
abs: Background: Variants of uncertain significance (VUS) can be reclassified, but standardized re-evaluation procedures remain insufficiently established. We report a case of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) in which expert panel (EP) discussion following comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) included a review of prior genetic testing results, leading to reclassification of a previously identified VUS as pathogenic. Case: A woman in her 50s with primary hyperparathyroidism, pituitary adenoma, a mediastinal neuroendocrine tumor, and a family history of hypercalcemia was clinically diagnosed with MEN1. Initial MEN1 genetic testing identified only a VUS (NM_130799.2:c.1351-9C<G); therefore, MEN1 management was continued based on the clinical diagnosis. Three years later, CGP using the NCC Oncopanel (NOP) was performed for the mediastinal neuroendocrine tumor. Although the variant was not identified by the NOP, EP discussion, which comprehensively reviewed her clinical findings and prior genetic history, revealed that the variant had been classified as pathogenic in ClinVar. Following inquiry to the testing laboratory, the variant was officially reclassified as pathogenic. The patient received genetic counseling, including genetic testing for at-risk relatives. Discussion: Reclassification of a VUS can inform surveillance and genetic counseling for at-risk relatives. This case suggests that EP may serve as a platform for the comprehensive reassessment of clinical and genetic data and provide an opportunity for re-evaluation of VUS beyond variants directly identified by CGP.

en: Respiratory Complex I Deficiency Caused by a Novel Multi-exonic PUS1 Deletion
ja: 新規の複数エクソンにわたるPUS1欠失による呼吸鎖複合体I欠損症
abs: Myopathy, lactic acidosis, and sideroblastic anemia type 1 (MLASA1) is an extremely rare mitochondrial disorder caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in PUS1, which encodes a mitochondrial tRNA pseudouridine synthase essential for mitochondrial protein synthesis. We describe two affected siblings presenting with progressive myopathy, lactic acidosis, sideroblastic anemia, short stature, developmental delay, and mild cognitive impairment. Depth-based copy number variation analysis of whole-exome sequencing data revealed a novel homozygous multi-exonic deletion in PUS1. The deletion breakpoints were defined by Sanger sequencing as a 9,964 bp deletion spanning part of intron 3 through exons 4 to 6 and extending into the untranslated region, resulting in complete loss of the C-terminal coding region. Skeletal muscle histology demonstrated ragged red fibers, whereas immunohistochemistry showed a selective and near-complete loss of NDUFB8, indicating impaired assembly of respiratory chain complex I. A systematic review of previously reported MLASA1 cases revealed marked clinical heterogeneity, including frequent developmental delay, dysmorphic features, and multi-organ involvement. These findings expand the genotypic and phenotypic landscape of MLASA1 and highlight the diagnostic value of copy number variation analysis in unresolved mitochondrial disorders. The impairment of complex I underscores the particular vulnerability of translation-dependent respiratory chain components in PUS1-related diseases.

en: Preserved mutant SOD1 transcript expression in familial ALS with splice-altering or protein-truncating variants
ja: スプライシング変化型・タンパク切断型バリアントの家族性ALSにおける変異SOD1転写産物発現の保持
abs: Background: Variants in the superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD1) gene are a major genetic cause of familial amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (FALS) in Japan. Most pathogenic SOD1 variants are missense and are thought to involve toxic gain-of-function. In contrast, splice-altering and protein-truncating variants are rare, and whether mutant transcript expression is preserved remains unclear. We investigate mutant SOD1 transcript expression in FALS cases carrying such variants. Methods: SOD1 complementary DNA (cDNA) from patient-derived lymphoblastoid cell lines was analyzed by direct nucleotide sequencing. Droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) analysis of cDNA was performed using allele-specific assays, with SDHA as an internal control, to compare wild-type and mutant transcripts. Results: Three patients with FALS carried heterozygous SOD1 variants: c.357_357+2dup, spanning the exon 4-intron 4 junction, c.379_380del [p.(Leu127GlyfsTer6); exon 5], and c.400G>T [p.(Glu134Ter); exon 5]. Direct nucleotide sequencing of cDNA demonstrated expression of all three mutant alleles: c.357_357+2dup generated an in-frame p.Val120dup transcript, whereas c.379_380del and c.400G>T transcripts carried the expected frameshift and nonsense variants, respectively. Allele-specific ddPCR showed no apparent reduction of mutant transcripts relative to wild-type transcripts. Conclusion: Mutant SOD1 transcripts were preserved in FALS cases with splice-altering or protein-truncating variants. These findings provide a molecular rationale for considering tofersen in patients with ALS carrying such SOD1 variants.

en: Investigation of c.3725G>A of dysferlin not to determine as a pathogenic variant
ja: 病的バリアントと判定されないdysferlin c.3725G>Aの検討
abs: In previous dysferlin gene analyses, five alleles of c.3725G>A (p.R1242H) were found in four individuals, but this could not be immediately classified as a pathogenic variant. Therefore, we investigated this variant further. In the dysferlin gene analyses performed so far, we were able to analyze exon 34, where this variant is present, in 371 individuals (287 using Sanger sequencing, and 84 using next-generation sequencing). We referred to the frequency in TogoVar. We prefered muscle immunohistochemistry and clinical features in cases with this variant. Sanger sequencing was performed on all exons in cases with this variant. This variant was found in one homozygous case, one compound heterozygous case, and two heterozygous cases. If we tentatively classify the homozygous and compound heterozygous cases as dysferlinopathy, the prevalence was 0.67% in dysferlinopathy (225 people) and 0.68% in non-dysferlinopathy cases (146 people). The database reported a frequency of 1.1~1.6%. Muscle immunohistochemistry showed absence in homozygous cases and decreased in one heterozygous case. The clinical presentation appeared typical in homozygous cases, but atypical in others. Although immunohistochemistry suggests this variant is pathogenic, attention should be paid to the presence of other variants, particularly the fact that typical case had variant which did not appear in the database. Considering the frequency of this variant in the general population, its frequency in dysferlinopathy seems too low. For these reasons, we concluded that this variant cannot be considered pathogenic.

en: Novel XK variant identified in a patient with McLeod syndrome presenting initially with sleep apnea
ja: 睡眠時無呼吸で初発したMcLeod症候群患者で同定された新規XKバリアント
abs: McLeod syndrome is known as a neuroacanthocytosis syndrome characterized by both hematological and neurological features and is inherited as an X-linked trait; affected individuals are generally males. This clinical entity is rare, with an estimated prevalence of 1:10,000,000. Recently, we encountered a male patient with MLS. There was a past history of receiving continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy. He was referred to our hospital with his complains of myalgia and fatigue in both lower legs. On examination, a nasal voice was noted. Neurological examination revealed decreased deep tendon reflexes. However, no muscle weakness or involuntary movements, such as tremor or fasciculations, were detected. Laboratory examination revealed elevated creatine kinase levels. For the aim of genetic diagnosis, clinical exome sequencing was performed and a novel frameshift variant in the X-linked Kx blood group antigen gene (XK) was detected. Retrospective laboratory analysis showed reticulocytes accounted for 1.7% and microscopic examination of a blood smear showed presence of acanthocytosis. Immunoblot analysis using a mouse monoclonal antibody against Kx showed absent Kx expression. These findings indicated the McLeod phenotype. It is important to recognize that patients with MLS exhibit a wide clinical spectrum and that only some symptoms may be present in the early stages, before the full clinical phenotype develops.

en: Epitranscriptomic landscapes of TDP-43 and FUS reveal convergent m6A-modified RNA networks in ALS
ja: TDP-43とFUSのエピトランスクリプトーム地図がALSで収束するm6A修飾RNAネットワークを明らかにする
abs: [Objective] Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is characterized by aggregates of RNA-binding proteins (RBPs), including TDP-43 and FUS. N6-methyladenosine (m6A), the most abundant internal RNA modification, regulates multiple aspects of RNA metabolism. We investigated the m6A-modified RNA interactomes of ALS-related RBPs using direct RNA sequencing. [Methods] We performed RNA immunoprecipitation in SH-SY5Y cells using anti-TDP-43 and anti- FUS antibodies, followed by Nanopore direct RNA sequencing of bound transcripts. Bioinformatic analyses were conducted using Dorado for basecalling, minimap2 for alignment, f5c for signal alignment, and m6Anet for m6A prediction. Functional enrichment analysis was performed using Metascape. [Results] We identified 192 m6A-modified RNAs associated with TDP-43 and 700 associated with FUS (modification probability >0.8). Functional enrichment that TDP-43-associated m6A RNAs were analysis revealed significantly enriched in axon injury response pathways, whereas FUS-associated m6A RNAs were linked to stress responses. Notably, both TDP-43- and FUS-associated m6A RNAs converged on pathways related to RNA metabolism and translation. [Conclusion] Direct RNA sequencing uncovered distinct yet overlapping m6A RNA networks associated with TDP-43 and FUS. Our findings suggest that interactions between ALS-related RBPs and m6A RNAs may be involved in dysregulated RNA metabolism, providing new insights into the epitranscriptomic mechanisms underlying ALS pathogenesis.

en: Clinical Stability Following a Switch to Migalastat in Fabry Disease with an Amenable GLA Variant (L300P)
ja: 治療反応性GLAバリアント（L300P）を有するFabry病でのミガーラスタット切替後の臨床的安定
abs: Background: Migalastat is an oral chaperone therapy for Fabry disease in patients with amenable GLA variants. We report a case with the GLA L300P variant showing clinical stability after switching from enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) to migalastat. Case Presentation: A 61-year-old man with Fabry disease carrying the GLA L300P (c.899T>C) variant was switched from agalsidase alfa to migalastat. Plasma lyso- Gb3 shifted from 17.3 ng/mL at baseline to 15.2, 20.7, and 12.0 at 4, 7, and 12 months, respectively. NT-proBNP values were 1,286 (baseline), 3,053 (during a pAF episode), 576, and 681 pg/mL at 4, 7, and 12 months. High-sensitivity troponin T levels remained comparable to those during agalsidase alfa therapy (range: 0.066-0.115 ng/mL), measuring 0.070, 0.074, 0.083, and 0.093 ng/mL after the switch. Alpha-galactosidase A activity was also maintained (3.62 pmol at baseline and 4.25 pmol at 7 months). Cardiac imaging showed an apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy pattern with marked right ventricular hypertrophy and LGE from the apex to the lateral wall. Although arrhythmia limited quantitative MRI assessment. He underwent catheter ablation for pAF. No overt heart failure progression occurred. Discussion: In this patient, lyso-Gb3, troponin T, and heart failure biomarkers remained stable. Despite limited quantitative MRI evaluation, the clinical course suggested maintained disease stability. Conclusion: Clinical stability was maintained after switching to migalastat in a patient with the GLA L300P variant, supporting genotype-based therapeutic selection.

en: Identification of a Novel NKX2-5 Variant in a Family with Atrial Septal Defect and Atrioventricular Conduction Disease
ja: 心房中隔欠損と房室伝導障害の家系における新規NKX2-5バリアントの同定
abs: Background: NKX2-5 encodes a cardiac transcription factor involved in cardiac septation and atrioventricular conduction. Heterozygous variants are associated with autosomal dominant familial atrial septal defect (ASD), often with progressive atrioventricular block (AVB), variable expressivity, and incomplete penetrance. Case: A 9-year-old girl was diagnosed with multiple ASDs at 5 years and underwent transcatheter ASD closure at 9 years. Because her father had cardiac disease and second-degree AVB and two siblings also had ASD, genetic testing was performed. A heterozygous NKX2-5 variant, NM_004387.4:c.565C>T (p.Arg189Trp), was identified. Holter monitoring revealed transient Wenckebach-type second-degree AVB. Her father had electrocardiographic abnormalities from adolescence, progressive aortic regurgitation with Wenckebach-type AVB, and underwent aortic valve replacement following infective endocarditis at 26 years. Her brother underwent surgical ASD closure at 7 years. Her sister had suspected right ventricular hypoplasia and left ventricular noncompaction prenatally and underwent transcatheter closure of multiple ASDs at 6 years. Conclusion: A novel heterozygous NKX2-5 variant was identified in a family with ASD and progressive AV conduction disease. Although full familial segregation analysis has not yet been completed, the highly concordant familial phenotype supported likely pathogenicity. This case highlights the importance of genetic evaluation in familial ASD for anticipatory surveillance of progressive conduction disease and long-term family management.

en: Exploration of a Rare-Variant Burden Signal Associated with Apical Aneurysm in Apical Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
ja: 心尖部肥大型心筋症の心尖部瘤に関連するレアバリアント負荷シグナルの探索
abs: Introduction Apical aneurysm is major complications of apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (ApHCM). It remains unclear whether the formation of apical aneurysm is caused by hemodynamic factors associated with apical hypertrophy or by a strong burden of rare genetic variants. Methods We studied 72 patients with ApHCM who underwent whole-exome sequencing (WES). Variants were annotated using ANNOVAR and filtered with gnomAD and ToMMo 54KJPN database. Strict rare-damaging variants and moderately rare predicted-damaging variants defined as allele frequency and CADD phred score were evaluated. Analyses included core HCM genes, extended cardiomyopathy genes, and candidate remodeling pathways genes including microvascular, inflammatory, fibrosis and extracellular matrix genes. Associations with apical aneurysm were assessed using Fisher's exact test. Results During a median follow-up of 12 years, an apical aneurysm developed in 8 patients. Core HCM variants were observed in 3 of 8 aneurysm cases and 12 of 64 non-aneurysm cases, without a significant association (odds ratio (OR), 2.60; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.54-12.41; P=0.35). Both extended cardiomyopathy genes and candidate remodeling pathways genes were not enriched in aneurysm cases. Under the both strict rare-damaging definition and moderately rare predicted-damaging definition, no significant associations were detected (OR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.14-3.96; P=1.00, OR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.14-2.62; P=0.70, respectively). Conclusion WES did not identify a strong rare-variant burden signal associated with apical aneurysm in ApHCM.

en: Genomic Sequencing Using FFPE-Derived DNA: Feasibility and Limitations in Variant Validation
ja: FFPE由来DNAを用いたゲノムシーケンス：バリアント検証における実現可能性と限界
abs: Genomic DNA extracted from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissues is usually fragmented, making sequencing challenging. Here, we report our experience with sequencing using FFPE samples. We received FFPE samples of liver or left ventricular myocardium from 6 patients obtained at autopsy in different hospitals. Genomic DNA was extracted using Agencourt FormaPure XL, and the quality of DNA was assessed with a TapeStation 4200 system. The median DNA Integrity Number (DIN) was 1.55 (1.4-1.7). In three cases, DNA fragments more than 250 bp were selected using BluePippin, followed by HaloPlex HS library preparation and sequencing on MiSeq. In the other three cases, libraries were prepared using SureSelect and sequenced on NextSeq. Short-read sequencing data were obtained in all cases, and variants potentially related to cardiac disease were detected in 5 cases. We performed Sanger sequencing for the validation of detected variants, however, we could not obtain PCR products in two cases with DIN values of 1.4. Even after repairing the DNA by NEBNext FFPE DNA repair and designing PCR amplicons less than 100 bp, the target regions could not be amplified. In contrast, PCR products could be obtained from a DNA with a DIN value of 1.3. These findings indicate that short-read sequencing is feasible even with highly fragmented FFPE-derived DNA, whereas Sanger sequencing remains challenging in samples with severely degraded DNA. We further need to optimize sequencing methods for FFPE-derived DNA.

en: Functional Validation of a MYH11 Splice-Site Variant by Minigene Assay in a Family with HTAAD
ja: HTAAD家系におけるMYH11スプライス部位バリアントのミニジーンアッセイによる機能検証
abs: Introduction Interpretation of splice-site variants can be challenging. We report a family with heritable thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection (HTAAD) in which a minigene assay clarified the pathogenicity of a MYH11 splice-site variant. Case The proband was a woman in her late 30s with short stature who developed acute aortic dissection. Family history revealed fatal aortic dissections in her mother, maternal uncle, and cousin. The cousin had tall stature, scoliosis, strabismus, and patent ductus arteriosus. He died from extensive aortic dissection in his late 30s. No molecular diagnosis had previously been established in the family. Genetic Analysis Genetic testing identified a heterozygous canonical splice donor variant in MYH11 (NM_002474.3:c.3963+1G>T). In silico analyses predicted either cryptic donor activation causing a frameshift with NMD or in-frame exon skipping. Because MYH11 haploinsufficiency is not an established mechanism of autosomal dominant HTAAD, pathogenicity remained uncertain. A minigene assay demonstrated predominant exon skipping without cryptic donor activation. The resulting in-frame transcript was predicted to encode an abnormal MYH11 protein with a dominant-negative effect, consistent with the known disease mechanism of MYH11-associated HTAAD. Conclusion The minigene assay demonstrated exon skipping as the primary consequence of the MYH11 splice-site variant and supported its pathogenicity. These findings highlight the value of functional assays for interpreting splice-site variants when computational predictions are inconclusive.

en: Association study of HLA-B in ANCA-associated vasculitis in a Japanese population
ja: 日本人集団のANCA関連血管炎におけるHLA-Bの関連研究
abs: Background: ANCA-associated vasculitis is classified into subtypes according to clinical features and ANCA specificity. In Japan, microscopic polyangiitis (MPA) and MPO-ANCA-positive vasculitis (MPO-AAV) are predominant. The HLA-DRB1*09:01 haplotype is associated with MPA and MPO-AAV in East Asian populations. In contrast, the contribution of HLA class I genes to AAV remains unclear. We previously reported an association of HLA-B*51:01-C*14:02 haplotype with MPA and MPO-AAV in a Japanese population. In this study, we re-examined the association of HLA-B with AAV using an independent sample set. Methods: 94 MPA and 147 MPO-AAV were included in the analysis. HLA-B alleles of the patients were determined using Sanger sequencing. HLA-B allele frequency data from 60KJPN, derived from the Japanese Multi Omics Reference Panel, were used as controls. Results: Previously reported association of HLA-B*51:01 with MPA and MPO-AAV was not replicated. We next tested the association with HLA-B*27:04, the established strong risk allele for spondyloarthritis in East Asian populations and also showed a tendency toward increased frequency in MPO-AAV in our previous study. In the present sample set, B*27:04 was nominally increased in MPO-AAV (P=0.020, Pc=0.082, odds ratio 5.32, 95% confidence interval: 1.69-16.7), although the significance disappeared after correction for multiple testing. Conclusion: Because of the rarity of both HLA-B*27:04 and MPO-AAV in the Japanese population, this association has not been explored thus far. This study warranted further studies using a larger sample size.

en: Marked Regional Variation in APOE ε4 Frequency Among Patients with Alzheimer,s Disease
ja: アルツハイマー病患者におけるAPOE ε4頻度の著明な地域差
abs: Objective: APOE ε4 is a known risk factor for the onset of Alzheimer,s disease (AD) and for amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) associated with anti-amyloid antibody therapy. In addition, regional differences in APOE genotype frequencies have been reported. In this study, we investigated the distribution of APOE genotypes among patients with AD in Tokushima Prefecture. Methods: We enrolled 139 patients who visited our department for evaluation of eligibility for anti-amyloid antibody therapy. AD was diagnosed based on the NIA-AA criteria. APOE genotypes were analyzed using Sanger sequencing. Genotype frequencies were subsequently calculated and compared with those reported in a previous study. Results: APOE genotype frequencies were as follows: ε4/ε4 in 11 patients (7.9%), ε3/ε4 in 68 (48.9%), ε2/ε4 in 5 (3.6%), ε3/ε3 in 49 (35.3%), ε2/ε3 in 6 (4.3%), andε2/ε2 in 0 (0%). The proportion of ε4 carriers was 60.4% (84/139). A previous large-cohort study of Japanese patients with AD reported an ε4 carrier frequency of 44.3% (2,775/6,261), which was lower than that observed in patients with AD in Tokushima Prefecture. Conclusion: The present Tokushima cohort showed a higher proportion of APOE ε4 carriers compared with previously reported Japanese patients with AD. Further studies are warranted to clarify the factors underlying the high frequency of APOE ε4 carriers, including regional variation in APOE frequencies in Japan and genetic variants within APOE locus associated with AD risk.

en: Genome-wide scan identifies candidate loci associated with smoking quantity in patients undergoing cancer pain treatment
ja: がん疼痛治療中患者の喫煙量に関連する候補座位のゲノムワイド探索
abs: Purpose: Smoking behavior is influenced by complex genetic and environmental factors, but its polygenic basis in Japanese populations remains unclear. This study aimed to identify genetic variants associated with cigarette consumption per day (CPD) in Japanese cancer patients receiving palliative care. Methods: Genome-wide association analyses were performed using genomic DNA and clinical data from 429 Japanese cancer patients. Approximately 650,000 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were genotyped using the Infinium Asian Screening Array. After quality control, associations between SNPs and CPD were analyzed using qualitative (CPD =<20 vs. >20) and quantitative [ln(1+CPD)] phenotypes. Trend tests and linear regression analyses with false discovery rate correction were applied. Results: Multiple candidate SNPs associated with CPD were identified, including loci on chromosomes 7, 5, 4, and 2. Several variants reached genome-wide significance after multiple-testing correction. Some SNPs were located within or near genes related to neural and behavioral functions, including DMD, LHFPL2, and LINC01317. Conclusions: These findings suggest that smoking behavior is regulated by a complex polygenic architecture involving neural and behavioral pathways. The identified variants may contribute to individual differences in smoking behavior and provide a basis for future personalized prevention strategies.

en: Risk-Reducing Surgery in BRCA1/2 Pathogenic Variant Carriers at a Regional Cancer Care Hospital
ja: 地域がん診療病院におけるBRCA1/2病的バリアント保持者のリスク低減手術
abs: Background: BRCA1/2 pathogenic variants (PVs) affect treatment selection, surgical planning, and long-term risk management, including risk-reducing mastectomy (RRM) and salpingo-oophorectomy (RRSO). We evaluated the status and challenges of risk-reducing surgery for BRCA1/2 PV carriers at a regional cancer care hospital. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 521 patients who underwent BRCA1/2 testing at our institution between February 2019 and December 2025. Forty-two women with BRCA1/2 PVs were analyzed for clinical background, indication for testing, genetic counseling, cancer status, and uptake of RRM/RRSO. Results: BRCA1/2 PVs were detected in 42 patients (8.0%): 15 with BRCA1 and 27 with BRCA2 PVs. The mean age was 44.5±13.5 years, and five were unaffected carriers. Among breast cancer patients, 29 had unilateral disease, one synchronous bilateral disease, and six metachronous bilateral disease. Genetic counseling was provided to 38 patients. Testing was performed for HBOC management alone in 22 patients, companion diagnostics in 16, and both in 4. RRM was performed in 12 patients and RRSO in 15. In contrast, none of the five unaffected carriers wished to undergo either procedure. Conclusion: RRM and RRSO were implemented mainly in affected BRCA1/2 PV carriers, whereas unaffected carriers were reluctant to choose risk-reducing surgery. Cancer experience may influence risk perception and decision-making. As BRCA testing expands for companion diagnostics, integration of genetic counseling, cancer treatment, risk-reducing surgery, and family-centered care is essential.

en: De novo in-frame CREBBP variant identified in a patient with developmental delay and velopharyngeal incompetence
ja: 発達遅滞と鼻咽腔閉鎖不全を呈した患者で同定されたde novoインフレームCREBBPバリアント
abs: CREBBP is associated with Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome and Menke- Hennekam syndrome, both characterized by developmental delay, intellectual disability, and craniofacial abnormalities. Recently, we encountered a female patient with velopharyngeal incompetence, cleft palate, and developmental delay. Brain MRI and chromosomal microarray analysis revealed no significant abnormalities. She was registered to IRUD, and trio-based genomic analysis identified a de novo CREBBP in-frame deletion variant. Although this variant has not been previously reported, her phenotype was considered compatible with a CREBBP-related disorder, particularly overlapping with the Menke-Hennekam syndrome spectrum. Clinical features of this case will be discuss

en: GATA4 In-Frame Deletion in a Boy with Congenital Heart Defects, Differences of Sex Development, and Diaphragmatic Hernia
ja: 先天性心疾患・性分化疾患・横隔膜ヘルニアを呈した男児のGATA4インフレーム欠失
abs: Introduction: Monoallelic pathogenic variants of GATA4 have been implicated in congenital heart defects, 46,XY differences of sex development, and congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). However, there is no report of GATA4-variant positive patients who concomitantly exhibited these three features. Furthermore, the genotype-phenotype correlation of GATA4 abnormality remains unclear. Case presentation: The patient was a 2-year-old Japanese boy who was suspected of having CDH during gestation. At birth, he exhibited hypospadias, bifid scrotum, bilateral inguinal hernia, and CDH. Endocrine evaluations of the patient were indicative of partial testicular dysgenesis. Echocardiography showed mild pulmonary valve stenosis and multiple small atrial septal defects. Molecular analysis: Exome sequencing identified a de novo 3-bp deletion in GATA4 that has not been reported previously. The variant eliminated one amino acid from the highly conserved five-threonine repeat in the second zinc finger domain (c.829_831del, p.T277del). The variant was assessed as deleterious by in silico analyses and was scored as likely pathogenic by the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics guidelines. The 3D structure model predicted that the T277del variant causes a slight shift of the protein loop around the zinc-binding site. Discussion: Our findings indicate that the five-threonine repeat in the second zinc finger domain contributes to GATA4 function. These results broaden the spectrum of GATA4 pathogenic variants and highlight the phenotypic diversity resulting from GATA4 abnormalities.

en: Compound heterozygous VUSs in the KCNQ1 gene with clinical features suggestive of Jervell and Lange-Nielsen syndrome
ja: Jervell and Lange-Nielsen症候群を示唆する臨床像を伴うKCNQ1遺伝子複合ヘテロ接合VUS
abs: Background Jervell and Lange-Nielsen syndrome (JLNS) is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by congenital sensorineural hearing loss and QT prolongation. KCNQ1 and KCNE1 are known causative genes. We report a case presenting with clinically typical features of JLNS in which two variants of uncertain significance (VUSs) were identified in trans. Case presentation A 4-year-old boy with no family history presented with moderate bilateral sensorineural hearing loss since birth. His hearing deteriorated to severe loss by age 3, and he underwent cochlear implantation at age 4. He had been diagnosed with ADHD and was receiving Kampo medicine. He had a history of a syncopal episode in a swimming pool. Electrocardiography revealed marked QT prolongation (QTc: 544 ms), and he is currently under observation with beta-blocker therapy. Target panel sequencing of 158 hearing-loss-related genes identified compound heterozygous VUSs in the KCNQ1 gene. Discussion Target panel sequence revealed two heterozygous variants: (1) a splice site variant affecting exon 9 and (2) a missense variant in exon 10. Neither variant has been previously reported, and both were classified as VUS according to ClinGen Potassium Channel Arrhythmia VCEP specifications ((1) PP4; (2) PM2 and PP4). As the clinical features are consistent with JLNS, appropriate information should be provided through genetic counseling. Conclusion This case highlights the importance of integrating clinical features with genetic findings when providing genetic counseling, even when the identified variants are classified as VUSs.

en: Phenotype-Driven Interpretation of a Heterozygous CNV Involving the Autosomal Recessive Gene SLC12A6
ja: 常染色体潜性遺伝子SLC12A6を含むヘテロ接合CNVの表現型駆動型解釈
abs: Background: Heterozygous copy number variants (CNVs) involving autosomal recessive (AR) disease genes are occasionally detected by chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA). Although such findings may represent carrier status alone, additional analysis of the second allele can establish a definitive diagnosis when the phenotype is consistent with the associated disorder. Case: The patient was a 3-year-old child with global developmental delay, generalized hypotonia, hypoplasia of the corpus callosum, and horizontal nystagmus. CMA identified a 2.3 Mb heterozygous deletion at 15q14 involving SLC12A6, the causative gene for agenesis of the corpus callosum with peripheral neuropathy (Andermann syndrome). Considering the clinical overlap with Andermann syndrome and other possible genetic causes, whole exome sequencing was performed as the next diagnostic step. This identified a frameshift variant in SLC12A6 (c.2635del), predicted to cause loss of function. A diagnosis of Andermann syndrome due to biallelic SLC12A6 loss-of-function variants was established. Discussion: In this case, interpretation of the heterozygous CNV involving SLC12A6 in the context of the phenotype led to further genetic evaluation and ultimately the diagnosis. Heterozygous CNVs involving AR disease genes may represent carrier status alone. However, when clinical features overlap with the affected gene-associated disorder, additional sequencing may identify pathogenic variants on the second allele. These findings highlight the importance of phenotype-driven interpretation of heterozygous CNVs.

en: Can MDCT (multidetector-row CT) Be an Alternative to Breast MRI Surveillance?
ja: MDCT（多列検出器CT）は乳房MRIサーベイランスの代替となりうるか
abs: Background: Annual contrast-enhanced breast MRI and mammography are currently recommended for breast surveillance in HBOC. However, MDCT is also useful for detecting incidental breast lesions and evaluating tumor extent. We evaluated the potential role of MDCT in breast surveillance by comparing CT, MRI, and pathological findings. Methods: We analyzed 108 breast cancer lesions in 105 patients who underwent breast-conserving surgery without neoadjuvant chemotherapy between January and December 2025. All patients underwent contrast-enhanced MDCT using a 320-row detector scanner with 0.5-mm slice reconstruction, while MRI was additionally performed in 33 selected cases. Lesions difficult to detect on CT and/or MRI were clinicopathologically analyzed. Results: MDCT detected 104 of 108 lesions (96.4%). Three lesions were difficult to detect on both CT and MRI, while one lesion was difficult to detect only on CT. The latter was a DCIS lesion with sparse amorphous calcifications. Among 16 DCIS lesions, only this lesion was difficult to visualize on CT. Discussion: The sensitivity of MDCT was comparable to previously reported MRI sensitivity. Although CT is not suitable for unaffected HBOC carriers because of radiation exposure, MDCT may have potential utility in postoperative surveillance of HBOC survivors. Institutional validation of imaging protocols is necessary. Conclusion: MDCT showed breast cancer detection sensitivity nearly equivalent to MRI. With appropriate attention to radiation exposure and quality control, MDCT may be applicable to HBOC breast surveillance.

en: The role of clinical geneticists in recommending genetic counseling for patients with MSI-H/ dMMR colorectal cancer
ja: MSI-H/dMMR大腸がん患者への遺伝カウンセリング推奨における臨床遺伝専門医の役割
abs: [Background] Although Microsatellite instability (MSI) and mismatch repair (MMR) gene testing using resected or biopsied specimens are performed in colorectal cancer (CRC) both to assist in selecting therapeutic agents and to screen novel Lynch syndrome (LS) cases, there are limited reports on the role of clinical geneticists (CGs) in explanation and referral of genetic counseling (GC) in real-world clinical practice. [Purpose] To clarify the difference in explanation and referral of GC rate and gene testing (GT) uptake rate between CG and non-CG surgeons. [Methods] After retrospectively identifying GC candidates who underwent MSI/ MMR testing from January 2021 to March 2025 in our hospital, the rates of GC explanation, GC referral, and GT uptake were investigated. [Results] A total of 25 (4.5%) MSI- H/dMMR patients without BRAF mutation (20 MSI-H and five dMMR) were identified in 555 CRC patients who underwent MSI/ MMR testing. Excluding eight patients aged 70 or older, with no family history of cancer or no history of multiple/synchronous cancers, 17 patients were candidates for GC. The GC explanation rate (100% [9/9] vs 50% [4/8]) and GC referral rate (89% [8/9] vs 38% [3/8]) were significantly different between CG and non-CG doctors (p= 0.029, 0.046), although genetic testing rate (67% [6/9] vs 25% [2/8]) was statistically not significant (p=0.109). [Conclusion] CG showed significant role in GC explaining and GC referral. Increasing the number of CGs and supporting non-CGs in the management of MSI- H/dMMRs is necessary to maximize the MSI/ MMR testing.

en: Chromosomal microarray diagnosis of Smith-Magenis syndrome in an ELBW infant with hyperacusis and estropia
ja: 聴覚過敏と内斜視を伴う超低出生体重児のSmith-Magenis症候群の染色体マイクロアレイ診断
abs: Background: Smith-Magenis syndrome (SMS) is a rare genetic disorder caused by a 17p11.2 microdeletion or RAI1 variants. It is characterized by developmental delay, sleep disturbance, behavioral abnormalities, and sensory hypersensitivity. Diagnosis may be delayed in early childhood because characteristic phenotypes can be subtle, particularly in preterm infants whose developmental delay is often attributed to prematurity. We report a case of SMS diagnosed by chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA) in an extremely low birth weight (ELBW) infant. Case: The patient was a 3-year-old girl born at 28 weeks and 3 days of gestation by emergency cesarean section due to fetal distress, with a birth weight of 908 g. Her neonatal respiratory and nutritional course was typical for an ELBW infant, although she required surgery for choledocholithiasis with suspected biliary perforation. Developmental delay became evident. Her developmental quotient (DQ) on the Kyoto Scale declined from 49 at 18 months (corrected age 46) to 31 at 3 years (corrected age 33). Hyperacusis and esotropia became prominent between 2 and 3 years, findings difficult to attribute solely to prematurity. CMA identified a 4.2-Mb microdeletion at 17p11.2 (arr[GRCh37]17p11.2(16,637,902_20,839,138)x1), confirming SMS. Discussion: In preterm infants, developmental delay may be attributed to prematurity, resulting in diagnostic overshadowing. This case highlights that phenotypic clues, such as progressive delay, sensory hypersensitivity, and strabismus, should prompt genetic evaluation even in ELBW infants.

en: A case of Peutz Jeghers syndrome suggestive of mosaic whole-gene deletion of the STK11 gene
ja: STK11遺伝子全欠失モザイクが示唆されたPeutz-Jeghers症候群の1例
abs: Background Peutz-Jeghers syndrome (PJS) is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by pathogenic variants in STK11 and characterized by hamartomatous gastrointestinal polyps and mucocutaneous pigmentation. We report a case of PJS with mosaic whole-gene deletion of STK11 suspected by NGS-based CNV analysis and confirmed by MLPA. Case A 15-year-old man presented with progressive pigmented macules on the lips and fingers. Endoscopy revealed multiple polyps in the stomach, small intestine, and colon, leading to a clinical diagnosis of PJS. No relevant family history was identified. Targeted sequencing using peripheral blood-derived DNA detected no pathogenic sequence variants in STK11. However, NGS-based CNV analysis suggested deletion of the entire STK11 coding region. MLPA showed reduced copy numbers across all STK11 probes, with probe signal ratios of 0.65-0.73 (mean, 0.69). Discussion This case illustrates that structural variants should be considered in clinically typical PJS when no pathogenic sequence variant is detected. MLPA supported mosaic whole-gene deletion of STK11. Given the typical PJS phenotype, guideline-based surveillance was recommended. Because gonosomal mosaicism was suspected, genetic counseling was provided regarding the uncertain risk of transmission to future offspring, with careful consideration of his young age. Conclusion NGS-based CNV analysis may help detect mosaic STK11 deletion in sequence-negative PJS. MLPA is useful for interpreting suspected CNV mosaicism and supports diagnosis, surveillance, and genetic counseling.

en: Clinical features of GBA1-related Parkinson's disease in Japanese patients
ja: 日本人患者におけるGBA1関連Parkinson病の臨床的特徴
abs: [Objective] Glucosylceramidase beta 1 (GBA1), the causative gene for Gaucher disease, is the most important risk gene associated with Parkinson's disease (PD). In this study, we aimed to screen GBA1 variants and elucidated the clinical features. [Methods] For 1,289 patients with PD and 163 patients with other neurodegenerative disorders (non-PD) whose GBA1 genotypes were determined, we compared 48 clinical symptoms between variant carriers and non-carriers, using chi-square tests or ANOVA. [Results] GBA1 variants were identified in 192 PD patients and 9 non-PD patients comprising 148 cases with severe variants, one case with a mild variant and 52 cases with variants of uncertain significance. The prevalence of GBA1 variant carriers in PD patients or non-PD patients was 14.9% and 5.5%, respectively. PD patients with GBA1 variants showed a younger age at onset, the rate of bradykinesia, rigidity, gait disturbance, and restless legs syndrome were higher than those in non-GBA1 carriers, whereas there was no difference in psychiatric symptoms other than hallucination. [Conclusions] Severe GBA1 variants constitute most of variant-positive PD cases in Japanese individuals, indicating a distinct variant spectrum compared with other ethnic groups. Despite showing a younger age at onset, these patients exhibit notably homogeneous and typical PD phenotypes, clinical features similar to those reported for GBA1-related PD. We emphasize the need to consider ethnic differences in variant distribution when interpreting the clinical implications of GBA1 variants as a risk gene for PD.

en: Fertility Preservation During Breast Cancer Treatment in Cowden Syndrome: Live Birth Despite Metachronous Cancers
ja: Cowden症候群の乳がん治療中の妊孕性温存：異時性がんを経ての生児獲得
abs: Background Cowden syndrome (CS) is an autosomal dominant disorder with hamartomatous lesions and elevated cancer risks. We report a CS patient with metachronous cancers achieving live birth through fertility-preserving multidisciplinary treatment. Case A 31-year-old with juvenile multiple papillomatosis (age 16), lipoma/hemangioma resection (22), and subclavian AVM embolization (31) was referred for genetic counseling. A pathogenic PTEN variant (c.37A>T, p. Lys13Ter, heterozygous) confirmed CS. Surveillance detected left breast cancer at 32; mastectomy yielded pT3N2aM0 StageIIIA (HR+/HER2-). Embryo cryopreservation preceded adjuvant chemotherapy and radiotherapy. Tamoxifen/LHRH agonist began at 34; abnormal bleeding at 35 revealed atypical endometrial hyperplasia. Tamoxifen was switched to letrozole; curettage during MPA confirmed endometrial cancer G1; subsequent curettage confirmed no residual disease. Treatment suspended at 36 for embryo transfer; pregnancy achieved at 37. Breast cancer treatment resumed at 39 with definitive endometrial surgery. No recurrence. Discussion CS diagnosis enabled breast cancer detection. Endometrial cancer during tamoxifen may reflect combined PTEN-related and drug-related risks. Multidisciplinary conferences guided stepwise decisions. PGT-M could be offered as an option for young patients with hereditary tumor syndromes. Conclusion Stepwise multidisciplinary fertility-preserving treatment enabled both standard therapy completion and live birth in CS-associated metachronous cancers.

en: A suspected Androgenetic/Biparental Mosaic/Chimeric Conception (ABMC) with discordant p57KIP2 immunostaining
ja: p57KIP2免疫染色の不一致を伴う雄核発生/両親性モザイク/キメラ受胎（ABMC）疑い例
abs: [Introduction] Early pregnancy loss with hydropic villi is difficult to classify, when molar and biparental components coexist. Loss of p57KIP2 suggests absent maternal CDKN1C expression and supports a complete molar component. We report a suspected ABMC in which p57KIP2 staining guided gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) risk management. [Case] A 33-year-old primigravida underwent evacuation for missed abortion at 8 weeks' gestation. Initial pathology was abortion (mole-negative). Because hCG did not decline appropriately, repeat evacuation was performed. Hydropic villi showed divergent p57KIP2 expression: p57-negative cytotrophoblasts and stromal cells, p57-positive villi suggesting biparental origin, and villi with mixed staining. Review of the first specimen also showed mixed villous populations with divergent p57KIP2 staining. These findings suggested mixed androgenetic and biparental/chimeric lineages and suspected ABMC. STR genotyping and FISH were not performed; ploidy and parental chromosomal contributions were unconfirmed. hCG later increased, leading to low-risk GTN (score 0). [Discussion] ABMC may arise from postzygotic mosaicism or zygote fusion. When an androgenetic complete molar component is present, accurate classification is important for hCG surveillance. p57KIP2 staining can identify divergent villous populations and select cases for molecular genotyping. [Conclusion] Divergent p57KIP2 staining suggest ABMC rather than a conventional mole. This case highlights the need for accurate classification and strict hCG surveillance.

en: Failure to thrive associated with recurrent aspiration pneumonia in a patient with Baraitser-Winter syndrome.
ja: Baraitser-Winter症候群患者における反復性誤嚥性肺炎に伴う体重増加不良
abs: We report a case of an infant with a moderate phenotype of Baraitser- Winter cerebrofrontofacial syndrome (BWCFF; OMIM #243310) who presented with recurrent asthmatic bronchitis and poor weight gain due to gastroesophageal reflux. The girl presented with characteristic craniofacial features, patent ductus arteriosus, and chylothorax at birth. There was no significant family history. At 3 months of age, she developed acute bronchiolitis requiring mechanical ventilation. Brain MRI revealed subependymal heterotopic gray matter. Although extubation was achieved one month later, generalized hypotonia and delayed gross motor development became evident. Thereafter, she repeatedly developed asthmatic bronchitis resulting in hospitalizations. Poor weight gain persisted, and enteral nutrition via a duodenal tube was initiated at 6 months of age. Following nutritional intervention, the frequency of bronchitis decreased and weight gain improved. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) performed through the Initiative on Rare and Undiagnosed Diseases (IRUD) identified a heterozygous missense variant [NM_001101.5:c217C>G (p.His73Asp)] in the ACTB gene. The same variant has previously been reported in individuals with relatively mild phenotypes, including acquisition of cruising at 10 months and independent walking at 24 months. In contrast, our patient showed marked hypotonia and had only recently begun cruising at over 2 years of age. This case suggests that even patients harboring the same ACTB variant may exhibit substantial variability in the severity of hypotonia and respiratory complications.

en: A case of infantile epileptic spasms syndrome and neurodevelopmental disorder with a homozygous DNAJA3 variant
ja: ホモ接合DNAJA3バリアントを有する乳児てんかん性スパズム症候群・神経発達症の1例
abs: We report a 13-year-old Japanese girl with epilepsy, neurodevelopmental delay, and intellectual disability who carries a homozygous variant in DNAJA3. DNAJA3 encodes a co-chaperone protein that interacts with mitochondrial Hsp70 to maintain protein homeostasis and is involved in the regulation of mitochondrial dynamics and neuronal survival. Previously reported patients with homozygous or compound heterozygous DNAJA3 variants (n = 3) presented with peripheral neuropathy, ophthalmological abnormalities, intellectual disability, neurodegeneration, and epilepsy. Some patients also exhibited brain MRI abnormalities, including basal ganglia involvement. In contrast, our patient initially presented with focal epilepsy and subsequently developed infantile epileptic spasms syndrome. She showed no clinical evidence of peripheral neuropathy or ophthalmological abnormalities. Brain MRI demonstrated progressive bilateral cerebral hemispheric atrophy. Exome sequencing identified a homozygous missense variant, NM_005147.6:c.283T>C, p.(Tyr95His), inherited from her unaffected heterozygous parents. According to the ACMG/AMP guidelines, this variant was classified as a variant of uncertain significance (VUS). This case may expand the phenotypic spectrum of DNAJA3-related disorders.

en: Hospital-Based Peer Support and Educational Meeting for Rare Genetic Diseases: Utility and Evolving Participant Needs.
ja: 希少遺伝性疾患の病院ベースのピアサポート・教育会：有用性と参加者ニーズの変化
abs: Background: In the care of rare genetic disorders, peer support among patients and families is an important complement to medical information provision. This study evaluated participant needs, satisfaction, and challenges. Methods: Pre- and post-questionnaires were administered to participants of peer support and educational meetings for Kabuki syndrome, Sotos syndrome, DYRK1A syndrome in 2025. Pre-questionnaires assessed expectations and needs; post-questionnaires assessed satisfaction and perceived outcomes. Data from previous meetings were also reviewed. Results: The most common need was learning about the disease and developmental support (40%), followed by hearing from older patients (36%). Satisfaction was high for both lectures and peer sessions. Preferred timing was most often at diagnosis (52.8%), followed by "at all times" (36.1%), suggesting a need for early and continuous peer support.
