Participants reported improved future outlook and reassurance after participation. Interest in up-to-date medical information and researched compared with past data. Limited discussion time and environmental issues were noted. Conclusion: This program provided informational and peer support. The need for peer support increased after diagnosis and tended to persist. Participant needs may extend beyond psychological support to include access to up-to-date information, highlighting the importance of adapting program operations.

en: Diagnostic Yield of Whole-Exome Sequencing in Fetuses with Unexplained Structural Anomalies
ja: 原因不明の構造異常を有する胎児における全エクソーム解析の診断率
abs: Objective: To investigate the diagnostic yield of whole-exome sequencing (WES) in fetuses with structural anomalies of unknown etiology. Methods: We analyzed 29 fetuses with structural anomalies identified by fetal ultrasound at our institution between 2015 and 2025. All cases remained undiagnosed after conventional genetic testing, including chromosomal analysis or chromosomal microarray. We extracted fetal and/or parental DNA after delivery and performed WES. Twenty-five of 29 patients underwent a trio analysis. We conducted this study with the participants consent institutional ethics committee approval. Results: We identified pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in 10 of the 29 cases (34.5 %) with detected genes comprising BICD2 (n=2), TFAP2A, SLC26A2, COL1A1, COL2A1, FLT4, MTM1, GLI3, and GNB1 (n=1 each). We identified four novel variants: TFAP2A, COL2A1, BICD2, and GLI3. The inheritance patterns included autosomal dominant (n=8), autosomal recessive (n=1), and X-linked disorders (n=1). We classified the diagnosed disorders as neuromuscular disorders (n=4), skeletal dysplasia (n=3), syndromic disorders (n=2), or lymphatic diseases (n=1). The diagnostic yield was higher in fetuses with multisystem than in those with isolated anomalies (i.e., 42.9 % [9/21] vs. 12.5 % [1/8]). Conclusions: WES retained a substantial diagnostic yield in fetuses with structural anomalies, particularly in those with multisystem anomalies. We commonly identified skeletal and neuromuscular disorders, highlighting the importance of detailed fetal phenotyping combined with genomic analysis.

en: Current Status of Genetic Panel Analysis for Intractable Rare Disorders at Tokyo Women's Medical University Hospital
ja: 東京女子医科大学病院における難治性希少疾患の遺伝子パネル解析の現状
abs: Introduction: Genetic panel analysis for intractable rare disorders has been covered by health insurance in Japan and has been performed in 63 cases at Tokyo Women's Medical University Hospital. We reviewed these cases to evaluate the diagnostic yield at our institution. Methods and Results: The analyzed cases were as follows: 20 using an intellectual disability panel, 17 for muscle weakness, 13 for proteinuria, 10 for cardiomyopathy, 2 for recurrent fever, and 1 for intractable epilepsy. Only one case (COL4A5 in the proteinuria group) was diagnosed using the insurance-covered gene panel alone. The remaining cases underwent additional analysis using FASTQ files obtained from the testing laboratory. Genomic analysis was performed using our in-house pipeline, and disease-causing variants were identified in 26 cases (41%), including one mitochondrial gene abnormality. Family analysis was required to confirm the diagnosis in 7 cases. In one undiagnosed case, whole-genome long-read sequencing identified a structural variant responsible for the disease. Conclusion: Since genetic panel analysis for intractable rare disorders covered by health insurance is typically performed using singleton sequencing, there are cases where parental samples are required to narrow down candidate variants and support variant curation. In some cases, a diagnosis could not be reached because parental samples were unavailable. There are limitations to singleton analysis covered by health insurance, and it is desirable that analysis of relatives also be covered by insurance.

en: A Japanese infant with chronic anemia harboring a novel pathogenic variant affecting the same residue as G6PD Ierapetra
ja: G6PD Ierapetraと同一残基に影響する新規病的バリアントを有する慢性貧血の日本人乳児
abs: Background: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency is the most common red blood cell (RBC) enzymopathy worldwide. While many common polymorphic variants have been well characterized, rare variants remain incompletely understood. G6PD Ierapetra (p.P353S) is a rare pathogenic variant originally reported in Greek patients. We report a Japanese infant harboring a novel variant affecting the same residue as G6PD Ierapetra. Case: The male proband was the second child of healthy, non-consanguineous Japanese parents. He was born at term, appropriate for gestational age. He developed severe hemolytic anemia during neonatal period, requiring phototherapy from postnatal days 2-6. The hemoglobin level subsequently declined to 6.7 g/dL, necessitating RBC transfusion on day 10. Direct and indirect Coombs tests were negative, and blood smear showed marked aniso-poikilocytosis. He continued to exhibit moderate hemolytic anemia and experienced an acute hemolytic crisis triggered by an infection at 11 months of age, which required RBC transfusion. To explore diagnosis, we performed a target-captured sequencing containing 68 hemolytic anemia-related genes, and it revealed a novel pathogenic variant G6PD p.P353H. It affects the same residue as Ierapetra but causes a Histidine for Proline amino acid replacement. Subsequent G6PD assay revealed the activity was 4% of normal. Conclusion: The clinical phenotype, including chronic non-spherocytic hemolytic anemia, supports provisional classification of this novel variant as a Class A variant according to the current WHO classification.

en: A case of TAF4 related intellectual developmental disorder with Cornelia de Lange syndrome-like facies
ja: Cornelia de Lange症候群様顔貌を呈したTAF4関連知的発達症の1例
abs: Introduction TAF4-related autosomal dominant intellectual developmental disorder-73 (MRD73; MIM #620450) is a variable neurodevelopmental condition characterized by delayed speech, behavioral abnormalities, and mild-to-severe intellectual disability. Since its delineation in 2022, clinical data on MRD73 have remained scarce due to the limited number of identified cases. A distinct common gestalt remains unestablished. Case Report The patient, the third child of non-consanguineous parents, was born at 40 weeks of gestation with a birth weight of 2,685 g. Clinical examination revealed dysmorphic facial features reminiscent of Cornelia de Lange syndrome, including arched eyebrows, synophrys, and low-set ears. Developmental milestones were delayed; independent walking and two-word speech at 32 months. Transient tactile hypersensitivity of the extremities resolved by 29 months, coinciding with the onset of selective mutism. Self-injurious behaviors emerged at age 8. At 9 years and 10 months, the WISC-V revealed a Full-Scale IQ of 64, with prominent deficits in verbal comprehension and fluid reasoning. IRUD and Whole-genome sequencing analysis project in Japan revealed a de novo heterozygous TAF4 deletion encompassing introns 1-11. Discussion Further case accumulation is essential to delineate the characteristic facial gestalt of MRD73. Moreover, characterizing the distinct behavioral phenotype observed in this patient, including selective mutism and self-injurious behaviors, will help expand and better define the clinical spectrum of this rare disorder.

en: Early Genetic Diagnosis Enabling Pre-symptomatic Intervention in an Extremely Preterm Infant with Menkes Disease
ja: Menkes病の超早産児における早期遺伝学的診断による発症前介入
abs: Introduction: Menkes disease is an X-linked disorder of copper metabolism caused by ATP7A variants. Early copper-histidine therapy improves neurological outcomes, but early diagnosis in extremely preterm infants remains challenging. We report a case of Menkes disease diagnosed shortly after birth through coordinated perinatal management. Case Presentation: A 35-year-old gravida 2 para 1 woman was known to be a carrier of Menkes disease after her first child was diagnosed with an ATP7A pathogenic variant. The pregnancy was achieved by in vitro fertilization, although the family did not request preimplantation genetic testing. During pregnancy, multidisciplinary conferences involving perinatal and genetics specialists were conducted before delivery. Fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios developed during the second trimester, and emergency cesarean section was performed at 26 weeks of gestation because of nonreassuring fetal status. A 614 g (-2.2 SD) male infant was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit. Genetic testing using umbilical cord blood identified the familial ATP7A pathogenic variant, and Menkes disease was diagnosed on day 7 of life. Copper-histidine therapy was initiated thereafter. Brain MRI at 2 months of corrected age demonstrated normal myelination for age, and no seizures have been observed. Conclusion: We report early genetic diagnosis and therapeutic intervention for Menkes disease in an extremely preterm infant. Rapid genetic diagnosis may facilitate timely treatment when biochemical evaluation is difficult in preterm infants.

en: ATP7B Variants and Structural Variant Analysis in Ecuadorian Wilson's Disease
ja: エクアドルのWilson病におけるATP7Bバリアントと構造多型解析
abs: Wilson disease (WD) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by variants in the ATP7B gene. We recently analyzed a cohort of 10 Ecuadorian WD patients using whole-exome sequencing (WES) (JSHG 2025; Romero et al., Human Genomics 2026), and identified two recurrent ATP7B variants in 5 patients: c.2012_2013insAT p. (Met671Ilefs*) (Canar/Cuenca; 2 patients; absent from gnomAD, ClinVar, HGMD, and LOVD) and c.2052dupC p.(Met685*) (Guayaquil; 3 patients). Lildballe et al. (JHEP Reports 2026) reported that approximately 98% of WD cases are explained by ATP7B alone, and that structural variants (SVs) are important for cases unsolved by exome sequencing. Therefore, we investigated SVs in patients whose disease cause was not identified by WES. In 1 patient, no ATP7B coding variants were detected by WES, although RT-qPCR analysis showed approximately 9.8-fold reduced ATP7B expression. In the present study, we focused on this unsolved case. By reanalyzing the WES data, we found that 5 common benign ATP7B polymorphisms (gnomAD AF 0.47-0.58) appeared homozygous, despite the absence of genome-wide runs of homozygosity (ROH). This pattern strongly suggests a localized hemizygous deletion in the ATP7B region. To verify this hypothesis, we will perform targeted long-read sequencing on PromethION with adaptive sampling. These findings indicate that SV analysis is the next step for WD cases unresolved by short-read sequencing.

en: Importance of Prior Awareness for Obtaining Participation Consent in Biobanking: A Literature Review
ja: バイオバンク参加同意取得における事前認知の重要性：文献レビュー
abs: Background: Stable biobank operation requires consent from patients. Trust, clear consent, and understanding of social value are determinants, but prior awareness of biobanking may also lower barriers to participation. Objective: To review how prior awareness relates to willingness to participate and to identify outreach practices for the JIHS Biobank. Methods: We reviewed studies on determinants of biobank participation, focusing on prior awareness, and examined outreach practices of UK Biobank, All of Us, and Tohoku Medical Megabank, plus reviews on media campaigns and waiting-room information tools. Results: Knowledge of biobanks remains limited. Reviews identified knowledge, understanding of research aims, data-security concerns, consent models, and trust as factors associated with willingness to participate. Surveys from Latvia and Slovakia showed that awareness and trust were associated with willingness to participate. UK Biobank used local media and charities to improve awareness and response rates. All of Us worked with trusted organizations and influencers to engage diverse populations. Tohoku Medical bank used television commercials and explanatory videos. Reviews showed that media campaigns can improve awareness and screening uptake, and waiting-room audiovisual tools can improve patient knowledge and intentions. Discussion: Prior awareness may be an important pre-consent step. Conclusion: Outreach to increase prior awareness should be positioned as an independent strategy, alongside trust building, clear consent explanations, and communication of participation value.

en: Immune Reference Datasets for Transcriptome Analysis and Interpretation
ja: トランスクリプトーム解析・解釈のための免疫リファレンスデータセット
abs: [Background] Transcriptome analysis is widely used with various immune cell samples; however, interpreting complex immune and cellular states requires appropriate reference datasets and analytical environments. We are constructing the IMMAGINE database, which combines Immune Reference Datasets based on immune cell-derived transcriptomes with a viewer for browsing analysis results. [Methods] In this study, we are developing multiple reference datasets composed of immune cell subsets derived from PBMCs. In addition to steady-state fine immune cell subsets, we created immune cell datasets under various stimulation conditions, aiming to establish a framework that enables the interpretation of immune and cellular states. [Results] This dataset is intended to support the interpretation of transcriptomic data, including bulk RNA-seq, the analysis of changes in cellular states, and applications such as representation learning and pattern extraction for AI and modeling purposes. It is also expected to serve as a platform for validating computational methods using real-world data and for comparative analysis. [Conclusion] The IMMAGINE database is considered a useful platform for interpreting immune and cellular states in transcriptome analysis. Moving forward, we aim to build a cloud-based collaborative analysis environment and develop it into an analytical platform that supports both AI modeling and biological interpretation.

en: Building a Cohort-wide Genomic Resource through Array Genotyping and Imputation in the Tohoku Medical Megabank Project
ja: 東北メディカル・メガバンク計画におけるアレイジェノタイピングとインピュテーションによるコホート全体ゲノムリソースの構築
abs: Population-specific genomic resources are critical for the equitable implementation of precision medicine, yet large-scale integrated datasets remain limited for non-European populations. The Tohoku Medical Megabank (TMM) Project has established two population-based cohorts comprising about 157,000 participants to support genomic medicine and population health research in Japan. Here, we present the cohort-scale array-based genotyping and downstream analytical framework implemented in the TMM Project and describe the quality, characteristics, and availability of the resulting datasets. Genotyping was conducted using the Japonica Array platforms implemented in this project, JPAv2 and JPA NEO, followed by batch-level quality control and genotype imputation. Across genotyping batches, failure rates were consistently low, with no substantial batch-or platform-specific biases after sample quality control. Marker retention patterns reflected array design and sample source. Population structure analysis demonstrated that most participants clustered in East Asian reference populations, while relatedness inference captured both the family-based cohort design and additional relatedness arising from community-based recruitment. Genotype imputation showed stable performance across batches, with high accuracy for variants with minor allele frequency >1%. Together, these data establish a robust population-scale genomic infrastructure in Japan and, in combination with ongoing whole-genome sequencing initiatives, provide a foundation for integrative analyses of common and rare variation.

en: NanbyoData: A Japanese Rare Disease Portal with Ontology-Based Data Integration
ja: NanbyoData：オントロジーに基づくデータ統合を行う日本の希少疾患ポータル
abs: Information on rare diseases covered by the Japanese national healthcare system is distributed across multiple systems and databases, making cross-disease analysis and international utilization challenging. NanbyoData (https://nanbyodata.jp/epidemiology) is a web portal that integrates domestic and international data to promote global data sharing and utilization. It provides curated information for designated intractable diseases and pediatric chronic diseases, including disease classification, definitions, and associated genes. These disease concepts are systematically structured using the Nanbyo Disease Ontology (NANDO). Mappings between NANDO and the widely used Mondo Disease Ontology (Mondo) have been curated by Japanese clinical experts, with approximately 70% of diseases successfully mapped. These mappings enable linkage to international databases such as OMIM and Orphanet, allowing integrated access to disease-associated gene information. NanbyoData also provides standardized datasets, including 8,431 disease-associated genes, 1,080 glycan-related genes, 511 clinical genetic tests based on the list provided by the Japan Society of Human Genetics, 61,547 clinical phenotypes, and 32,591 rare disease-specific bioresources, along with genetic variant and literature information. In this presentation, we describe the data integration framework and key features of NanbyoData, and discuss future directions for data expansion and international collaboration.

en: BioBank Japan: Better Biological Resource Toward the Further Utilization of Samples and Data
ja: バイオバンク・ジャパン：試料・データのさらなる利活用に向けたより良い生物資源
abs: BioBank Japan (BBJ) was established in 2003 to advance personalized medicine using genetic information. Until now, BBJ collected DNA, serum, and clinical information of approximately 270,000 patients with 51 diseases (440,000 cases). Then, BBJ obtained genetic SNP data for almost all individual, increasing omics data of whole genome sequencing (WGS), metabolome and proteome analyses. These samples and data were utilized in many researchers from both academic institutions and companies, leading to a wealth of outstanding research findings. Recently, we began providing "Data Packages", which bundle clinical information, genomic information, metabolome data, and other information, to researchers. By these initiatives, the utilization of BBJ's samples and information, particularly the data, has increased significantly in recent years, contributing to the promotion of both large-scale studies and smaller-scale research. Furthermore, we have developed and partially launched a platform that enables two-way communication between research participants and BBJ. Through these new activities and the promotion of research utilization, we are contributing to drug discovery research, healthcare, and societal implementation. This report introduces the progress of these BBJ initiatives.

en: A multicentre study on craniofacial anomalies in orthodontic patients in Japan: diagnosis and insurance eligibility
ja: 日本の矯正歯科患者における頭蓋顔面異常の多施設研究：診断と保険適用
abs: Health-insurance coverage for orthodontic treatment in patients with congenital disorders has expanded in Japan; however, many conditions remain unrecognized. This study investigated the clinical characteristics and insurance eligibility for hereditary craniofacial anomalies in Japan. We included patients with congenital craniofacial anomalies (excluding nonsyndromic cleft lip and/or palate) who visited the Departments of Orthodontics at nine university hospitals up to December 2024. Disease names and insurance eligibility were collected using an electronic data-capture system. Among registered 1,224 patients (640 males and 584 females), 1,107 (90.4%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 88.6-92.0) were diagnosed with one of the 65 health insurance-covered disorders. The most frequent diagnoses were congenital absence of >6 teeth (343, 28.0%), followed by Down syndrome (102, 8.3%), craniofacial microsomia (67, 5.5%), craniosynostosis (53, 4.3%), and cleidocranial dysplasia (50, 4.1%). Among the 117 patients (9.6%; 95% CI, 8.0-11.4) with other disorders, 58 (4.7% of total cohort) were eligible for insurance coverage owing to symptoms overlapping those of the 65 designated disorders or diagnosis of cleft lip and/or palate or jaw deformities. The remaining 59 patients (4.8%; 95% CI, 3.7-6.2) were ineligible for coverage. Although most hereditary craniofacial anomalies are currently covered by health insurance, many rare conditions are excluded. Continued data collection and expansion of participating institutions are needed to establish a more comprehensive support system.

en: TogoVar data expansion: structural variants, JGA-derived variants, and splice-site creating variants
ja: TogoVarデータ拡充：構造多型・JGA由来バリアント・スプライス部位創出バリアント
abs: TogoVar is a variant database that integrates allele frequencies in the Japanese population from sources such as the Japanese Genotype-phenotype Archive (JGA) and the ToMMo allele frequency panel. Because individuals with Japanese ancestry are underrepresented in international databases such as gnomAD, TogoVar is an important resource for human genetics research in Japan. In addition to Japanese allele frequencies, TogoVar includes non-Japanese allele frequencies from gnomAD, annotations by the Ensembl Variant Effect Predictor (VEP), clinical significance data from ClinVar, Japanese population-derived clinical significance data from the Medical Genomics Japan Variant Database (MGeND), and literature data from LitVar and PubTator. In the latest release, TogoVar was expanded by adding structural variants, variants derived from JGA-deposited data, and splice-site creating variants. For structural variants of 51 bp or longer, TogoVar incorporated JoGo: Joint Open Genome and Omics Platform v1 (258 samples; 377,965 variants), JSV1: Japanese Structural Variation (222 samples; 72,342 variants), and gnomAD-SV v4.1 (63,046 samples; 1,931,561 variants). In addition, allele frequencies and genotype counts calculated from aggregate VCF datasets registered in JGA under JGAD000867 and JGAD000868 were added to TogoVar. These datasets were generated by variant calling of whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data from 1,026 and 1,964 BioBank Japan individuals, respectively. Furthermore, TogoVar variants matching 48,569 variants in SSCV DB v1.1 were annotated as splice-site creating variants (SSCVs).

en: Identifying risk factors for childhood obesity associated with genetic factors in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
ja: 妊娠高血圧症候群における遺伝要因に関連する小児肥満のリスク因子の同定
abs: Objective: Childhood obesity is a multifactorial disease caused by complex interactions between genetic and environmental factors and is strongly associated with obesity, hypertension, and diabetes in adulthood. Children born to mothers with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) are at increased risk of obesity later in life. However, the relationship between single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and childhood obesity in children born to mothers with HDP remains unclear. This study aimed to identify obesity-associated SNPs and related biological pathways in children born to mothers with HDP. Methods: Approximately 20,000 mother-child pairs enrolled in the Tohoku Medical Megabank Project Three-Generation Cohort Study were analyzed. Children were classified into normal-weight and obese groups according to BMI percentiles at ages 3 and 5 years. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) were performed in the obese groups, and SNPs with Manhattan plot scores more than 5 were selected for Gene Ontology and pathway analyses. Results: GWAS identified 43 SNPs associated with obesity at age 3 years and 21 SNPs associated with obesity at age 5 years. Pathway analyses revealed enrichment of pathways associated with leptin signaling, glucolipid metabolism, and insulin resistance. Conclusions: Children who develop obesity at an early age may carry obesity-associated SNPs. In particular, genetic variants identified in children born to mothers with HDP may help predict future obesity risk from birth.

en: PanelSearch Nanbyo for evidence-based curation of gene lists in designated intractable diseases
ja: 指定難病の遺伝子リストをエビデンスに基づきキュレーションするPanelSearch Nanbyo
abs: Multigene testing for designated intractable diseases is being implemented under public health insurance in Japan. Sustainable use requires knowledge bases, as exemplified by Genomics England PanelApp, that manage disease-specific gene lists together with evidence, expert evaluations, inclusion decisions, and change history. In Japan, notification numbers, diagnostic criteria, subtypes, and external identifiers are interrelated in complex ways, requiring a framework tailored to the national system. We developed NANDO, a disease vocabulary that organizes disease names, notification numbers, and subtypes in Japan's designated intractable disease system. We also developed PanelSearch Nanbyo, a NANDO-based platform for searching, reviewing, and curating evidence-linked gene lists. It maps diseases in NANDO to external identifiers and aggregates disease-gene associations from OMIM, MedGen, Orphadata, GenCC, and literature. The platform separates public resource-derived disease-gene associations from expert reviews and curator decisions. Database and literature-derived information is not treated as a final list; evaluations and inclusion decisions by clinical geneticists, disease specialists, and curators can be recorded. Users can trace each gene's rationale, review process, inclusion process, and change history. The platform manages disease-specific gene lists as updateable knowledge resources. By accumulating reviews and expanding curation workflows, it aims to improve reproducibility in gene-list development and support the collaborative maintenance of genomic testing resources.

en: Pentose phosphate pathway dysfunction and lipid peroxidation in inflammatory liver injury in Lars1 mutant mice
ja: Lars1変異マウスの炎症性肝障害におけるペントースリン酸経路の機能不全と脂質過酸化
abs: Background: Infantile liver failure syndrome type 1 (ILFS1), caused by pathogenic LARS1 variants, is characterized by recurrent liver dysfunction triggered by inflammatory stress. We previously generated Lars1-I451F knock-in mice harboring a pathogenic variant identified in ILFS1 patients. Transcriptomic analysis of lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated livers demonstrated suppression of hepatic metabolic pathways under inflammatory stress. Histological analyses also revealed aggravated hepatic steatosis and liver injury in mutant mice, but the specific metabolic alterations underlying liver injury remain unclear. Methods: Homozygous Lars1-I451F mice were challenged with LPS, and liver tissues were collected 24 hours later. Hepatic metabolomic analysis was performed to identify altered metabolic pathways. Pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) activity was evaluated using NADP+/NADPH assays. Lipid peroxidation was assessed by western blotting for 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal (4-HNE). Results: Metabolomic analysis identified suppression of the PPP in mutant livers after LPS stimulation. NADP+/NADPH assays demonstrated reduced PPP activity in mutant mice compared with controls. Western blot analysis revealed marked accumulation of 4- HNE in mutant livers, indicating enhanced lipid peroxidation and oxidative stress. Conclusions: These findings suggest that impaired PPP activity and disrupted redox homeostasis contribute to inflammatory stress-induced liver injury in Lars1-I451F mutant mice. Accumulation of 4-HNE may represent a pathogenic mechanism and potential therapeutic target in ILFS1.

en: EDA1 variants impair EDAR signaling in severe permanent tooth agenesis
ja: 重度永久歯欠損におけるEDA1バリアントによるEDARシグナル障害
abs: Ectodysplasin A (EDA) regulates ectodermal organ development through activation of its receptor EDAR. Pathogenic EDA variants are a major cause of X-linked hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia (XLHED), characterized by hypodontia, hypotrichosis, and hypohidrosis. However, the mechanisms by which missense variants impair EDA-EDAR signaling remain unclear. Here, we identified two EDA1 missense variants, p.Gln254Lys and p.Thr378Met, in individuals with XLHED. Both variants are located within the TNF homology domain responsible for EDAR binding. NF-κB luciferase reporter assays demonstrated complete loss of EDAR activation by both variants. Consistently, conditioned media containing either variant failed to bind EDAR-expressing HEK293 cells. Biochemical analysis of Fc-tagged EDA proteins showed reduced secretion of p.Gln254Lys, whereas p.Thr378Met showed secretion comparable to wild type, suggesting that impaired signaling may result from either decreased ligand availability or defective receptor interaction. AlphaFold2-based structural models demonstrated preservation of the overall TNF homology domain architecture, with only subtle local alterations near the substituted residues. The p.Gln254Lys variant may alter local interactions involved in receptor binding, whereas p.Thr378Met may affect local packing within the β-sandwich core required for receptor engagement. These findings demonstrate that subtle local structural perturbations, rather than global folding defects, can disrupt EDA-EDAR signaling and contribute to XLHED pathogenesis.

en: Functional analysis of AMOTL1, a candidate gene for orofacial clefts, during palatal development
ja: 口唇口蓋裂候補遺伝子AMOTL1の口蓋発生における機能解析
abs: Recent human genetic studies have identified pathogenic variants in angiomotin-like 1(AMOTL1) in multiple patients with orofacial clefts, suggesting that AMOTL1 may represent a novel disease-associated gene in craniofacial development. AMOTL1 is a Hippo pathway-associated molecule that regulates the intracellular localization and transcriptional activity of Yes-associated protein (YAP); however, its role in palatal development remains unclear. To provide functional evidence supporting the involvement of AMOTL1 in orofacial clefts, we investigated its expression during murine palatal development and examined its relationship with YAP using human embryonic palatal mesenchymal (HEPM) cells. Immunofluorescence analysis demonstrated AMOTL1 expression in both epithelial and mesenchymal cells of the developing secondary palate at E13.5-E14.5 in C57BL/6 mouse embryos. In HEPM cells, AMOTL1 localized to both the cytoplasm and nucleus. Furthermore, siRNA-mediated knockdown of AMOTL1 reduced YAP1 expression. These findings suggest that AMOTL1 may contribute to palatal development through regulation of YAP signaling and provide functional support for the pathogenic relevance of AMOTL1 variants in patients with orofacial clefts.

en: Establishment of disease-specific iPSCs derived from Japanese familial NBCCS with a novel PTCH1 mutation
ja: 新規PTCH1変異を有する日本人家族性NBCCS由来の疾患特異的iPS細胞の樹立
abs: Background: Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome (NBCCS) is a rare autosomal dominant disorder caused by mutations in the PTCH1 gene, characterized by bifid ribs and palmar pits, as well as a predisposition to various tumors, including basal cell carcinoma, and odontogenic keratocyst. In this study, we identified a novel PTCH1 mutation in a Japanese family with NBCCS and established patient-derived disease-specific induced pluripotent stem cells (NBCCS-hiPSCs). Methods: Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were obtained from patients and family members of NBCCS. Mutation analysis was performed using next-generation sequencing. NBCCS-hiPSCs were generated using a non-integrating Sendai virus vector under fully defined, serum- and feeder-free conditions. Results: A novel PTCH1 mutation, designated PTCH1_c.3298_3299insAAG, was identified. In silico analysis indicated that the detected variant was pathogenic. The established NBCCS-hiPSCs retained the mutation, could be stably maintained under defined conditions, and exhibited both pluripotency and trilineage differentiation potential. Conclusion: A novel pathogenic mutation was identified in a familial NBCCS, and disease-specific iPSCs carrying this mutation were established. These cells are expected to serve as a valuable model for elucidating the pathogenesis of NBCCS and as a resource for the development of novel therapeutic strategies for rare genetic skeletal disorders. This work has been published in Human Genome Variation 7(1):38, 2020, and In Vitro Cellular & Developmental Biology - Animal, 59(6):395-400, 2023.

en: Transcriptomic analysis of brain organoids derived from a patient with a GNAO1 Variant
ja: GNAO1バリアント患者由来脳オルガノイドのトランスクリプトーム解析
abs: Background: GNAO1 is one of the genes associated with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE). Pathogenic variants in GNAO1 cause severe developmental delay, epilepsy, and involuntary movements. Previous studies have suggested that GNAO1 plays an important role in neuronal polarization and cytoskeletal remodeling and may be involved in Rho GTPase signaling. However, the effects of GNAO1 variants on human neurodevelopment and the underlying molecular pathways remain unclear. Objective: To generate brain organoids from patient-derived iPS cells carrying a GNAO1 variant and investigate molecular alterations associated with neurodevelopment and Rho GTPase signaling. Methods and Results: Brain organoids were generated from healthy control and GNAO1 variant iPS cells. Samples were collected at days 18, 35, and 60 for RNA extraction. Bulk RNA sequencing was performed to comprehensively evaluate transcriptomic alternations, followed by quantitative PCR validation of selected neurodevelopmental and Rho GTPase signaling-related genes. Differential gene expression was observed between control- and GNAO1-derived organoids, including genes associated with neuronal development and cytoskeletal regulation. Conclusions: These findings suggest that GNAO1 variants may alter neurodevelopmental pathways and Rho GTPase signaling during human brain development. Comprehensive transcriptomic analysis of GNAO1-derived brain organoids may provide insights into disease mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets for DEE.

en: Rapid Genetic Evaluation for Suspected Marfan Syndrome in Late Pregnancy: A Case Report
ja: 妊娠後期のMarfan症候群疑いに対する迅速遺伝学的評価：症例報告
abs: <Introduction> Marfan syndrome (MFS) is associated with serious perinatal risks. Ideally, MFS should be diagnosed before conception; however, some patients remain undiagnosed until late pregnancy. We report a case in which rapid genetic evaluation helped avoid potentially unnecessary obstetric intervention. <Case> A 36-year-old woman (G2P1) was referred to our cardiology department at 30w5d of gestation. MFS was suspected due to scoliosis and family history; however, she did not meet the Ghent diagnostic criteria, complicating perinatal management and causing anxiety. Genetic counseling was provided and genetic testing performed. Due to the advanced gestational age, we coordinated with the testing laboratory to obtain an interim report earlier than usual. No pathogenic variants were identified. Integrating the genetic and clinical findings enabled reconsideration of the planned obstetric management, including painless delivery and medication. After explanation of the results and revised management plan, the patient was reassured and later had an uncomplicated vaginal delivery. <Discussion> This case highlights the role of expedited genetic evaluation when clinical findings alone are insufficient to guide obstetric management. Rapid communication among the genetic counseling team, testing laboratory, cardiology department, and obstetric team facilitated interpretation of results and refinement of management. Such coordination may be valuable in late pregnancy, when clinical decisions must be made within limited time frames and uncertainty may increase patient anxiety.

en: Psychosocial Aspects of Families of Children Diagnosed with ReNU Syndrome: A Retrospective Review of Clinical Narratives
ja: ReNU症候群と診断された児の家族の心理社会的側面：臨床記録の後方視的検討
abs: Background: Recently, non-coding RNA-related disorders that are difficult to diagnose by conventional exome sequencing have been identified. ReNU syndrome is a newly recognized neurodevelopmental disorder caused by variants in small nuclear RNA genes and aberrant splicing. This study examined family perceptions of result disclosure and genetic counseling issues in ReNU syndrome. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed counseling records of three ReNU syndrome cases, focusing on diagnosis, family reactions, and counseling needs. Results: The causative genes were RNU4-2, RNU5-2, and RNU2-5, and ages at diagnosis ranged from 6 to 14 years. During result disclosure counseling, clinicians explained that previous testing had failed because the variants were located in non-coding RNA genes and represented newly recognized disorders. Families expressed relief, expectations for future disease information, and willingness to contribute to medical knowledge despite remaining uncertainty. Discussion: Patients with ReNU syndrome often experience a prolonged diagnostic odyssey because conventional exome sequencing fails to detect non-coding RNA variants. Explanation of the relationship between non-coding RNA variants and their functional effects may help families understand why diagnosis had been difficult and facilitate acceptance of the disorder. Families also viewed the diagnosis as a hope for future medical contributions and knowledge accumulation, suggesting the importance of genetic counseling in supporting personal resilience.

en: Temporal trend in clinical needs for genetic counseling at a children's hospital
ja: 小児病院における遺伝カウンセリングの臨床ニーズの経時的傾向
abs: Since the introduction of non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) to Japan in 2013, the number of institutions offering the test has continuously increased. At present, 20 certified hospitals and clinics in Saitama provide NIPT with genetic counseling required prior to testing. Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) is a molecular approach to reveal genomic alterations known to drive cancer growth, which may inform targeted therapies and clinical trial options for cancer patients. Following the implementation of CGP in 2019, increasing numbers of patients have been diagnosed with hereditary cancer syndromes. As a result, the demand and role for genetic counseling at children's hospitals has changed. We reviewed the referral reasons in 124 genetic counseling cases between 2018 and 2024. In 2018, providing information on prenatal diagnosis and recurrence risk for Down syndrome was the most frequent reason, which decreased significantly to only 3 cases in 2024. In contrast, concerns regarding the risk to family members of hereditary cancer syndromes showed a marked increase, becoming the most prevalent reason for genetic counseling in 2024. The widespread use of CGP in pediatric patients may have increased referrals for genetic counseling related to hereditary cancer syndromes. In contrast, with the increasing number of hospitals and clinics offering NIPT, the need for genetic counseling regarding prenatal diagnosis and recurrence risk for Down syndrome may have decreased. Genetic counseling in pediatric hospitals should continue to evolve to meet changing clinical needs.

en: Continuous Genetic Counseling from the Prenatal Period for the Family of a Child with a TUBB2A- Related Disorder
ja: TUBB2A関連疾患児の家族への出生前からの継続的遺伝カウンセリング
abs: Introduction: Families of children with severe congenital anomalies often experience both a desire for a diagnosis and concerns about parental responsibility. We report continuous genetic counseling(GC) provided from pregnancy through diagnosis in a child with a Tubulinopathy. Case: A 34-year-old primigravida was referred for abnormal prenatal ultrasound findings. G-banding, followed by postnatal chromosomal microarray analysis, was nondiagnostic. WES identified a novel TUBB2A(NM_001069.3) variant, c.293G>A (p.Gly98Glu). The parents wished to know the cause of their child's condition but feared that one of them might carry the causative variant. The mother was particularly hesitant to pursue testing because of concerns about parental culpability. Multiple GC sessions were conducted before and after testing to discuss the purpose, benefits, limitations, and possible outcomes of genomic analysis while exploring the parents' emotions and concerns. Through ongoing GC, they reframed participation in the study as a way to help other families and agreed to proceed. At result disclosure, the parents expressed relief that a diagnosis had been established and reassurance that neither parent carried the variant, while also grieving confirmation of a severe neurodevelopmental disorder. Continued psychosocial support was provided. Conclusion: Continuous GC facilitated informed decision-making, reduced guilt and uncertainty, and supported acceptance of the diagnosis. Longitudinal counseling is essential for families undergoing genomic evaluation for severe congenital disorders.

en: Sharing Genetic Information with Relatives: Decision-Making Processes and Challenges
ja: 血縁者との遺伝情報の共有：意思決定プロセスと課題
abs: Background: Genetic information (GI) on hereditary diseases is crucial for probands and their relatives; however, attitudes toward sharing such information vary among individuals. In this study, we identified factors influencing decision making regarding sharing GI among patients with positive genetic testing (GT) results and examined associated challenges. Methods: Between 2018 and 2026, 760 individuals underwent GT at our center, of which 129 carried a pathogenic variant and were the first in their family to undergo GT. To focus on actionable conditions, 75 individuals with pathogenic variants in genes on the ACMG SF v3.3 list were included. Results: Among the 75 individuals, 69 intended to share their GI with relatives, 3 declined to do so, and the intentions of 3 individuals could not be determined. Information sharing was confirmed in 51 of 69 cases (44 had tumor-related diseases, 4 had cardiovascular diseases, and 3 had endocrine/metabolic diseases), leading to genetic testing among 23 relatives from 20 families. Analysis of the 11 individuals who postponed sharing despite expressing willingness and the 3 individuals who declined sharing identified five barriers to information sharing: patient-related, perceived characteristics of relatives, family relationships, disease-related characteristics, and healthcare/support. Discussion: Especially when at-risk relatives are minors, a long-term approach to support may be needed, considering disease acceptance, treatment status, and concerns about potential psychological burdens associated with information sharing.

en: Consensus on presymptomatic diagnosis of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 in children: A single- center experience
ja: 小児の多発性内分泌腫瘍症1型の発症前診断に関するコンセンサス：単一施設の経験
abs: Approximately 90% of individuals with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) are diagnosed after developing clinical manifestations, which typically appear in adulthood. Therefore, the optimal approach for diagnosing MEN1 during childhood remains under investigation. We present our single-center experience in developing an institutional consensus on the presymptomatic diagnosis of MEN1 in children. A 1-year-6-month-old girl was referred to our division to consider presymptomatic genetic testing for MEN1. Her father, paternal grandfather, and paternal aunt were all diagnosed with MEN1. The parents wished to pursue genetic testing for their child in her adulthood and obtain information regarding the indications for testing in childhood. To optimize the approach to presymptomatic diagnosis, a multidisciplinary conference was subsequently held involving endocrinologists, oncologists, geneticists, and genetic counsellors, resulting in consensus recommendations for surveillance in their respective areas of expertise. We particularly focused on the appropriate age for pediatric presymptomatic diagnosis and the disclosure of the possibility of MEN1 to the child, while respecting the child's right to know (or not to know). Based on these discussions, an institutional consensus was established and shared with the family, recommending consideration of presymptomatic genetic testing after the child reaches 10 years of age. Building consensus through multidisciplinary conferences is expected to become increasingly important in future genomic medicine practice.

en: A case referred for genetic counseling following internet-based information searches by family members
ja: 家族によるインターネット情報検索を契機に遺伝カウンセリングへ紹介された1例
abs: <Background> Recently, people can easily access disease related information on the Internet. A study conducted in the United States found that more than 80% of families used the Internet before attending a pediatric genetics clinic. <Case 1> A boy aged 10 presented with episodes of upward eye deviation beginning around 6 months of age, along with psychomotor developmental delay. Extensive evaluations at a previous hospital failed to make a diagnosis. At the initial visit, his mother mentioned that she had found a paper describing CACNA1A related disorders on the internet. As the clinical presentation were consistent with those previously reported, CACNA1A genetic testing was performed, and a previously reported pathogenic variant was identified. <Case 2> A man aged 22 with a history of growth hormone therapy for short stature during childhood, autism spectrum disorder, and mild intellectual disability visited our division. His mother had been suspected Prader Willi syndrome (PWS) as a possible diagnosis after coming across it while searching the internet. Although PWS was considered a differential diagnosis, our division recommended chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA). CMA revealed no clinically significant copy number variants. <Conclusion> In the present two cases, the parents'searches for disease names based on symptoms in children motivated them to seek medical attention. Understanding how the parents came to suspect a particular disorder may help guide the diagnostic evaluation and etiological investigation of the children.

en: Role of Genetic Counselors based on Three Cases of Marfan Syndrome Patients Diagnosed in School age
ja: 学童期に診断されたMarfan症候群3例からみた遺伝カウンセラーの役割
abs: Background: A diagnosis of Marfan syndrome (MFS) in childhood contributes to early health management, but causes significant issues regarding disease disclosure to the patient and familial genetic analysis. School aged patients who have their life foundations such as school life and club activities, have to incorporate health management for MFS into their daily life with their cooperation. Objective and Methods: The purpose is to consider the role of certified genetic counselors based on mainly supporting pediatric MFS patients in understanding their diseases. Eight children were diagnosed with MFS in our hospital from April 2025 to March 2026. We retrospectively reviewed the medical records of three cases of school aged patients among them. Results: Because all subjects play sports regularly, exercise restrictions were estimated to change their daily lives. In genetic counseling session, the disease information was provided to the patients as well as their parents before and after genetic testing and disclosure. Consequently, one patient could accept the diagnosis and ask a cardiologist about exercise restrictions. Another patient spoke very little about the diagnosis during genetic counseling, making it difficult to assess their understanding of MFS. From these cases, internalization of their disease and adjusting their current lifestyles turned out to be important so that the MFS patients who got a diagnosis when teenager can manage their health properly. The role of genetic counselors is to enhance patient awareness of their constitution.

en: Genetic Counseling Facilitated Recognition and Family Health Management in NFKB1 Immunodeficiency
ja: NFKB1免疫不全症において遺伝カウンセリングが認識と家族の健康管理を促した例
abs: [Introduction] NFKB1-related immunodeficiency presents with diverse phenotypes, including antibody deficiency, recurrent infections, autoimmunity, and lymphoproliferation. This heterogeneity may obscure recognition of a shared genetic basis within a family. We report a mother and child with different phenotypes caused by the same NFKB1 variant. [Case] A 41-year-old woman developed delayed wound healing after vaginal delivery and recurrent intra-abdominal and incisional abscesses following subsequent cesarean sections. She was referred for evaluation of suspected immunodeficiency. During genetic counseling, family history revealed that her first child was receiving immunoglobulin replacement therapy for IgG2 subclass deficiency. Genetic testing identified the same heterozygous NFKB1 variant (NM_003998.4:c.157delC,p.Gln53Argfs*74) in both the mother and child. The diagnosis explained the mother's recurrent infections and the child's antibody deficiency. Because NFKB1-related immunodeficiency shows marked phenotypic variability, her other asymptomatic children were referred for immunological evaluation. [Discussion] Phenotypic diversity in NFKB1-related immunodeficiency can hinder recognition of a common genetic etiology within a family. In this case, genetic counseling and testing clarified the relationship between different clinical manifestations and enabled follow-up for at-risk relatives. Inborn errors of immunity should be considered when multiple immune-related abnormalities occur within a family, even when the phenotypes differ.

en: Presymptomatic PALB2 carrier surveillance and genetic counseling enabling early breast cancer detection: a case report
ja: PALB2保因者の発症前サーベイランスと遺伝カウンセリングが早期乳がん発見につながった1例
abs: PALB2 germline pathogenic variant (GPV) carriers require risk-based surveillance and shared decision-making at cancer diagnosis, yet gene-specific management protocols for PALB2 remain to be standardized in Japan. We report a case illustrating the role of sustained genetic counseling in enabling early cancer detection and informed decision-making. A woman in her 60s voluntarily sought genetic counseling based on a family history of breast/thyroid cancer in her sister and pancreatic cancer in her father. Multi-gene panel testing at the presymptomatic stage identified a PALB2 GPV. Guideline-concordant, self-funded surveillance was initiated in close collaboration with the breast surgery department. Three years later, contrast-enhanced breast MRI detected a 5-mm lesion, leading to a diagnosis of early-stage breast cancer. Following diagnosis, ongoing genetic counseling addressed surgical decision-making (including breast-conserving surgery versus mastectomy, risk of new ipsilateral primary breast cancer, contralateral risk-reducing mastectomy, and surveillance of related organs) with support tailored to the patient's values. The prior therapeutic relationship built through continuous genetic counseling from GPV identification facilitated smooth shared decision-making between the patient and the multidisciplinary team. This case suggests that presymptomatic surveillance embedded within a structured hereditary tumor screening program, combined with sustained genetic counseling, contributes to early cancer detection and supports informed treatment decisions in PALB2 GPV carriers.

en: Improving genetic literacy through public lectures and workshop on a pedigree drawing
ja: 公開講座と家系図作成ワークショップによる遺伝リテラシーの向上
abs: Background: Higher genetic literacy among the general public is expected to be achieved through an appropriate understanding of one's own family history; however, such opportunities are limited in Japan. Objective: This study aimed to improve genetic literacy through public lectures on pedigree drawing and to identify challenges for the future development of pedigree notebooks that are easy for the general public to use. Methods: Following the genetics lectures, participants practiced pedigree drawing using two mock cases. Subsequently, questionnaires were conducted to assess the participants' understanding and evaluation of the lecture. Results: Of the 13 participants, questionnaire responses were obtained from 6 participants and scanned pedigree drawings from 11 participants. Although staff support contributed to minimizing notation errors, seven of the 11 participants had difficulty aligning individual symbols within the same generation. In the questionnaire responses, a participant noted that understanding genetic information may help manage one's own health, and requested opportunities for individual consultation regarding their personal concerns. Some participants also sought consultations regarding their family history after the lectures and workshop. Conclusion: The lectures and workshop encouraged participants to view genetics as personally relevant and highlighted the need for opportunities to address genetic concerns. Providing pedigree templates with predefined generation identifiers may improve future notebook development.

en: Identifying Challenges in Providing Remote Supervision to Clinical Genetics Trainees in Hokkaido
ja: 北海道における臨床遺伝研修医への遠隔指導の課題の抽出
abs: [Background and Objectives] In regions such as Hokkaido, where genetic healthcare resources are unevenly distributed, clinical genetics trainees may face limited access to sufficient educational opportunities and supervision. This study aimed to identify the challenges experienced by board-certified clinical geneticists (CGs) in Hokkaido during their training and the educational support they perceived as necessary. [Methods] We conducted a web-based survey regarding training experiences among 78 CGs working in Hokkaido. [Results] As of June 3, 2026, 26 CGs responded (response rate: 33%). Among them, 13 had obtained certification through the transitional system and had not undergone formal training; therefore, responses from the remaining 13 were analyzed. The key challenges included uneven distribution of case types in genetic counseling, limited opportunities for case experience and observation, and financial burdens, including travel expenses. Open-ended comments highlighted institution-dependent case disparities and a desire for systematic educational opportunities in medical genetics. Additionally, a need for online lectures and seminars was identified. [Discussion] Online platforms could address time constraints, travel expenses, and institutional case disparities by enabling trainees to experience cases from other institutions. While the genetic medicine seminar by JSHG and the GCRP by JSGC have already been fully transitioned to online formats, applying similar online approaches to case-based training may offer a potential solution to these challenges.

en: Awareness and Education for Multidisciplinary Staff in Introducing family tree into Electronic Medical Record
ja: 電子カルテへの家系図導入における多職種スタッフの認識と教育
abs: [Background] Family trees are essential for hereditary disease risk assessment. Our hospital plans to introduce family trees in addition to traditional genograms; therefore, we assessed multidisciplinary staff awareness and educational needs. [Objective] To clarify staff awareness of family tree use, reasons for its necessity, perceived need among staff groups, and educational issues. [Methods] An anonymous web-based survey was conducted among staff who use electronic medical records. [Results] Responses were obtained from 195 staff. While 89.7% had viewed family history data in electronic medical records, only 39.0% had entered such data. On a 5-point scale of medical necessity, 53.8% rated family trees as "5" and 29.2% as "4" Reasons included understanding patients' biological relationships (69.2%) and cohabitants (67.7%), identifying carers (65.1%) and emotional support (61.0%), confirming family medical history (60.0%), and assessing hereditary disease risk (58.5%). The perceived need was highest among nurses, cancer counselors, and physicians. [Discussion] Family trees were recognized not only for assessing hereditary disease risk but also for obtaining information about family support. However, despite shared access to the data, data entry was limited compared with viewing frequency, suggesting that recording and updating may be limited to certain professions. To utilize family trees effectively in electronic medical records, profession-specific training on the purpose, clinical use, characteristics, and handling of the data is necessary.

en: Communicating Genomic Information to the Public: Preliminary Findings from a Scoping Review
ja: ゲノム情報の市民への伝え方：スコーピングレビューの予備的知見
abs: Advances in genomic medicine are transforming healthcare from a one-size-fits-all model to precision medicine. To ensure that these innovations benefit a broad and diverse population, effective communication between researchers and the public is essential. However, some populations remain insufficiently reached by existing communication strategies. To identify effective approaches for engaging these populations, we conducted a scoping review and examined existing methods for communicating genomic information. The review focused on 1) communication strategies employed and 2) target populations, with particular attention to groups that are difficult to reach. Systematic searches of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science identified 965 articles published between 2005 and 2025. After the first screening based on predefined eligibility criteria, 330 studies were included. Half of them highlighted the population's literacy/ knowledge, perceptions, and feelings as a strategy to improve communication. Patients and their relatives comprised 42% of the target population. Since 2010, studies have increasingly targeted diverse groups, including the public and specific ethnic communities. From the late 2010s onward, both the range of communication strategies and the diversity of target populations increased. Among the included studies, 31 articles focusing on hard-to-reach populations were selected for full-text analysis. Our next step is to identify key characteristics of these groups for more effective and inclusive communication of genomic information.

en: Public awareness of genetic and genomic medicine: a survey of randomly sampled citizens in Japan
ja: 遺伝・ゲノム医療に関する市民の認知度：日本の無作為抽出市民調査
abs: Background: To optimize information provision in genetic and genomic medicine, public awareness should first be assessed in community settings. Methods: We conducted a questionnaire survey among 2,000 randomly sampled citizens using an online survey platform. Awareness was scored as an ordinal variable (0-2). Associations between respondent characteristics, genetic counseling needs, and awareness were examined using non-parametric statistical methods. Free-text responses regarding "genetic" and "genome" were analyzed by word-frequency and co-occurrence network analyses. Results: A total of 372 citizens responded (18.6%). Awareness scores differed by education level, with higher scores in groups with higher educational attainment (Kruskal-Wallis test, p<0.01). Respondents with current or previous genetic counseling needs had higher awareness scores than those without such needs (Wilcoxon rank-sum test, p<0.001). Item-level analysis showed that this difference was mainly attributable to test-related items, including genetic testing and prenatal genetic testing. In qualitative analyses, frequent and connected words for "genetic" included inherited, family, good, and bad, whereas those for "genome" included gene, analysis, difficult, and afraid. Discussion: Awareness was associated with education level and genetic counseling needs. Item-level analysis showed that the difference by genetic counseling needs was mainly attributable to test-related items, suggesting that community interest may be shaped by concrete testing situations rather than abstract medical concepts.

en: Three-Year Implementation of Genomic Literacy Lectures for the General Public: A Questionnaire- Based Analysis
ja: 一般市民向けゲノムリテラシー講座3年間の実施：質問紙調査に基づく分析
abs: Background: With the advancement of genomic medicine, improving genomic literacy among the general public has become increasingly important. Since 2024, we have conducted annual public genomic literacy lectures in a hybrid format. Methods: The lectures covered fundamental concepts of DNA, genes, and genome; characteristics and diversity of genomic information; limitations of direct-to-consumer genetic testing; cancer genomic medicine; reproductive and perinatal medicine; genetic counseling; and perspectives from patients and their families. Results: A total of 476 individuals participated over three years, and 349 questionnaire responses (response rate: 73.3%) were analyzed. Among respondents, 54.6% were female. Participants aged 40 years or older accounted for the majority; however, junior and senior high school students participated in 2026, representing 21.9% of participants. Overall, 87.7% of respondents rated the lectures as "excellent" or "good." Although some participants found specialized topics difficult to understand, free-text responses suggested increased awareness of the relationship between genomic information, personal health, and family health. Experiences shared by patients and their families encouraged participants to view genetic information as personally relevant. Conclusions: Public genomic literacy lectures may contribute to improving public understanding of genomic medicine and genetic information. Future efforts should focus on age-appropriate educational programs and collaboration with school-based education.

en: A Case of Pregnancy Following Miscarriage of a Tetraploid Fetus with a Balanced Translocation, Achieved Through PGT-SR
ja: 均衡型転座保因者の四倍体胎児流産後にPGT-SRで妊娠に至った1例
abs: <case> We report a case in which Chromosome Analysis of product of conception (POC)was performed in a patient with a history of three recurrent miscarriages, identified tetraploid and a balanced translocation (BT), followed by chromosomal testing of the couple. After BT was confirmed in the wife, preimplantation genetic testing for structural rearrangements (PGT-SR) was performed, achieving a successful pregnancy. The patient was a 37-year-old woman who had spontaneous miscarriages at 5 weeks of gestation at 35 and 36 years of age; she was diagnosed with a symptomless miscarriage at 5 weeks of gestation in this instance as well. Due to this history, genetic counseling (GC) was provided for this miscarriage, and POC was performed. The results were 92,XXXX, t(3;10)(q25;q26) ×2. Based on these results, GC was conducted, and chromosomal testing was performed on the couple. The wife's karyotype was 46XX, t(3;10)(q25;q26). GC focused on recurrent miscarriage was conducted, and it was decided to perform PGT-SR to prevent recurrent miscarriage. Normal embryos or embryos with BT were obtained, and frozen-thawed embryo transfer was performed. Pregnancy was achieved.checkups. <Discussion> The determination that the wife carried the same translocation as the miscarried fetus allowed us to identify one of the causes of the miscarriage and provided information on specific steps to take in preparation for a subsequent pregnancy. Identifying a factor contributing to recurrent miscarriages is considered important for relieving anxiety regarding pregnancy.

en: Changes in Prenatal Genetic Counseling and NIPT Uptake After Certification System Revision at Our Hospital
ja: 当院における認証制度改定後の出生前遺伝カウンセリングとNIPT受検の変化
abs: Background: In 2022, Japan revised the NIPT implementation system, allowing testing regardless of maternal age. Although prenatal genetic counseling (PGC) visits by younger women were expected to increase, the effects on test selection and results remain unclear. Objective: To examine changes in PGC clients and NIPT test takers at our hospital before and after the revision. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed first-visit PGC cases from April 1, 2021, to October 31, 2023. July 2022 was excluded as a transition month. The pre- and post-revision periods were April 1, 2021, to June 30, 2022, and August 1, 2022, to October 31, 2023; both spanned 15 months. Age, gestational age, NIPT uptake, and results were collected from medical records. Statistical analyses were performed using Python, with pp <0.05 considered significant. Results: The study included 195 cases before and 211 after revision. Mean age decreased from 36.4±3.9 to 35.5±4.7 years, and the proportion aged<35 years increased from 28.2% to 42.7%. Among NIPT test takers, mean age changed only slightly, from 37.1±3.7 to 36.7±4.1 years. Gestational age was 12.96±1.89 and 12.88±2.06 weeks, and NIPT uptake was 71.3% and 69.7%, with no significant changes. Positivity rates were low in both periods and did not differ significantly. Conclusion: After relaxation of age restrictions, PGC clients became younger, whereas age among NIPT test takers changed only modestly. The uptake and positivity rates of NIPT did not change significantly. PGC may support informed decision-making, including the option not to undergo testing.

en: Two Sibling Cases of Fetal Cleft Lip and Palate Prenatally Diagnosed by Three-Dimensional Ultrasonography
ja: 三次元超音波で出生前診断された胎児口唇口蓋裂の同胞2例
abs: [Introduction] Cleft lip and/or palate can cause feeding difficulty, delayed speech, and malocclusion. Because sibling recurrence burdens parents, prenatal diagnosis and counseling are important. We report two sibling cases diagnosed prenatally by three-dimensional ultrasonography (3D-US). [Case 1] A 26-year-old gravida 4, para 3 woman had no relevant history. Her third child had cleft lip. Cleft lip was suspected at 24 weeks, and 3D-US at 34 weeks showed a hard-palate defect, leading to diagnosis of cleft lip and palate. No other anomalies were detected. She delivered vaginally at 36 weeks. The male infant weighed 2,164 g, had Apgar scores of 8/9, and had cleft lip and palate. After Hotz plate placement on day 13, feeding improved, and he was discharged on day 26. [Case 2] A 26-year-old gravida 2, para 1 woman used topical steroids for atopic dermatitis. Her first child had cleft lip. 3D-US at 21 weeks showed fetal cleft lip without cleft palate; the same finding was confirmed at 25 weeks. Labor was induced at 39 weeks, followed by vaginal delivery under epidural anesthesia. The female infant weighed 2,942 g, had Apgar scores of 9/9, and had cleft lip and alveolar cleft without cleft palate. Mother and infant were discharged on day 5. [Discussion and Conclusion] Cleft palate is harder to diagnose prenatally because it is difficult to visualize by ultrasonography. 3D-US may help diagnose fetal morphological abnormalities and explain treatment plans to families. In these cases, 3D-US enabled prenatal diagnosis, genetic counseling, and planning of postnatal management.

en: Amniocentesis in the NIPT Era: Patient Background and Psychological Factors with AMA as the Sole Indication
ja: NIPT時代の羊水検査：高年妊娠のみを適応とした患者背景と心理的要因
abs: Objectives: NIPT was introduced in Japan, including our center, in 2013. The launch of the new NIPT accreditation system in 2022 led to an increase in testing facilities. With the growing number of NIPT cases, amniocentesis has shown a downward trend. While most current cases have high-risk indications (e.g., ultrasound abnormalities, positive NIPT), some choose it solely for advanced maternal age (AMA). We aimed to clarify the backgrounds and psychological factors (K6 scores) of women who chose amniocentesis. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 68 women whose sole indication was AMA requesting amniocentesis (2020-2025), divided into pre- (2020-2022, n=53) and post-accreditation (2023-2025, n=15) groups to compare backgrounds and K6 scores. Results: Requests due to previous amniocentesis history decreased from 24.5% to 6.7%(p=0.17), while requesting tests beyond three major trisomies increased from 13.4% to 26.7%(p=0.24). Multiparous women decreased (56.6% to 26.7%, p=0.077). Conversely, pregnancies via fertility treatment (28.3% vs 53.3%,p=0.12), miscarriage history (17.0% vs 33.3%, p=0.28), and K6 scores >=5 (5.7% vs 13.3%,p=0.30) showed upward trends post-accreditation. Conclusions: Changes in patient backgrounds and reasons for testing have changed before and after 2022. Pregnant women currently requesting amniocentesis are considered a group with higher anxiety, who may be actively seeking information regarding congenital disorders and prenatal testing. Meticulous pre-test genetic counseling and careful post-test follow-up are necessary.

en: False-Positive Expanded Non-Invasive Prenatal Testing Result Associated with a Vanishing Twin Pregnancy: A Case Report
ja: バニシングツイン妊娠に関連した拡大NIPTの偽陽性：症例報告
abs: Non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) is a prenatal screening method that evaluates the risk of fetal chromosomal abnormalities using fetal-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in maternal blood. Expanded NIPT, which additionally screens for sex chromosome aneuploidies and microdeletion syndromes, has recently been introduced overseas. We report a case of a vanishing twin pregnancy in which expanded NIPT detected a 4.05-Mb deletion in the 11p15.4 region. She was a 44-year-old Japanese woman (gravida 2, para 1) who conceived by IVF-ET with her Chinese partner. NIPT performed in China revealed a 4.05- Mb microdeletion in 11p15.4, and she was referred to our hospital for amniocentesis at 17 weeks of gestation. Medical interview and ultrasonography revealed a vanishing twin pregnancy. G-banding demonstrated a maternal karyotype of 46, XX and a fetal one of 46, XY. Chromosomal analyses of maternal and amniotic fluid samples showed no 11p deletion or other pathogenic abnormalities, although loss of heterozygosity was observed on maternal chromosomes 2 and 3. Vanishing twin syndrome occurs in 10-39% of IVF pregnancies, and cfDNA from the demised twin may persist in maternal plasma for several weeks after fetal demise. In this case, the absence of abnormalities in the surviving fetus by G-banding, amniocentesis, and ultrasonography suggested that the NIPT finding reflected the genetic background of the demised twin. These findings indicate that NIPT results in vanishing twin pregnancies should be interpreted carefully because cfDNA from the demised fetus may cause false-positive results.

en: Trends in Prenatal Testing at Our Hospital from Fiscal Years 2018 to 2025
ja: 当院における2018〜2025年度の出生前検査の動向
abs: [Background] Our hospital offers prenatal screening including amniocentesis (AC), chorionic villus sampling (CVS), combined screening, maternal serum marker testing, and non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT). In February 2022, the Japanese Association of Medical Science issued new guidelines on prenatal testing, introducing changes in information provision for pregnant women and eligibility criteria for NIPT. [Objective] This study aimed to investigate trends in prenatal screening utilisation at our hospital. [Methods] We analysed the numbers and demographic characteristics, including maternal age, of patients undergoing prenatal testing at our hospital between April 2018 and March 2026. Patients were included regardless of their planned delivery site. [Results] During the study period, 7,288 patients underwent prenatal testing. The number of NIPT tests increased from 658 in fiscal year (FY) 2018 to 760 in FY2025. The proportions of each test changed as follows: AC/CVS, 9.4% to 3.7%; maternal serum marker testing, 5.3% to 1.8%; combined screening, 17.2% to 5.4%; and NIPT, 68.1% to 89.1%. The proportion of NIPT recipients aged 34 years or younger increased from 4.1% to 45.8%, while the median maternal age decreased from 38 to 35 years. [Discussion] Prenatal tests other than NIPT showed a decreasing trend. The increasing proportion of younger NIPT recipients and decrease in median maternal age may indicate expansion of NIPT use across a broader maternal age range.

en: A maternal COL1A1 variant segregating with skeletal dysplasia in successive pregnancies
ja: 連続する妊娠で骨系統疾患と分離する母由来COL1A1バリアント
abs: Molecular diagnosis is essential for recurrence-risk counseling in fetal skeletal dysplasia. We report a family in which a maternally inherited COL1A1 variant segregated with severe fetal/infantile skeletal disease despite minimal maternal manifestations. The mother had short stature (138.5 cm) but no fractures, blue sclerae, dental abnormalities, hearing loss, or relevant family history. In the first affected pregnancy, ultrasonography showed severe short and bowed long bones, and postmortem radiography revealed a very thin skull and multiple fractures, consistent with severe osteogenesis imperfecta; genetic testing was not performed. In the second affected pregnancy, targeted gene panel testing of products of conception identified a heterozygous COL1A1 variant, NM_000088.4:c.2236G>A (p.Gly746Ser), classified as likely pathogenic. The variant was confirmed in the fetus and mother, but not in the father. After one early miscarriage, a subsequent child showed severe limb shortening from 18 weeks, carried the same variant after birth, and was diagnosed with osteogenesis imperfecta type III; she remains alive at over 1 year with bisphosphonate therapy. In contrast, the next child had normal prenatal skeletal findings, was appropriate for gestational age, and did not carry the variant. These findings support segregation of the maternal COL1A1 variant with the phenotype. This case highlights the importance of molecular and parental testing, as counseling may change from apparently sporadic disease to autosomal dominant inheritance with a 50% recurrence risk.

en: Role of Genetic Counseling in Chromosomal Microarray Analysis for Fetal Ultrasound Abnormalities
ja: 胎児超音波異常に対する染色体マイクロアレイ解析における遺伝カウンセリングの役割
abs: Background: At our institution, chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA) is offered to pregnant women with fetal ultrasound abnormalities requesting further genetic evaluation. CMA is a useful test when rapid chromosomal testing indicates a low likelihood of trisomy 13, 18, 21, and sex chromosome aneuploidies. We reviewed cases that underwent CMA and examined the role of genetic counseling (GC). Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 13 cases that underwent CMA between 2023 and 2025: 5 with increased nuchal translucency, 5 with cystic hygroma, and 3 with other structural abnormalities. GC was evaluated according to test results and clinical circumstances. Results: No pathogenic copy number variants were detected in any case. During pre-test GC, information on additional testing options, including RASopathy panel testing and exome analysis, was provided. However, considering cost, turnaround time, and inconclusive findings, no additional testing beyond CMA was selected. Most cases underwent second-trimester ultrasound examinations. Discussion: The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists recommends CMA for invasive prenatal diagnosis when fetal structural abnormalities are identified. However, GC should include an explanation of CMA limitations, including the possibility that abnormalities may remain undetected. Information regarding disorders beyond CMA, such as single-gene disorders, may broaden testing options. Cost and turnaround time may burden patients. Individualized GC is essential to support informed decision-making based on patient circumstances and values.

en: Parental Somatic Mosaicism in KIF11-Related Disorder: A Case Report
ja: KIF11関連疾患における親の体細胞モザイク：症例報告
abs: Pathogenic KIF11 variants cause microcephaly with or without chorioretinopathy, lymphedema, or intellectual disability (MCLMR), characterized by incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity. The proband is a 5-year-old girl born to non-consanguineous healthy parents at 37weeks and 5days of gestation. She presented microcephaly and non-pitting edema from neonatal period. Follow-up revealed persistent microcephaly, developmental delay, and chorioretinopathy. Congenital infection screening was negative, and karyotyping was normal. Exome sequencing of the proband identified a heterozygous KIF11 variant (NM_004523.4:c.1604G>A p.(Gly535Asp)). Sanger sequencing confirmed paternal somatic mosaicism via a mutant allele peak in the asymptomatic father. The variant was classified as uncertain significance (PM2 + PP3 + PP4). The clinical presentation of the proband supports pathogenicity of the variant, aligning with documented KIF11 transmission from asymptomatic mosaic parents. The Sanger sequencing chromatogram of unaffected father's leukocyte DNA suggests a high mutant allele fraction. Incomplete penetrance or tissue-specific mosaicism may be responsible for his asymptomatic condition. Therefore, apparently de novo cases necessitate parental mosaicism screening. Paternal gonadal mosaicism cannot be ruled out, elevating recurrence risk. We recommended paternal ophthalmological evaluation to unmask subclinical retinal lesions. This strategy is vital for accurate recurrence risk assessment, carrier management, and genetic counseling.

en: A Case of Gastrointestinal Polyposis and Intellectual Developmental Delay Diagnosed by MGPT and CMA
ja: MGPTとCMAで診断された消化管ポリポーシスと知的発達遅滞の1例
abs: With the widespread use of multigene panel testing for hereditary cancer (MGPT), genetic testing has increasingly been recommended for diagnosing hereditary tumor predisposition syndromes. We report a case in which MGPT and chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA) helped clarify the genetic background of disease. A 14-year-old boy was found to have colorectal polyposis at 12 years of age. Because he also exhibited mild intellectual developmental delay, MGPT was performed and revealed deletions of APC promoter 1A and 1B regions, leading to a diagnosis of familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP). However, his neurodevelopmental phenotype could not be fully explained by the APC promoter deletions alone. CMA subsequently identified a copy number loss at 5q21.3-q22.2 including APC (5q22.2) and an approximately 1-Mb copy number gain at 21q22.13. Loss of the 5q22 region containing APC has previously been reported in patients with FAP and intellectual developmental delay. In this case, the 5q21.3-q22.2 deletion may have contributed to the neurodevelopmental phenotype through haploinsufficiency of neighboring genes. In addition, the duplicated 21q22.13 region contains several genes associated with intellectual developmental delay in trisomy 21. These findings suggest that the developmental delay may result from the combined effects of the 5q deletion and 21q duplication. Comprehensive genomic analysis, including CMA, may be useful in patients with polyposis accompanied by atypical clinical features such as intellectual developmental delay.

en: A Japanese boy with CTNNB1 neurodevelopmental disorder identified by whole-exome sequencing
ja: 全エクソーム解析で同定されたCTNNB1神経発達症の日本人男児
abs: CTNNB1 encodes β-catenin, a multifunctional protein involved in cell adhesion and Wnt signaling, and has recently emerged as an important cause of neurodevelopmental disorders and cerebral palsy-like phenotypes. The phenotypic spectrum of CTNNB1 neurodevelopmental disorder (CTNNB1-NDD) is broad and includes developmental delay, intellectual disability, microcephaly, motor impairment, visual abnormalities, and various dysmorphic features. A 3-year-old Japanese boy was referred for evaluation of global developmental delay and microcephaly. He was unable to walk independently and had no meaningful speech. Physical examination revealed microcephaly (-2.5 SD), poor weight gain, large ears, downslanting palpebral fissures, bilateral fifth-finger clinodactyly, right fifth-toe macrodactyly, and truncal hypotonia.
