Brain magnetic resonance imaging and metabolic investigations were unremarkable. Chromosomal microarray analysis failed to identify a causative abnormality. Trio-based whole-exome sequencing performed through the Initiative on Rare and Undiagnosed Diseases (IRUD) identified a de novo variant in CTNNB1 (c.274C>T, p.Gln92Ter). This variant has been reported in ClinVar as pathogenic and was considered causative of the patient's phenotype. This case highlights the clinical utility of comprehensive genomic testing in children with unexplained neurodevelopmental disorders and expands awareness of the phenotypic spectrum of CTNNB1-NDD among physicians and geneticists.

en: ADAR-related autosomal dominant hereditary spastic paraplegia in a girl whose father showed only skin lesions
ja: 父が皮膚病変のみを示したADAR関連常染色体顕性遺伝性痙性対麻痺の女児
abs: Background: ADAR (Adenosine Deaminase, RNA specific) variants usually cause autosomal recessive Aicardi-Goutieres syndrome (AGS) 6 and autosomal dominant (AD) dyschromatosis symmetrica hereditaria (DSH). The heterozygous c.3019G>A, p.(Gly1007Arg) variant is associated with AD AGS/hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP), with or without DSH, and incomplete penetrance. Case: A 6-year-old girl developed frequent falls and spastic gait at age 2 years after normal walking acquisition. Brain MRI showed only nonspecific findings, and HSP was suspected. During a febrile infection at age 3 years, she transiently lost speech and ambulation. Whole-genome sequencing identified a heterozygous ADAR c.3019G>A, p.(Gly1007Arg) variant, also detected in her neurologically normal father. After the diagnosis, both were found to have brown macules on the dorsal hands, consistent with DSH. Brain CT revealed bilateral basal ganglia calcifications. Cerebrospinal fluid findings, including neopterin, were normal. Her 1-year-old brother is asymptomatic and has not undergone genetic testing. Discussion: In HSP with this variant, testing neurologically asymptomatic parents can clarify recurrence risk. Neurological deterioration may be triggered by inflammation, including infection or vaccination. Corticosteroids and Janus kinase inhibitors have been reported as treatment options. As no preventive therapy is established, carrier testing in asymptomatic minors may be deferred until they can decide for themselves. Conclusion: Genetic diagnosis for ADAR-related HSP facilitates family evaluation and management.

en: Tethered Cord in Two Patients with PIEZO2-Related Distal Arthrogryposis
ja: PIEZO2関連遠位型関節拘縮症2例における脊髄係留
abs: [Background] Pathogenic PIEZO2 variants cause the distal arthrogryposis (DA) spectrum, including DA3, DA5, and Marden- Walker syndrome. Although spinal deformities are recognized, tethered cord has not been well characterized. We report two patients with PIEZO2-related DA who had sacral dimples and tethered cord. [Cases] Patient 1 was a 9-month-old girl of Japanese and Filipino ancestry. She had arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, deep-set eyes, and a hypomimic face. Spinal MRI performed for a sacral dimple showed a low-lying conus at L3 without lipoma. She underwent untethering at 9 months. Panel testing identified a heterozygous pathogenic PIEZO2 variant, NM_022068.4:c.8181_8183del, p. (Glu2727del). Patient 2 was a Japanese boy referred neonatally with arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, deep-set eyes, and a hypomimic face. Spinal MRI showed a low-lying conus at L4 and a filum terminale cyst without lipoma. He underwent untethering at 5 months. Panel testing identified a heterozygous pathogenic PIEZO2 variant, NM_022068.4:c.8057G>A, p.(Arg2686His). In both patients, postoperative urodynamic abnormalities were observed. [Discussion] To our knowledge, tethered cord has not been described in detail in PIEZO2-related DA. Although causality remains unclear, the recurrent combination of sacral dimples, low-lying conus, and bladder dysfunction is noteworthy. Careful examination for lumbosacral cutaneous stigmata and consideration of spinal imaging may be useful in PIEZO2-related DA. Deep-set eyes and a hypomimic face may help recognize the DA spectrum in congenital arthrogryposis.

en: Familial Supravalvular Aortic Stenosis associated with 7q11.23 Microdeletion including ELN gene detected by CMA and MLPA
ja: CMAとMLPAで検出したELN遺伝子を含む7q11.23微小欠失に伴う家族性大動脈弁上狭窄
abs: Introduction Williams-Beuren syndrome (WS; OMIM #194050) is caused by a heterozygous deletion in 7q11.23. WS is characterized by supravalvular aortic stenosis (SVAS), peripheral pulmonary stenosis (PPS), intellectual disability, and elfin facies. Although FISH is commonly used for diagnosis, atypical deletions may yield false-negative results. Case report The proband was a female infant born at 40 weeks and 4 days of gestation, weighing 2,962 g. Right ventricular hypertrophy was noted prenatally. Postnatal echocardiography showed severe PPS, mild aortic stenosis, and right ventricular hypertrophy. Her mother and maternal grandfather had ventricular hypertrophy and had been diagnosed with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Although the mother had mild cognitive impairment and anxiety disorder, typical facial features and neurodevelopmental abnormalities were absent in both relatives. FISH for WS was negative. Chromosomal microarray analysis and multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification identified a 7q11.23 microdeletion involving the entire ELN and part of LIMK1 , in all three individuals. Discussion The ventricular hypertrophy in this family was likely caused by SVAS-related pressure overload due to ELN haploinsufficiency. This highlights the risk of delayed diagnosis when FISH is negative and typical WS features are absent. Partial LIMK1 deletion may confer risk for subtle visuospatial impairment. Conclusion7q11.23 microdeletion involving ELN and LIMK1 can present with atypical WS phenotype including cardiovascular and potential neurocognitive features.

en: A case of 5p deletion syndrome treated with tracheostomy due to bilateral vocal cord paralysis.
ja: 両側声帯麻痺のため気管切開を行った5p欠失症候群の1例
abs: Background: 5p deletion syndrome is characterized by variable clinical features, including a cat-like cry, dysmorphic facial features, microcephaly, and developmental delay or intellectual disability. Although genotype-phenotype correlations have been investigated, prediction of individual phenotypes remains limited because deletion size and gene content vary among patients. Case: A five-month-old girl born to non-consanguineous Japanese parents as their first child. She was born at 39 weeks and 3 days via vacuum-assisted delivery. Her weight was 2,444 g (-1.4 SD), length was 49.3 (+0.4 SD), and head circumference was 30.5 cm (3-10th percentile). From birth, she had stridor, a round face, telecanthus, epicanthus and micrognathia. She was hospitalized at one month of age due to worsening respiratory conditions and poor feeding. She was diagnosed with bilateral vocal cord paralysis and laryngomalacia and underwent a tracheostomy at two months of age. G-banding karyotyping showed 46,XX. Chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA) identified a 3.9-Mb deletion at 5p15.33: arr[GRCh37] 5p15.33(22149_3955850)x1. Discussion: The observed variability of phenotypes among individuals with 5p deletion is thought to be influenced by differences in breakpoints, deletion size, and gene content. Deletions in similar in size to that in the present case have been reported in apparently asymptomatic individuals. We compare this case with previous reports and discuss the relationship between the extent of the deletion and the clinical manifestations.

en: Dual molecular diagnoses of EBF3 and TG variants in a child with neurodevelopmental disorder & congenital hypothyroidism
ja: 神経発達症と先天性甲状腺機能低下症を有する児のEBF3・TGバリアントの二重分子診断
abs: With the widespread use of comprehensive genomic analysis such as whole exome sequencing (WES), dual molecular diagnoses are increasingly recognized. We report a case of a child with congenital hypothyroidism and neurodevelopmental symptoms in whom WES revealed variants in both the EBF3 and TG genes. The patient is a 3-year-old girl born small for gestational age. Congenital hypothyroidism was detected by newborn mass screening, and thyroid hormone replacement therapy was initiated during the neonatal period. Despite treatment, she had hypotonia, poor growth, epilepsy, limited facial expression, and severe developmental delay. Her developmental quotient was 53 on the Kyoto Scale of Psychological Development. At 18 months of age, G-banded karyotyping and chromosomal microarray analysis revealed no pathogenic abnormalities. WES was performed at 27 months of age because of the severe neurodevelopmental phenotype. WES revealed a de novo heterozygous variant in EBF3, NM_001375380.1:c.486-8_501delinsGCT. This novel variant involved the splice acceptor site, and SpliceAI predicted exon 6 skipping. Because congenital hypothyroidism could not be fully explained by EBF3 alone, additional evaluation identified compound heterozygous TG variants, NM_003235.5:c.[2131C>T];[6017G>A], inherited from each parent. In this case, a single molecular diagnosis could not fully explain the complex clinical phenotype. WES led to dual molecular diagnoses, highlighting the importance of reconsidering the phenotype in complex neurodevelopmental disorders.

en: Williams syndrome characterized by shortened femurs and radioulnar synostosis: A case report
ja: 大腿骨短縮と橈尺骨癒合症を特徴としたWilliams症候群：症例報告
abs: Background: Williams syndrome (WS) is caused by a microdeletion in the 7q11.23 region of chromosome 7, and is associated with developmental delay, growth failure, characteristic facial features, and cardiac complications. However, it may also be accompanied by skeletal abnormalities, requiring consideration of skeletal disorders. We report this case as a lesson in the differential diagnosis of WS, without cardiac complications and exhibiting primarily skeletal changes. Case: A 6-year-old boy, born at 40 weeks of gestation and weighing 2735 g, exhibited shortened femurs since the fetal period. His nose was upturned and small, and his auricles were slightly low-set. He had a developmental delay and remained small for his age, with a height of -2 SD and a weight of -1.5 SD. Chromosome analysis revealed a normal male karyotype (46XY), and growth hormone secretion was normal. A cardiac echocardiogram at birth and thereafter, following a diagnosis of Kawasaki disease at 18 months, showed no abnormalities. At the age of 4, he was unable to perform pronation and supination of the forearms effectively. X-ray and MRI examinations revealed bilateral radioulnar synostosis. Microarray chromosomal analysis revealed a 1.4 Mb deletion at 7q11.23, leading to a definitive diagnosis of WS. Discussion: This case was characterized by shortened femurs and radioulnar synostosis, without cardiac complications. Specifically, radioulnar synostosis is reported in 10% of WS cases, suggesting its importance in the differential diagnosis.

en: Homozygous GJB2-Related Sensorineural Hearing Loss and 22q11.2 Deletion Syndrome Identified by Genetic Testing
ja: 遺伝学的検査で同定されたホモ接合GJB2関連感音難聴と22q11.2欠失症候群
abs: 22q11.2 deletion syndrome is characterized by congenital heart disease in approximately 80% of affected individuals, along with developmental delay, characteristic facial features, immunodeficiency due to thymic hypoplasia or aplasia, cleft palate or velopharyngeal insufficiency, hypernasal speech, and hypocalcemia. The condition results from a microdeletion on chromosome 22 that encompasses approximately 30 genes, whose haploinsufficiency contributes to the clinical manifestations. In particular, deletion of TBX1 is strongly associated with conotruncal cardiac defects such as tetralogy of Fallot and interrupted aortic arch. We report a Vietnamese patient who did not exhibit typical features of 22q11.2 deletion syndrome but presented with congenital hearing loss and a low TREC value on newborn screening. Genetic evaluation using a next-generation sequencing-based hearing loss gene panel and chromosomal microarray analysis identified congenital sensorineural hearing loss caused by a homozygous pathogenic GJB2 variant, as well as a 22q11.2 microdeletion. Assessment of characteristic facial features was challenging because the patient was of foreign nationality and clinicians were less familiar with dysmorphic features in this population. Moreover, the clinical presentation was atypical for 22q11.2 deletion syndrome, making a clinical diagnosis difficult prior to genetic testing. Through detailed investigation of the underlying etiology and pathophysiology, we were able to establish diagnoses of two distinct genetic disorders in this patient.

en: Association between genotype and age at diagnosis in Noonan syndrome
ja: Noonan症候群における遺伝型と診断年齢の関連
abs: Background: Noonan syndrome (NS), one of the RASopathies, is characterized by a broad spectrum of clinical manifestations. Although clinical diagnostic criteria have been proposed, the diagnosis of NS remains challenging because of its clinical heterogeneity. Prior studies have increasingly elucidated genotype-phenotype correlations in NS, suggesting that the age at diagnosis may differ according to the underlying molecular diagnosis. To further clarify genotype-phenotype correlations, we investigated the association between genotype and age at diagnosis in NS. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 49 patients with molecularly diagnosed NS between 2018 and 2025. Genotypes, diagnostic age, and reasons for referral and genetic testing were extracted. Results: The overall median age at diagnosis was 15 months, ranging from 0 months to 14 years. The gene-specific analysis revealed that patients with RAF1, RIT1 and SHOC2 variants were more likely to be diagnosed during infancy, with median ages at diagnosis of 3.5, 4.0 and 9.0 months, respectively. In contrast, NS patients with PTPN11, SOS1 and KRAS variants were generally diagnosed after infancy, with median ages at diagnosis of 20.0, 24.0 and 50.5 months, respectively. Discussion: The increased prevalence of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy among patients with RAF1 or RIT1 variants may contribute to earlier recognition and diagnosis of NS. Furthermore, the early age at diagnosis in patients with SHOC2 variants may reflect their specific clinical features.

en: Chronic Recurrent Multifocal Osteomyelitis Associated with A20 Haploinsufficiency
ja: A20ハプロ不全症に伴う慢性再発性多発性骨髄炎
abs: Background: A20 haploinsufficiency (HA20) is an inborn error of immunity caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in TNFAIP3, presenting with overlapping autoinflammatory and autoimmune features. Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis (CRMO) has rarely been reported in HA20. Case : A 13-year-old boy had perianal abscesses in infancy and periodic fever in early childhood. At 7 years, he developed swelling and pain of the right lateral malleolus. Bone biopsy of the right distal tibial epiphysis showed aseptic osteomyelitis, followed by multifocal lesions in the left tibia and right navicular bone, consistent with CRMO. Genetic testing identified a TNFAIP3 variant, NM_006290.4:c.448C>T (p.Gln150Ter), confirming HA20. Anti-TNF-α therapy controlled the bone inflammation, however, Behcet-like manifestations, including oral aphthae, abdominal pain, diarrhea, and ileocecal aphthous ulcers, subsequently became apparent. His mother had genital/oral ulcers and chronic diarrhea at his diagnosis. She carried the same variant and was also diagnosed with HA20, leading to therapeutic intervention. Discussion: This familial case highlights HA20 as a monogenic cause of CRMO and underlines its intrafamilial phenotypic variability. A20 negatively regulates NF-κ signaling, and its dysfunction promotes inflammatory bone disease through dysregulated osteoclastogenesis and autoinflammation. When CRMO is accompanied by recurrent fever, mucosal ulcers, or gastrointestinal inflammation, HA20 should be considered, and family-based genetic evaluation is essential.

en: Neonatal subgaleal hematoma following non-instrumental delivery as an early manifestation of Marfan syndrome
ja: Marfan症候群の早期徴候としての非器械分娩後の新生児帽状腱膜下血腫
abs: Subgaleal hematoma (SH) is a neonatal hemorrhagic condition typically associated with instrument-assisted delivery. We report a rare case of SH following non-instrumental vaginal delivery in an infant subsequently diagnosed with Marfan syndrome (MFS). A female infant was born at 39 weeks of gestation via uncomplicated vaginal delivery. Her length and weight were average, but arachnodactyly was noted. Immediately after birth, progressive scalp swelling was observed, and SH was diagnosed. Progressive anemia developed, requiring packed red blood cell transfusion on day 2 of life. No coagulation abnormalities or intracranial hemorrhage were identified. At 9 months of age, ankle joint laxity, instability while standing, and marked postnatal growth acceleration raised suspicion of MFS. At 1 year of age, genetic testing identified a pathogenic de novo FBN1 variant, confirming the diagnosis of MFS. Fibrillin-1 abnormalities may increase connective tissue fragility and predispose neonates to SH in response to delivery-related mechanical stress. This case suggests that SH following non-instrumental delivery may represent an early clue to an underlying connective tissue disorder, including MFS.

en: Reduced fetal movements, congenital contractures, and micrognathia with limited mouth opening in QRICH1-related disorder
ja: QRICH1関連疾患における胎動減少・先天性拘縮・開口制限を伴う小顎症
abs: Background: Pathogenic variants in QRICH1 are associated with a rare neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by developmental delay, growth deficiency, and skeletal abnormalities. Severe prenatal manifestations have rarely been reported. Case Presentation: A female infant was referred prenatally because of reduced fetal movements, micrognathia, bell-shaped thorax, and polyhydramnios. At birth, she showed multiple congenital contractures, micrognathia with limited mouth opening, and thoracic hypoplasia. Skeletal radiographs revealed mandibular hypoplasia, slender ribs, and vertebral abnormalities. Brain MRI, karyotyping, and chromosomal microarray analysis showed no significant abnormalities. She exhibited developmental delay with impaired motor and adaptive skills but relatively preserved language development. Trio-based exome sequencing identified a heterozygous de novo missense variant in QRICH1, c.1649A>G, p.(Tyr550Cys). Discussion and Conclusion: The clinical features were largely consistent with those previously reported in QRICH1-related disorder. Reduced fetal movements, congenital contractures, micrognathia with limited mouth opening, and polyhydramnios suggest a severe prenatal presentation of this condition. Micrognathia with limited mouth opening may represent a clinically important manifestation because of its potential impact on feeding and airway management. QRICH1-related disorder should be considered in the differential diagnosis of fetuses with reduced movements and congenital contractures when conventional neuromuscular etiologies are excluded.

en: Introduction of the BRAF V600E mutation using engineered prime editor in induced pluripotent stem cells
ja: 改変プライムエディターを用いたiPS細胞へのBRAF V600E変異の導入
abs: Background: The prime editing (PE) system allows the introduction of point mutations at specific genomic loci without creating double-strand breaks. However, the conventional PE is limited to its target sequences because of the PAM preference to the Streptococcus pyogenes Cas9 protein. Here, we report the efficiency of engineered PE-mediated gene correction in human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). Purpose: To establish iPSCs carrying the BRAF p.V600E variant, which is a well-known driver mutation in various cancers. Methods: Wildtype- PE or engineered-PE plasmids were transfected into iPSCs derived from healthy man via electroporation. Transfected cells were selected using flow cytometry-based cell sorting. Single-cell clones were expanded and analyzed by Sanger sequencing. Results: Among the clones, engineered-PE improved prime editing activity (6-10%) compared with the activity of wildtype-PE (0%). After expansion, all corrected clones expressed pluripotent stem cell markers. Conclusion: The engineered-PE system represents a promising approach for precise gene correction.

en: Identification of CNKSR2 pathogenic variant and detection of strong XCI in a female patient with severe DEE-SWAS
ja: 重症DEE-SWAS女性患者におけるCNKSR2病的バリアントの同定と強いXCIの検出
abs: Introduction and case presentation: CNKSR2 is a crucial regulator of RAC1, which plays a significant role in the growth of neuronal dendrites. Heterozygous pathogenic variants of CNKSR2 are associated with intellectual disability with epilepsy, including Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with spike-wave activation in sleep (DEE-SWAS). However, due to its X-linked recessive genetic disorder, girls are typically asymptomatic. In this study, we identified a pathogenic variant in CNKSR2 (c.2134C>T, p. (Arg712Ter) heterozygous variant (de novo, previously reported)) in a girl with intractable epilepsy and also demonstrate that there was a strong skewing of X chromosome-inactivation (XCI) (85:15). This made it possible to make a definitive diagnosis and provide appropriate treatment. We also present a case of a boy with a novel pathogenic variant in CNKSR2 (c.492C>A, p.(Cys164Ter) hemizygous variant (maternal, novel)). He had symptoms like Angelman syndrome, including a distinctive facial appearance and ataxic gait. Discussion: There have been reports of neurological symptoms caused by a skewing of XCI in females with heterozygous pathogenic variants in CNKSR2. However, this case was more severe than the previously reported female cases, and the skewing of XCI was more pronounced. There is a strong possibility that the severity of this condition in women is correlates with the skewing of XCI.

en: Current Status of Germline BRCA1/2 Testing in Patients with Pancreatic Cancer at a Regional University Hospital
ja: 地域大学病院における膵がん患者の生殖細胞系列BRCA1/2検査の現状
abs: Background: BRACAnalysis, a germline BRCA1/2 genetic test, became covered by the national health insurance system in Japan for pancreatic cancer as a companion diagnostic for Olaparib. We investigated the current status of BRACAnalysis in pancreatic cancer patients. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed pancreatic cancer patients who underwent BRACAnalysis at Tokushima University Hospital between March 2021 and April 2026. We evaluated the timing of BRACAnalysis, pathogenic variants, and clinical outcomes. This study was approved by the ethics committee of Tokushima University Hospital (No. 3095). Results: BRACAnalysis was performed in 25 patients. Testing was conducted during first-line chemotherapy in 21 patients, second-line chemotherapy in 2 patients, and third-line chemotherapy in 2 patients. Pathogenic BRCA variants were identified in 3 patients, all of whom harbored BRCA2 pathogenic variants. All patients had a family history of pancreatic cancer. Olaparib was administered in 2 patients. Two patients died 9 and 19 months after diagnosis, whereas 1 patient remains alive 42 months after diagnosis. In the surviving patient, mFOLFIRINOX achieved a partial response, followed by Olaparib treatment and conversion surgery, resulting in recurrence-free survival. Conclusions: BRACAnalysis identified pathogenic BRCA2 variants in 12% of pancreatic cancer patients. Early implementation of BRACAnalysis and appropriate use of Olaparib and platinum-based chemotherapy may improve outcomes in patients with BRCA1/2 pathogenic variants.

en: Lynch Syndrome Associated with Diffuse Glioma and Co-existence of Germline Variants in MLH1 and ATM
ja: びまん性神経膠腫を伴うLynch症候群とMLH1・ATM生殖細胞系列バリアントの共存
abs: Introduction: Lynch syndrome (LS) is caused by germline variants in DNA mismatch repair (MMR) genes and is associated with various malignancies. Gliomas are the most common brain tumors associated with LS, and recent reports suggest the efficacy of the immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) in tumors with a high tumor mutation burden (TMB). The majority of LS cases are attributed to germline variants in either MLH1 or MSH2; however, cases with concomitant germline variants in other DNA repair genes have also been reported. Case Presentation: A male patient with a family history of LS with germline MLH1 variant in his mother. At 26 years of age, he underwent surgery of brain tumor, which was pathologically diagnosed as anaplastic oligodendroglioma. At 49 years of age, surgery was performed for a newly developed brain tumor, which was pathologically diagnosed as high-grade glioma. In the same year, he was diagnosed with transverse colon cancer and subsequently underwent surgery for a cerebellar tumor, which was pathologically diagnosed as glioblastoma. A comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) using GenMineTOP performed on the cerebellar tumor specimen revealed TMB-high status (81.2 mut/Mb). Pembrolizumab treatment was administered; however, no therapeutic response was observed, and the patient died 6 weeks later. Secondary findings from the CGP identified germline variants in both MLH1 and ATM. Discussion: ATM is a well-known DNA repair gene. Further investigation is warranted regarding both the prevalence of such cases and their responsiveness to immune checkpoint inhibitors.

en: Lynch Syndrome Identified After Endometrial Cancer in a Patient with Prior Rectal and Subsequent Sigmoid Cancer
ja: 直腸がん・S状結腸がんの既往後に子宮体がんを契機に同定されたLynch症候群
abs: [Introduction] Lynch syndrome (LS) is an autosomal dominant hereditary disorder caused by pathogenic variants in DNA mismatch repair (MMR) genes, significantly increasing the risk for colorectal (CRC) and endometrial cancers (EC). We report a case of LS diagnosed via genetic testing after EC treatment in a patient with early-onset CRC, which subsequently led to detecting metachronous sigmoid colon cancer. [Case Report] A 50s female with a history of rectal cancer at age 29 had undergone regular colonoscopies and multiple endoscopic resections for polyps. Her father had CRC at age 34 and died of gastric cancer at 45. At age 48, she was diagnosed with EC and underwent hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and pelvic/para-aortic lymphadenectomy. Pathology showed Grade 2 endometrioid carcinoma, Stage IB (pT1bN0M0). Postoperatively, she received six cycles of adjuvant chemotherapy with paclitaxel and carboplatin. Given her clinical history, MMR protein immunohistochemistry (IHC) showed a loss of MLH1 and PMS2 expression. Following genetic counseling, a pathogenic variant in the MLH1 gene was identified, confirming LS. One year later, surveillance colonoscopy identified early sigmoid colon cancer within a polyp, which was managed by laparoscopic total colectomy and ileo-lower proctostomy in our Hospital. [Conclusion] In gynecology, EC and ovarian cancer are key sentinel indicators for LS diagnosis. Clinicians must prioritize not only proband treatment and surveillance but also strategies for the early detection and prevention of cancer in at-risk relatives.

en: Identification of a novel pathogenic variant of gastric adenocarcinoma and proximal polyposis of the stomach (GAPPS)
ja: 胃腺がん・近位胃ポリポーシス（GAPPS）の新規病的バリアントの同定
abs: <Background> GAPPS is an autosomal dominant genetic disorder predispose to development of proximal gastric polyposis, that is associated with a high risk dysplasia and gastric adenocarcinoma. Several pathogenic variants for GAPPS in the APC promoter 1B region have already been identified. <Patient> A 50 years old male patient who developed a proximal gastric polyposis at the age of 35, who has a family history of gastric cancer in his mother and maternal aunt, and gastric polyposis in his sister at 37 years old. Moreover, his cousin has diagnosed as clinically GAPPS(PP$). <Method> We conducted a panel sequencing of genes relative to the gastrointestinal cancer-polyposis syndromes. For functional analysis, we constructed luciferase reporter constructs driven by a 500 bp fragment of APC promoter 1B region harboring a wild type or variants and examined the promoter activities in DLD-1 cells. <Results> We identified a novel variant, APC(NM_001127511.2):c.-195A>T located within the APC promoter 1B region in the proband. This variant is not registered at gnomAD nor ToMMo jMorp 61KJPN datebases (PM2). A promoter activity was reduced to 63.5% compared to those of the WT variant and was comparable to the established pathogenic variant for GAPPS, c.-191T>C (PS1). Sanger sequencing demonstrated the proband's sister also possessed this novel variant, while his healthy brother did not (PP1). <Consideration> According to the ACMG/AMP guidelines, we classified this novel variant as likely pathogenic. The functional analysis was key evidence for a proper classification of the variant.

en: Establishing a Clinical System for Unaffected HBOC Relatives under Japan's 2026 Medical Fee Revision
ja: 2026年診療報酬改定下でのHBOC未発症血縁者の診療体制構築
abs: Background: Japan's 2026 medical fee revision expanded insurance coverage for HBOC care, including BRCA1/2 testing for unaffected first-degree relatives and subsequent risk-management services such as RRSO, RRM, and breast MRI surveillance. Objective: To report the streamlined clinical system established at our institution to accept eligible relatives. Methods: We adopted a mainstreaming approach and developed a pathway linking the Department of Breast Oncology, the Risk Assessment Unit, and the Regional Medical Liaison Office. Breast oncologists provide dedicated outpatient slots, standardized pre-test information, and test ordering, while genetics professionals support complex counseling, interpretation of results, and post-test decision-making. Referrals are centralized through the liaison office, and eligibility checklists, referral forms, patient information sheets, and web-based guidance have been prepared. Results: An operational intake system was established. The pathway clarifies referral routes, initial explanation and testing, timing of genetics involvement, and access to result disclosure and risk management. This structure is expected to reduce confusion, distribute workload beyond genetics-only access points, and enable smooth acceptance of eligible relatives. Conclusion: The 2026 medical fee revision requires not only expanded coverage but also institutional redesign to transition HBOC care from special to standard. Our experience illustrates one practical approach to implementing HBOC care for unaffected relatives in routine oncology practice.

en: Retrospective Analysis of the Timing of Risk-Reducing Salpingo-Oophorectomy in Women With BRCA1/2 Pathogenic Variants
ja: BRCA1/2病的バリアント保持女性におけるリスク低減卵管卵巣摘出術の時期の後方視的解析
abs: Background: Risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy (RRSO) reduces ovarian and fallopian tube cancer risk in women with BRCA1/2 pathogenic variants, but factors influencing RRSO uptake and timing in Japan remain unclear. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 70 women with BRCA1/2 pathogenic variants who received genetic counseling at Nagasaki University Hospital from 2013 to 2025. Clinical factors associated with RRSO uptake and with RRSO within 365 days after genetic testing were evaluated using logistic regression. Time to RRSO was also assessed by Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression. Results: The mean age was 47.8 years; 55 patients had breast cancer. BRCA1 and BRCA2 variants were identified in 26 and 44 patients, respectively. Overall, 32 patients underwent RRSO, giving an uptake rate of 45.7%. RRSO was covered by public insurance in 29 patients. Multivariable analysis showed that age >45 years and breast cancer history were significantly associated with RRSO uptake. Among patients who underwent RRSO, BRCA1 carriers were more likely than BRCA2 carriers to undergo surgery within 365 days after genetic testing. Kaplan-Meier analysis also showed a shorter median time to RRSO in BRCA1 carriers. The main reasons for not undergoing RRSO were young age or no cancer onset, and ongoing breast cancer treatment. Conclusion: Older age and breast cancer history were associated with RRSO uptake, while BRCA1 status was associated with earlier surgery. Individualized counseling and longitudinal support are essential for informed and timely RRSO decision-making.

en: Clinical MEN1 Without an Identifiable Germline MEN1 Variant: Phenocopy or Undetected Hereditary Disease
ja: 生殖細胞系列MEN1バリアントが同定されない臨床的MEN1：フェノコピーか未検出の遺伝性疾患か
abs: Background) MEN1 is diagnosed either by identifying a pathogenic MEN1 variant or clinically by the presence of tumors in at least two of the parathyroid, pituitary, and pancreas. However, the interpretation of variant negative cases remains controversial. Case Presentation) A woman in her 60s with recurrent urolithiasis was referred for hypercalcemia and elevated iPTH levels. Ultrasonography suggested enlargement of the left inferior parathyroid gland, and 99Tc-MIBI scintigraphy showed abnormal uptake in both the left lower neck and right thyroid region, suggesting multiglandular parathyroid disease. Further endocrine evaluation at a referral center revealed a growth hormone secreting pituitary adenoma causing acromegaly. Based on the coexistence of PHPT and a pituitary adenoma, she fulfilled the clinical diagnostic criteria for MEN1. Genetic testing was performed, but no MEN1 variant was identified. Discussion) Approximately 5-10% of clinically diagnosed MEN1 patients have no detectable MEN1 variant. Possible explanations include phenocopies, pathogenic variants in other MEN1 related genes such as CDKN1B, or mosaic MEN1. Mutation negative patients are generally older at diagnosis and less likely to develop pancreatic NEN and multiple parathyroid tumors. Considering these characteristics, in this case makes a simple phenocopy difficult to conclude. This case highlights the limitations of current germline testing and emphasizes the importance of integrating clinical phenotypes with genetic findings when managing suspected hereditary endocrine tumor syndromes.

en: A Presumed Germline STK11 Pathogenic Variant identified by CGP in a Young Patient with Advanced Breast Cancer
ja: 進行乳がんの若年患者でCGPにより同定された生殖細胞系列由来と推定されるSTK11病的バリアント
abs: Background Comprehensive genomic profiling may identify presumed germline pathogenic variants in addition to somatic alterations. However, the clinical handling of such findings can be challenging in patients with advanced cancer, particularly when the patient's condition, treatment course, and family circumstances must be considered. Case and Clinical Course A 35-year-old woman was diagnosed with breast cancer at the age of 32 and received multimodal therapy. She subsequently developed lymph node recurrence and continued systemic treatment. BRACAnalysisR identified a germline BRCA1 pathogenic variant, and olaparib was administered. During fourth-line therapy, FoundationOneR CDx detected a frameshift variant in STK11, which was reported as a presumed germline pathogenic variant. The patient had a minor child, and the result had potential implications for her relatives. The CGP result, including the presumed germline finding, was disclosed to the patient and her mother. However, as her disease progressed, she required repeated hospitalizations, and confirmatory germline testing could not be pursued. She died 3 years and 10 months after the initial diagnosis. Conclusion This case illustrates the complexity of managing presumed germline pathogenic variants identified by CGP in patients with advanced cancer. Even when disclosure is performed, confirmatory testing and subsequent genetic counseling may be limited by disease progression and family circumstances. Flexible and context-sensitive approaches are needed when addressing presumed germline findings in advanced cancer care.

en: Expected Roles of Our Cancer Genetic Services: Review of Community Liaison Office Referrals
ja: 当院がん遺伝外来に期待される役割：地域連携室紹介例の検討
abs: Background: Our hospital established a genetic counseling clinic in 2012 and began accepting external referrals in 2019. We evaluated referrals coordinated through the Community Liaison Office to clarify the role of our cancer genetic services. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed clients referred through the Community Liaison Office between April 2019 and March 2026. Reasons for referral, genetic testing, and subsequent management were analyzed. Results: During the study period, 197 clients were referred, accounting for 379 genetic counseling sessions and 118 genetic tests (16%, 15%, and 11% of total clinic activity, respectively). HBOC testing was the most common test (86 cases, 73%), followed by MGPT (14 cases, 12%) and other genetic tests (18 cases, 15%). Sixty clients (30%) had already received a genetic diagnosis elsewhere and were referred mainly for consultation regarding risk-reducing surgery and management of at-risk relatives. Conclusions: Although hereditary cancer testing has become widely available, comprehensive post-test management remains limited. Thirty percent of referrals involved clients already diagnosed elsewhere, indicating a regional need for specialized services, including risk-reducing interventions and management of at-risk relatives. Referrals are expected to increase as insurance coverage expands for testing of relatives. Continued demand for self-funded testing, surveillance, and risk-reducing interventions highlights the need to strengthen cancer genetic services.

en: Hereditary tumor treatment system in an emergency hospital with no prior experience of genetic medicine
ja: 遺伝医療の経験がない救急病院における遺伝性腫瘍診療体制
abs: Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer Syndrome (HBOC) treatment has rapidly spread nationwide since 2020. But significant institutional disparities remain. Two years ago, we started providing breast cancer (BC) treatment and genetic counseling (GC) at the emergency hospital with the highest number of ambulance arrivals in the prefecture, with no previous experience in GC. This paper outlines the development and status of a hereditary tumor care system in our hospital. Weekly hereditary tumor clinic has been established by a clinical geneticist specializing in BC. Ovarian cancer surveillance and risk-reducing salpingo oophorectomy were referred to another institution, and risk-reducing mastectomy (RRM) was started at our hospital. 70 BC patients received GC and 67 underwent BRCA genetic testing (GT) (62 for diagnosis, 5 as a CDX for olaparib). Of the 62 for diagnosis, 23 were ≤ 45 years old, 12 had TNBC ≤ 60, 14 had multiple breast cancers and 36 had a family history of HBOC-related cancers. Pathogenic variants (PV) of BRCA1 /2 were detected in 6. 2 of them decided to undergo a contralateral RRM during surgery for BC. One received olaparib. Even emergency hospitals without prior experience in GC were able to establish a system for treating HBOC rapidly by a clinical geneticist. The results of GT were used to reduce the mortality risk through surveillance, risk-reducing surgery, and olaparib administration. However, only 3 have utilized MGPT, and only 2 have received GC for cancers other than breast cancer. To further promote genetic medicine, awareness education is necessary.

en: BCCR/OCCR-Based Risk Stratification in BRCA Pathogenic Variant Carriers: A Single-Institution Analysis
ja: BRCA病的バリアント保持者におけるBCCR/OCCRに基づくリスク層別化：単一施設解析
abs: Background: Breast/ovarian cancer cluster regions (BCCRs/OCCRs), defined by Kuchenbaecker et al. (JAMA 2015), are BRCA1/2 genomic segments with differentially elevated organ-specific cancer risks. However, major guidelines including NCCN do not recommend cluster region-based management stratification. Methods: Among 301 individuals undergoing BRCA testing at our institution (September 2018-January 2025), 31 PV-positive carriers were identified (BRCA1: n=19, BRCA2: n=12). PVs were annotated by BCCR/OCCR framework. BCCRs: BRCA1 c.179-505 (BCCR1), c.4328-4945 (BCCR2); BRCA2 c.772-1806 (BCCR1'), c.7394-8904 (BCCR2). OCCRs: BRCA1 c.1380-4062; BRCA2 c.3249-5681 (OCCR1), c.6645-7471 (OCCR2). Surveillance and risk-reducing surgery (RRM/ RRSO) were reviewed. Results: 8 carriers (26%) had BCCR variants (5 types: BRCA1 BCCR1 c.188T-A [n=4], BRCA1 BCCR2 c.4485-2A-G [n=1], BRCA2 BCCR1' c.933G-T [n=1], c.1013del [n=1], BRCA2 BCCR2 c.7954dup [n=1]). 13 (42%) had OCCR variants (8 types: BRCA1 OCCR c.2800C-T [n=2], c.1931del [n=2], c.2269del [n=2], c.3038_3040delinsGAAG [n=1], c.2389_2390del [n=1], c.3397_3398del [n=1]; BRCA2 OCCR2 c.6952C-T [n=2], c.7187del [n=2]). 10 had non-cluster variants. RRSO was more frequent in OCCR carriers; however, cluster region-based counseling was not systematically differentiated. Conclusion: 68% of PV carriers harbored BCCR or OCCR variants. Mutation location-aware counseling - enhanced breast surveillance/RRM for BCCR carriers and proactive RRSO for OCCR carriers - may enable more individualized HBOC management beyond gene-level distinction.

en: Current Status and Challenges of BRCA Genetic Testing in Breast, Ovarian, Prostate, and Pancreatic Cancer
ja: 乳がん・卵巣がん・前立腺がん・膵がんにおけるBRCA遺伝学的検査の現状と課題
abs: Background: Following the expansion of insurance coverage for BRCA genetic testing in Japan, the number of patients undergoing testing has increased, leading to a growing number of families diagnosed with hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (HBOC). We reviewed the current status of BRCA genetic testing at our institution. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 233 patients with breast, ovarian, prostate, or pancreatic cancer who underwent BRCA genetic testing at our institution between October 2018 and April 2026. Results: Of the 233 patients, 155 had breast cancer, 9 ovarian cancer, 44 prostate cancer, and 25 pancreatic cancer. Pathogenic BRCA variants were identified in 27 patients. BRCA1 pathogenic variants were detected in 12 patients (9 breast cancers, 2 ovarian cancers, and 1 pancreatic cancer), and BRCA2 pathogenic variants in 15 patients (11 breast cancers, 2 ovarian cancers, 1 prostate cancer, and 1 pancreatic cancer). Three breast cancer patients had variants of uncertain significance (VUS). Genetic counseling was provided to 10 patients. Two families subsequently received genetic counseling, and genetic testing of relatives was confirmed in one family. Conclusions: Differences in testing practices and surveillance were observed among departments. Closer collaboration is needed to ensure appropriate access to BRCA genetic testing. Establishing follow-up systems for pathogenic variant carriers and their relatives remains an important challenge.

en: Efficacy of PARP inhibitors for patients with BRCA2c.5576_5579del variants; retrospective study at single institution
ja: BRCA2 c.5576_5579delバリアント患者に対するPARP阻害薬の有効性：単一施設後方視的研究
abs: Background: Few reports have described differences in clinical behavior among BRCA1/2 variants, and the efficacy of PARP inhibitors by genotype has rarely been studied. No reports exist on PARP inhibitor efficacy in carriers of the BRCA2 c.5576_5579del variant(KAKO variant), which is common in the Kansai region, particularly Hyogo Prefecture. Methods: In this retrospective study using our hospital's Genetic Counseling Department database, we compared PARP inhibitor efficacy between carriers of the KAKO variant and patients with other genotypes. Results: We analyzed 298 patients: 224 tested for BRCA1/2 at our hospital between 2013 and 2025 with confirmed pathogenic variants, and 74 referred after confirmation elsewhere. KAKO variant accounted for 44 cases (14.8%) and was the most common variant in both BRCA2 and BRCA1/2 overall. Excluding relatives, 218 associated cancers were diagnosed: 120 breast, 84 ovarian, 8 prostate, 5 pancreatic, and 1 of unknown primary. PARP inhibitors were prescribed to 91 patients (olaparib 80, niraparib 6, rucaparib 2, veliparib 3). By genotype, 42 had BRCA1 and 49 had BRCA2 (including 8 with KAKO variant). The median PARP inhibitor duration was 12 months (range 0-72): 12 for BRCA1 and 13 for BRCA2 (8 for KAKO variant vs 19 for other BRCA2 variants). Discussion: Treatment duration was longest for other BRCA2 variants, followed by BRCA1, and shortest for KAKO variant. Because PARP inhibitor duration is strongly influenced by cancer type and treatment setting, further investigation is warranted.

en: Identification of a Germline PALB2 Pathogenic Variant by Multigene Panel Testing in a Young Woman with Breast Cancer
ja: 若年乳がん女性で多遺伝子パネル検査により同定された生殖細胞系列PALB2病的バリアント
abs: Background: Breast cancer diagnosed before 30 years of age strongly suggests an inherited cancer predisposition. Although TP53 testing is often prioritized because of its association with Li-Fraumeni syndrome, multigene panel testing (MGPT) may identify pathogenic variants in other susceptibility genes. Case Presentation: A woman in her 20s presented with a right breast mass and was diagnosed with luminal HER2 type breast cancer. She was referred to our institution for treatment. Because of her young age at diagnosis, BRCA1/2 genetic testing was performed and was negative. She was subsequently referred for genetic counseling. Although no remarkable family history of hereditary cancer was identified, hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes were suspected because of the early onset of disease. While TP53 testing would generally be prioritized in a patient diagnosed before 30 years of age, MGPT was selected to evaluate a broader range of cancer susceptibility genes. A pathogenic PALB2 variant, c.3350+5G>A (NM_024675.3), was identified. Functional studies have demonstrated that this variant causes exon skipping (from 11 to 12) , resulting in loss of PALB2 function. Current NCCN Guidelines estimate the lifetime breast cancer risk for PALB2 pathogenic variant carriers from 32% to 53%. Conclusion: MGPT identified a germline PALB2 pathogenic variant in a young woman with breast cancer despite negative BRCA1/2 testing. This case highlights the clinical utility of MGPT in early-onset breast cancer and its value in detecting actionable pathogenic variants beyond TP53 and BRCA1/2.

en: Transcriptome Analysis of HBV-related Hepatocellular Carcinoma Using Long-read Sequencing
ja: ロングリードシーケンスを用いたHBV関連肝細胞がんのトランスクリプトーム解析
abs: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a highly heterogeneous malignancy, and many aspects of hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related hepatocarcinogenesis remain poorly understood. In particular, the relationship between carcinogenesis and gene expression in HCC has not been fully elucidated. Comprehensive analysis of full-length transcripts may reveal novel gene expression patterns associated with HBV-related HCC. We performed long-read RNA-seq of 114 HCC and 72 nontumor liver tissues using the Oxford Nanopore. Analysis of the resulting data identified and quantified 52,997 transcripts, including 8,368 novel transcripts, providing a comprehensive view of the HCC transcriptome. HBV-derived transcripts were detected in 119 samples (64%), including fusion transcripts between HBV and host genes such as fibronectin and cyclin family genes. Differential expression analysis identified 7,956 upregulated and 3,513 downregulated genes. Notably, 1,036 differentially expressed genes were detected only at the transcript level, indicating that isoform-resolved analysis can uncover novel HCC-associated genes that are missed by conventional gene-level approaches. To identify novel genes involved in HCC pathogenesis, we conducted a knockdown screen of 18 differentially expressed genes in HepG2 and Huh-7. Knockdown of several candidates significantly inhibited cell proliferation, whereas overexpression enhanced proliferation. Further characterization of these candidates will provide insights into the biological functions and molecular mechanisms of novel driver genes involved in the HCC development.

en: Case report of a breast cancer patient with the BRCA2 p.Ser2616Phe variant
ja: BRCA2 p.Ser2616Pheバリアントを有する乳がん患者の症例報告
abs: BACKGROUND: It has been suggested that the BRCA2 p.Ser2616Phe variant may be a likely pathogenic variant specific to the Japanese population. We report a case of breast cancer with this variant. CASE: A 57-year-old woman with no significant past medical history. Family history of gastric cancer (father, died at age 37). She visited our hospital following an abnormal screening result and was diagnosed with bilateral breast cancer after further evaluation. During preoperative chemotherapy, a BRACAnalysis was performed, which identified this variant in BRCA2; this was classified as a VUS. ClinVar lists this as a 'Conflicting classification of pathogenicity.' After discussion during genetic counseling, the management strategy was determined. Breasts: Among the options of (1)bilateral mastectomy or (2)partial resection followed by breast surveillance, option (1) was selected. Ovaries and fallopian tubes: If RRSO is desired, the plan is to consider performing it as self-pay treatment following ethical review. Genetic testing for relatives: Testing is available upon request. DISCUSSION: This variant has been reported in Japanese patients with breast or ovarian cancer, and in silico functional analyses suggest a high likelihood of pathogenicity. Furthermore, while the allele frequency is reported in the Japanese ToMMo38KJPN database, it is not reported in gnomAD, TopMed, HGVD, or other databases. Since ethnicity-specific variants are also found in genes associated with hereditary tumors, measures are needed to ensure that variants specific to the Japanese population are not overlooked.

en: Clinicopathological Study of Patients Who Underwent Risk-Reducing Salpingo-Oophorectomy for HBOC
ja: HBOCに対しリスク低減卵管卵巣摘出術を受けた患者の臨床病理学的検討
abs: Objective: This study aimed to investigate the clinicopathological factors and outcomes of patients with hereditary breast and ovarian cancer who underwent risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy . Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 22 patients who underwent RRSO at our hospital between April 2021 and March 2026. Data extracted from medical records included age at HBOC diagnosis and surgery, pathogenic variants, history and family history of breast cancer, concurrent risk-reducing mastectomy, parity, surgical procedure, and histopathological findings. Results: The median age at HBOC diagnosis was 51 years (range: 32-68), and the median interval from diagnosis to RRSO was 19 months (range: 3-128). The median age at surgery was 52.5 years (range: 41-68). 8 patients carried BRCA1 pathogenic variants, and 14 carried BRCA2 pathogenic variants. A history of breast cancer was present in 21 patients. No concurrent RRM was performed, while concurrent total hysterectomy was performed in 6 patients (27.3%). In one case, ovarian cancer was suspected intraoperatively, leading to primary debulking surgery following frozen section examination. Histopathological evaluation using the SEE-FIM protocol revealed serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma in one case (4.5%). Conclusion: Although no unaffected individuals underwent self-funded RRSO at our hospital due to financial barriers, the FY2026 medical fee revision has expanded insurance coverage for HBOC medical care to include first-degree relatives under specific criteria. This change is expected to broaden options for high-risk individuals.

en: Cases of Pregnancy Following In Vitro Fertilization in Patients with HBOC Toward Empathetic Genetic Counseling
ja: HBOC患者の体外受精後妊娠例：共感的な遺伝カウンセリングに向けて
abs: Introduction When individuals with HBOC develop cancer at a young age, it is not uncommon for this to coincide with their reproductive years. However, there are few case reports in Japan regarding HBOC patients who have undergone in vitro fertilisation. We report on our experience providing genetic counselling for a case of HBOC related breast cancer in which pregnancy was achieved. Case Report The patient developed breast cancer in her thirties. Preoperative chemotherapy was administered. During genetic counselling, the option of fertility preservation was also discussed. Subsequently, the AYA Support Team became involved, and it was decided that egg retrieval and freezing would be carried out at another hospital. Chemotherapy was administered following the egg retrieval. A pathogenic BRCA2 variant was subsequently detected. A total mastectomy was performed, and during post operative genetic counselling, the patient said through tears, While I was in hospital, the doctor told me, you can not possibly have children. I was so sad. I wondered if it had all been in vain. Following hormone therapy, she took a break from treatment and subsequently became pregnant. Conclusion Patients with hereditary tumours experience significant stress as they must simultaneously consider their cancer diagnosis, disclosure of the hereditary tumour, and concerns regarding fertility. The medical team must prioritise the patient`s life above all else and provide support that is sensitive to their personal outlook on life.

en: A Case of Breast Cancer in a Patient with a History of Retinoblastoma
ja: 網膜芽細胞腫の既往を有する患者の乳がんの1例
abs: It has been noted that hereditary retinoblastoma is associated with an increased risk of secondary malignancies, including breast cancer. Patients with hereditary retinoblastoma are highly sensitive to radiation, and it is recommended that they avoid radiation exposure. Because the diagnosis and treatment of malignant tumors carry a high risk of radiation exposure, special consideration is required when performing examinations and treatments. We report a case of breast cancer in an adult woman with a history of right retinoblastoma in childhood. Genetic testing of the Rb1 gene suggested a somatic mosaic with a mutation arising during the early embryonic two cell stage. We discuss breast cancer in hereditary retinoblastoma, including considerations for diagnosis and treatment. The patient is a woman in her 30s. She has a history of right retinal blastoma. There is a family history of pancreatic cancer on her maternal grandmother side. She was referred to our hospital due to a lump in her right breast and was diagnosed with right breast cancer, cT3N2bM0, Stage 3A, estrogen receptor positive, progesterone receptor negative, and HER2 negative. MRI was used for the systemic examination. She underwent preoperative chemotherapy, surgery, postoperative radiation therapy, and medical therapy.

en: Surveillance Initiatives and Challenges for Asymptomatic Relatives of Patients with Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer
ja: 遺伝性乳がん卵巣がん患者の無症状血縁者に対するサーベイランスの取り組みと課題
abs: Background and Objectives Following the 2026 revision of medical fees in Japan, genetic testing and surveillance for asymptomatic relatives of HBOC patients became covered by national health insurance. This requires more efficient follow-up systems. We evaluated surveillance practices at our institution and identified future challenges. Methods We retrospectively reviewed asymptomatic relatives of individuals with confirmed HBOC who underwent genetic counseling between April 2019 and April 2026. Genetic test results and surveillance status were analyzed. Results Twenty-eight relatives were included (6 males, 22 females; median age 39.5 years). HBOC was identified at our hospital in 22 cases (4 of whom were participants in our department of surgery study) and at other institutions in 6 cases. Pathogenic variants were BRCA1 (n = 15) and BRCA2 (n = 13). Surveillance was initiated at our hospital and continued either locally or at other facilities. Genetic counseling was provided alongside surveillance. Of the 28 individuals, 23 (82.1%) continued surveillance, 3 (10.7%) did not initiate, and 2 (7.1%) transferred care. Reasons for non-initiation included younger age (n = 2) and patient preference (n = 1). Discussion High adherence may reflect centralized management and annual consultations. However, increasing numbers of identified carriers under insurance coverage may exceed the capacity of specialized centers. Collaboration with regional providers will be essential for sustainable surveillance.

en: Current Status and Challenges of Cancer Panel Testing at Our Hospital-Focusing on Gene Mine TOP-
ja: 当院におけるがん遺伝子パネル検査の現状と課題：Gene Mine TOPを中心に
abs: [Background and Objectives] In recent years, genomic cancer medicine has become increasingly widespread. While our hospital offers several testing panels, we currently use three main panels: Foundation One CDx (F1CDx), Foundation One Liquid (F1Liquid), and GenMineTop. This study focuses on GenMineTop - a test using paired tumor and normal tissue samples that became eligible for National Health Insurance coverage in August 2023- intending to retrospectively evaluate its current status at our hospital and contribute to the future advancement of genetic medicine. [Subjects and Methods] We analyzed 63 cases (41 men and 22 women) who underwent GenMineTop testing at our hospital between July 2024 and April 2026. We compared the GPV detection rate and gene distribution with C- CAT data reported by Habano et al. [Results] The median age was 57 years for both men and women (men: 25-83 years, women: 7-80 years). Central nervous system tumors, including glioblastoma and glioma, accounted for 37 cases (approximately 60%). The next most common were gallbladder and bile duct cancers, with 10 cases (approximately 16%). The GPV detection rate was 4 cases (6.3%), but none of these patients requested genetic counseling. [Discussion] One possible reason for the lack of referrals for genetic counseling was that patients with central nervous system tumors may have found it difficult to understand their own condition and test results.

en: Integrative genomic and transcriptomic analysis identifies BAX as a regulator of disease progression in prostate cancer
ja: 統合ゲノム・トランスクリプトーム解析が前立腺がん進行の制御因子としてBAXを同定
abs: Clinical outcomes following androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) in prostate cancer vary considerably. Because endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress mediates apoptosis and tumor adaptation, we investigated associations between ER stress‒related genetic variants and overall survival (OS) in patients receiving ADT. This multicenter study enrolled 630 prostate cancer patients undergoing ADT across three Taiwanese medical centers. We analyzed 89 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) across 12 ER stress–related genes, utilizing Kaplan–Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models to evaluate prognostic associations. Public databases were also integrated for expression, gene set enrichment, and immune infiltration analyses. Among the analyzed SNPs, BAX rs182509214 demonstrated the strongest association with OS; its minor G allele significantly correlated with poorer OS. Prostate tumors exhibited elevated BAX expression compared to normal tissues, predicting worse survival outcomes. Functionally, BAX-associated genes were predominantly enriched in ribosomal, oxidative phosphorylation, and proteasomal pathways. Additionally, BAX expression negatively correlated with CD8+ T-cell infiltration, indicating a regulatory impact on the tumor immune microenvironment. Ultimately, the ER stress–related variant BAX rs182509214 influences OS in prostate cancer patients undergoing ADT. BAX may drive disease progression by modulating mitochondrial metabolism and the immune microenvironment, emerging as a potential prognostic biomarker that warrants broader validation in larger cohorts.

en: Detection of Leukemia-Associated Structural Variants Using Electronic Genome Mapping Technology
ja: 電子ゲノムマッピング技術を用いた白血病関連構造多型の検出
abs: Structural variants (SVs) are frequently associated with adverse outcomes in hematologic malignancies. Detection remains challenging in clinical laboratories due to limitations of conventional cytogenetics and molecular methods. Reliable identification of these SVs is crucial for improving risk stratification and guiding treatment. Electronic genome mapping (EGM), a solid-state nanochannel-based platform, was used to detect SVs and copy number variants (CNVs) associated with leukemia in 11 cell lines. High molecular weight DNA was extracted, processed with a dual-enzyme workflow, and analyzed on the OhmX™ Platform. SVs were detected using Human Chromosome Explorer® de novo assembly, SV- Verify™, a targeted, alignment-based variant detection application, and CNV analysis pipeline. Variants were confirmed with orthogonal techniques such as sequencing, OGM, and CMA. EGM accurately detected TP53 deletions ranging from 3.8–87 kb, an inv(3) leading to a MECOM rearrangement, a 22.3 kb KMT2A-PTD, an 848 kb deletion forming FILIP1: PDGFRA, a microRNA cluster deletion of miR-15a/16-1, as well as gene fusions such as BCR::ABL1, PML::RARA, and RUNX1::RUNX1T1. These results were resolved with high concordance to published data and orthogonal techniques. We demonstrated EGM’s capability to detect various classes of SVs and CNVs associated with hematological malignancies, complementing traditional cytogenetic and molecular technologies. The cost-effectiveness, precision, and throughput of EGM using the OhmX Platform make it a strong candidate for integration into hematopathology workflows.

en: Comparison of Quality Control Status Groups in Cancer Genomic Profiling Testing at a Community Hospital.
ja: 市中病院のがんゲノムプロファイリング検査における品質管理ステータス群の比較
abs: Background: Quality control (QC) in cancer genomic profiling (CGP) testing is essential for identifying optimal therapeutic strategies; however, few studies have evaluated how QC outcomes affect CGP results in routine community hospital practice. We compared clinicopathological and genomic characteristics between QC status groups. Methods: Fifty-three patients who underwent FoundationOne CDx testing were analyzed. Differences between QC groups (Pass vs. Qualified) were evaluated by comparing tumor cell content, tumor purity estimated from CGP data, sequencing depth, number of short variants, variant allele frequency (VAF), and tumor mutational burden (TMB). The relationship between histological tumor cell content (% tumor nuclei, %TN) and tumor purity was also examined. Results: Of 53 cases, 44 were Pass and 9 Qualified. The Pass group showed significantly higher %TN (36.8% vs. 27.2%, p=0.008) and tumor purity (52.8% vs. 17.1%, p<0.001). Mean exon depth and median exon coverage did not differ significantly. The number of short variants (10.6 vs. 7.1, p=0.019) and TMB (4.44 vs. 0.81 mut/Mb, p<0.001) were significantly higher in the Pass group, whereas mean VAF showed no significant difference. Tumor purity predicted QC Pass status with an AUC of 0.962 and an optimal cutoff of 28.7%. %TN moderately correlated with tumor purity. Conclusions: Histological tumor cell content is important for achieving QC Pass status in FoundationOne CDx testing.

en: Clinical Spectrum of SCA17 and SCA17-DI in Japan
ja: 日本におけるSCA17とSCA17-DIの臨床スペクトラム
abs: Background and Objectives: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 17 (SCA17) is a rare autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder caused by CAG/CAA repeat expansion in TBP. Digenic TBP/STUB1-related SCA17 (SCA17-DI) has recently been proposed. However, their clinical spectrum in Japanese patients remains insufficiently characterized. We investigated clinical and genetic characteristics of patients with SCA17 and SCA17-DI. Methods: We reviewed clinical and genetic data of patients diagnosed with SCA17 or SCA17-DI registered in J-CAT. Results: Six patients were identified, including 3 with SCA17 and 3 with SCA17-DI. Among SCA17 patients, TBP repeat lengths ranged from 48 to 54 repeats. Age at onset ranged from 20 to 50 years. Clinical manifestations were heterogeneous and included cerebellar ataxia, cognitive impairment, dystonia, and parkinsonism. Among SCA17-DI patients, TBP repeat lengths ranged from 45 to 46 repeats and all harbored pathogenic STUB1 variants. Age at onset ranged from 36 to 43 years. Cerebellar ataxia, cognitive impairment, parkinsonism, tremor, and sensory disturbance were observed. Family history suggestive of autosomal dominant inheritance was present in 5 patients. Brain MRI demonstrated cerebellar atrophy in all 6 patients. Discussion and Conclusion: Japanese patients with SCA17 and SCA17-DI exhibited heterogeneous but overlapping clinical manifestations. These findings highlight the importance of comprehensive genetic evaluation, including both TBP repeat and STUB1 variant analyses, in patients with adult-onset cerebellar ataxia and SCA17-like phenotypes.

en: A long-term follow up of a Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease caused by a rare mutation
ja: 稀な変異によるCharcot-Marie-Tooth病の長期経過観察
abs: A long-term follow up of a case with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease caused by a rare mutation is presented. The patient is a 75 years-old female subject with a long history of weakness in all extremities. She first noticed a gradual wasting at her lower legs when she was 40. When she became 50, she could only walk by using cane, and she also felt numbness on her feet and weaknesses in hand and fingers. Neurological examination at the age of 52 disclosed bilateral, distal dominant weakness in 4 extremities. Electrophysiological tests revealed severe sensory and motor axonal neuropathy. Sural nerve biopsy disclosed severe loss of myelinated fibers with thickening of myelin in remaining nerves. A diagnosis of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease was made. The patient also had bilateral sensory healing loss. After this diagnosis, she gradually became unable to move her extremities. She can still speak now, but cannot eat as normal, which made her to have gastrostomy and feeding. Respiratory muscles are also affected. She is also complicated with a pericardial effusion leading to low cardiac output. A panel genetic testing disclosed a homozygous 2-base pair deletion in a gene, SH3TC2, predicted to cause frameshift. The SH3TC2 protein is specifically expressed in Schwann cells where it is localized to the plasma membrane and to the perinuclear endocytic recycling compartment, suggesting a possible function in myelination and/or in regions of axo-glial interactions. Several mutations are reported from western countries. Report on longstanding course is very few.

en: Integrated Targeted Whole-Genome and RNA Sequencing Reveals the Pathogenicity of an Intronic GNE Variant in GNE Myopathy
ja: ターゲット全ゲノムとRNAシーケンスの統合がGNEミオパチーにおけるイントロンGNEバリアントの病原性を明らかにする
abs: GNE myopathy is a rare autosomal recessive myopathy caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in GNE, which encodes an essential enzyme for sialic acid biosynthesis. Most variants are located in exonic regions, whereas significance of intronic variants remains unclear, leaving many suspected cases genetically unresolved. We aimed to assess the pathogenicity of intronic GNE variants using targeted whole-genome and RNA sequencing. We performed Combined Long Amplicon Sequencing (CoLAS) in two siblings with GNE myopathy. DNA and RNA were extracted from muscle biopsy specimens and peripheral blood mononuclear cells. Variants were validated using Sanger sequencing. Splicing effects were predicted using SpliceAI and SpliceRover and validated by RNA sequencing. Muscle sialylation was assessed using peanut agglutinin lectin staining. An uncharacterized intronic variant, NC_000009.12(NM_001128227): c.1163+5G>T, was identified in trans with a known missense variant (NM_001128227): c.1807C>G, p.V603L). RNA sequencing demonstrated aberrant splicing caused by intronic mutation, leading to a non-productive transcript in muscle and blood cells. Reduced sialic acid biosynthesis further supported the pathogenicity of the intronic mutation. These findings demonstrate that CoLAS can elucidate the genetic basis of GNE myopathy undetectable by exome sequencing. This approach provides a clinically applicable, less invasive diagnostic strategy and expands the spectrum of pathogenic GNE variants.

en: Perinatal Experiences in DM1 in Japan: A Nationwide Survey of Parents of Congenital and Childhood- Onset Patients
ja: 日本におけるDM1の周産期経験：先天性・小児期発症患者の親への全国調査
abs: Background/Objectives: DM1 is often diagnosed in mothers after the birth of a child with congenital DM1 (cDM) and is associated with perinatal complications. We investigated perinatal experiences among families affected by DM1 in Japan. Methods: We analyzed data from a nationwide questionnaire survey of parents of patients with congenital or childhood-onset DM1. Participants were recruited through the Remudy registry, patient groups, and medical institutions. Maternal diagnosis, perinatal experiences, and reproductive genetic testing were examined. Results: Of 483 questionnaires, 145 were returned. Fifty-eight mothers with DM1 were analyzed. Histories of infertility treatment, infertility, miscarriage, and stillbirth were reported by 36%, 48%, 18%, and 5%, respectively. DM1 symptoms worsened during pregnancy in 33%. Delivery occurred in general hospitals in 61% of cases, and 47% underwent cesarean section. Only 10% had been diagnosed before pregnancy and 10% during pregnancy, whereas 64% first became aware of possible DM1 after the birth of their affected child. These trends remained unchanged over four decades. Conclusion: Perinatal complications were common, while maternal diagnosis often remained unrecognized until after childbirth. Families may therefore first encounter disease- and genetics-related decisions during the perinatal period. Earlier access to genetic services and information is needed. Further analyses of reproductive genetic testing and its influence on subsequent reproductive decisions will be presented.

en: Perinatal Manifestations Leading to the Diagnosis of Maternal and Congenital Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1: A Case Report
ja: 母体・先天性筋強直性ジストロフィー1型の診断につながった周産期所見：症例報告
abs: Background: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) is an autosomal dominant neuromuscular disorder. Undiagnosed childbearing women are at high risk of delivering neonates with severe congenital DM1, often preceded by non-specific perinatal complications. Case Presentation: A 34-year-old, Gravida 2, Para 1 woman without family history of neuromuscular disorders conceived spontaneously. At mid-trimester, she was diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). Despite insulin therapy, glycemic control remained poor. She was transferred to our hospital at 34 weeks of gestation. Ultrasound examination revealed that the estimated fetal weight was +2.2 SD and severe polyhydramnios (AFI: 48 cm). Maternal serum CK was elevated. 5 days later, she delivered following premature rupture of membranes and labor onset. The neonate presented with severe generalized hypotonia and respiratory depression, requiring immediate and extensive resuscitation by neonatal team. The postpartum course was complicated by uterine atony requiring intrauterine balloon tamponade. Due to retained products of conception (RPOC) and progressive hemorrhage, uterine artery embolization (UAE) was performed on postpartum day 20. Subsequent genetic testing revealed an abnormal CTG triplet repeat expansion in the DMPK gene in both the mother and the infant, confirming a definitive diagnosis of DM1. Conclusion: This case illustrates that refractory GDM, severe polyhydramnios, uterine atony, and RPOC can serve as critical diagnostic clues for maternal DM1, which carries profound implications for congenital neonatal outcomes.

en: Effects of Oral Semaglutide, a GLP-1 receptor agonist, on Body Weight in Down Syndrome and Type 2 Diabetes.
ja: Down症候群・2型糖尿病におけるGLP-1受容体作動薬経口セマグルチドの体重への効果
abs: <Introduction> In the management of weight in adult patients with Down syndrome accompanied by obesity, there are cases where patients find it difficult to understand the necessity of self-weight management and to take action toward weight reduction. Therefore, this report presents cases of two adult patients with Down syndrome and mild diabetes mellitus who were treated with oral semaglutide, a GLP-1 receptor agonist. <Subjects> Two women in their 40s. Both were classified as severely obese. Despite undergoing dietary and exercise therapy for six months, there was no significant weight loss. Consequently, oral semaglutide (3mg daily) was initiated, resulting in approximately 10kg (about 13%) weight loss over one year. No adverse effects or rebound weight gain were observed during the course. Furthermore, the patients’ joy in weight loss led to increased motivation for health, expressed as “happy” and “I will work hard on dieting.” <Discussion> The use of GLP-1 receptor agonists not only contributed to weight reduction but also enhanced patients’ health awareness. For patients with Down syndrome exhibiting severe obesity, where consciously understanding and implementing weight management can be challenging, pharmacotherapy may serve as a viable treatment option.

en: Infection-triggered Acute Psychiatric Onset of Adrenoleukodystrophy Mimicking Encephalitis in an Adolescent
ja: 青年期に脳炎様の感染誘発性急性精神症状で発症した副腎白質ジストロフィー
abs: Background: Adrenoleukodystrophy (ALD) is an X-linked metabolic disorder characterized primarily by progressive demyelination within the central nervous system. Clinical presentations vary in age at onset and phenotype, making differentiation sometimes challenging. As hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) in the initial stages is the only effective therapy, prompt diagnosis is critical. Case: A 17-year-old boy developed acute irritability and incoherence following pneumonia infection. There were no other abnormal neurological findings. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated hyperintense lesions extending from the lateral lemniscus to the medial geniculate body. Infectious or autoimmune encephalitis was initially suspected, but the treatment was ineffective. Detailed reassessment of the family history revealed that the maternal grandfather was previously diagnosed with ALD after manifesting gait disturbance. Additional investigations demonstrated elevated very-long-chain fatty acids levels, and genetic analysis identified a pathogenic ABCD1 variant (c.1772G>T, p.Arg591Leu), confirming the diagnosis of ALD. The patient was eligible for HSCT and subsequently underwent transplantation. Conclusion: Clinical manifestations of ALD vary even within families, highlighting the importance of detailed family history assessment. ALD should be considered in patients with an acute onset of isolated psychiatric symptoms for early diagnosis and favorable prognosis.

en: A family with OTC deficiency in which a novel variant was identified and functionally validated by minigene analysis
ja: 新規バリアントを同定しミニジーン解析で機能検証したOTC欠損症の家系
abs: Introduction OTC deficiency is an X linked urea cycle disorder. Although molecular diagnosis is usually established by genetic testing of the OTC gene, pathogenic variants may remain undetected by conventional sequencing approaches. We report a family in which a novel intronic variant affecting the splice acceptor site was identified approximately 40 years after the initial diagnosis, enabling definitive carrier diagnosis. Case The proband was a boy who died of hyperammonemia at three years of age. Reduced hepatic OTC enzyme activity confirmed the diagnosis of OTC deficiency. A male cousin in the maternal lineage also died of hyperammonemia in early childhood, and the proband's mother had been presumed to be a carrier. Approximately 40 years later, the proband's younger sister requested carrier testing prior to marriage. Genetic Analysis Commercial genetic testing using short read sequencing in the proband's mother failed to identify a pathogenic variant. Targeted long read sequencing did not detect any structural variants but identified a novel intronic splice altering variant, c.387-12G>A. In silico analysis predicted abnormal splicing. A minigene assay confirmed that the variant caused aberrant splicing, resulting in insertion of a 10bp sequence between exons and a consequent frameshift predicted to trigger nonsense mediated mRNA decay. Conclusion Our findings highlight the utility of minigene assays for evaluating suspected splice-altering variants and the importance of extended genetic analysis in genetically unresolved families with OTC deficiency.

en: Newborn Screening and Follow-up for X-linked Adrenoleukodystrophy in Kumamoto Prefecture
ja: 熊本県におけるX連鎖副腎白質ジストロフィーの新生児スクリーニングとフォローアップ
abs: Background: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (ALD) can cause adrenal insufficiency and cerebral demyelination in boys. Presymptomatic detection enables endocrine surveillance and timely hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Kumamoto introduced ALD newborn screening (NBS) in October 2024. Methods: Male newborns were screened using dried blood spots collected at 4-6 days of age. LysoPC(26:0) was measured by LC- MS/MS, and infants above the cutoff underwent repeat testing. Screen-positive infants were referred to Kumamoto University Hospital for assessment, genetic counseling, plasma very-long-chain fatty acid (VLCFA) analysis, and ABCD1 sequencing. Follow-up included adrenal testing from infancy and brain MRI from 2 years. Results: From October 2024 to March 2026, 8,072 boys were screened. Seven exceeded the initial LysoPC(26:0) cutoff, and two remained positive after repeat testing. Both had no known family history, were clinically normal at referral, and showed elevated VLCFA ratios. Genetic testing identified an ABCD1 variant of uncertain significance in one infant and a pathogenic ABCD1 variant with suspected somatic mosaicism in the other. Both remain asymptomatic with age-appropriate growth and development under regular endocrine follow-up. Conclusion: ALD NBS in Kumamoto identified boys requiring long-term surveillance, including cases with uncertain variant interpretation and somatic mosaicism. The program highlights the need for multidisciplinary follow-up, careful genetic interpretation, counseling, and psychosocial support.

en: Deoxynucleoside supplementation rescues mitochondrial defects in TWNK-mutant patient-derived NPCs
ja: デオキシヌクレオシド補充はTWNK変異患者由来NPCのミトコンドリア異常を回復させる
abs: Background: Pathogenic variants in TWNK, encoding the mitochondrial DNA helicase Twinkle, cause mtDNA maintenance disorders with severe neurological involvement. Disease-relevant human neural cell models for testing mitochondrial rescue strategies remain limited. Methods: We generated iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells (NPCs) from a patient with compound heterozygous TWNK variants and control iPSC lines. NPC identity was confirmed by neural progenitor markers. Mitochondrial phenotypes were assessed by qPCR for mtDNA copy number, ROS levels, and ATP measurement. Mutant NPCs were treated with deoxynucleoside supplementation and compared with vehicle-treated cells. Results: TWNK-mutant iPSCs were successfully differentiated into NPCs. Compared with controls, patient-derived NPCs showed reduced mtDNA copy number, increased ROS, and decreased ATP production, indicating mitochondrial dysfunction. Deoxynucleoside supplementation partially restored mtDNA copy number, reduced ROS accumulation, and increased ATP production in mutant NPCs. Conclusion: Patient-derived iPSC-NPCs recapitulate mtDNA depletion and mitochondrial dysfunction associated with TWNK-related disease. These findings support deoxynucleoside supplementation as a potential mitochondrial rescue strategy and highlight the utility of this model for investigating neural vulnerability caused by mtDNA maintenance defects.

en: Clinical and Genetic Analysis of Cleidocranial Dysplasia with RUNX2 Missense Variants
ja: RUNX2ミスセンスバリアントを有する鎖骨頭蓋異形成症の臨床・遺伝学的解析
