abs: Clinical and Genetic Analysis of Cleidocranial Dysplasia with RUNX2 MissenseVariants Cleidocranial dysplasia (CCD) is a rare autosomal dominant skeletal disordercharacterized by delayed closure of the cranial sutures, clavicular hypoplasia, delayedpermanent tooth eruption, and supernumerary teeth. Pathogenic variants in runt-relatedtranscription factor 2 (RUNX2), a key regulator of bone and tooth development, are themajor cause of CCD. In particular, missense variants in the runt domain may impair DNAbinding and transcriptional regulation, although their clinical significance can sometimes bedifficult to interpret because of phenotypic variability. Recent advances in clinical genetics have highlighted the importance of integrated variantinterpretation using clinical findings, in silico analyses, segregation data, and functionalstudies based on ACMG/AMP guidelines. However, the pathogenicity of rare or novelRUNX2 missense variants may remain uncertain. Here, we report 3 patients clinically diagnosed with CCD based on characteristic skeletaland dental findings. Genetic analyses identified heterozygous missense variants within theRUNX2 runt domain, including one novel variant. To evaluate its pathogenicity, in silicoanalyses and molecular functional studies were performed. We discuss the clinicalsignificance of RUNX2 runt domain variants and the utility of integrated variantinterpretation in CCD.

en: A case of Cowden syndrome harboring two pathogenic PTEN variants
ja: 2つのPTEN病的バリアントを有するCowden症候群の1例
abs: Background: Cowden syndrome is autosomal dominant disorder caused by pathogenic PTEN (phosphatase and tensin homolog) variant. NCCN Guideline 2023, Version 1, simplified the testing criteria of Cowden syndrome. Breast, endometrial or thyroid cancer female patients with head circumference greater than 58cm are eligible for PTEN genetic testing. We report a case meeting this criteria, disclosed two pathogenic PTEN variants. Case Report: A 35-year-old woman underwent bilateral partial mastectomies for breast cancers at age 34. On tamoxifen use, she was found to have endometrial atypical hyperplasia. She had a past history of hemithyroidectomy at 21. Her mother suffered from endometrial cancer at 61. BRCA1/2 testing was negative; head circumference of 61.6cm met Cowden testing criteria, prompted PTEN analysis. Results and Discussion: PCR/direct sequencing analysis from peripheral blood lymphocytes (PBL) identified two pathogenic variants (PTEN NM_000314.8 c.733C>T p.Gln245Ter and c.737C>T p.Pro246Leu), both ClinVar-Pathogenic. RT-PCR/direct sequencing analysis from puromycin treated PBLs resulted in nonsense-mediated mRNA decay for both variants, implying Cis-localization. PCR-SSCP analysis separated the mutant allele; sequencing of the excised band revealed two adjacent variants on the same allele. HGVS nomenclature was corrected to c.733_737delCAGCCinsTAGCT. This report emphasizes routine head circumference measurement in case with relevant cancers and demonstrates that careful RNA and allele-specific analyses may be required to define complex PTEN variants.

en: A case diagnosed as Usher syndrome at young adulthood after genetic analysis of congenital hearing loss
ja: 先天性難聴の遺伝学的解析により若年成人期にUsher症候群と診断された1例
abs: Introduction: Usher syndrome is autosomal recessive disease with hearing loss and retinitis pigmentosa, and is the most popular cause of deaf-blindness. USH2A is one of the genes which are known to cause Usher syndrome. We report a case in which retinitis pigmentosa was identified after USH2A variants were detected by genetic analysis of hearing loss, leading to the diagnosis of Usher syndrome. Case: The proband is a 21-years-old female with congenital hearing loss. The pure-tone audiometry bilaterally showed sloping sensorineural hearing loss. After filtering and selection of the candidate variants detected by targeted resequencing of 156 deafness genes, we identified two heterozygous nonsense variant NM_206933.2:c.13639G>T(p.E4547*) and NM_206933.2:c.7252C>T(p.Q2418*) of USH2A. In addition, each variant was identified in the normal-hearing parents as a heterozygous variant. These nonsense variants were interpreted as autosomal recessively pathogenic according to the ACMG2015/ClinGen HLEP criteria. A detailed medical interview after genetic testing results revealed symptoms of night blindness recently. Ophthalmological findings were consistent with retinitis pigmentosa, and the patient was diagnosed with Usher syndrome. Discussion: In this case, genetic analysis detected USH2A variants, and USH2A is known as the representative gene mutation for Usher syndrome. Thus, the identification of USH2A variants enabled the early detection of retinitis pigmentosa, leading to the diagnosis of Usher syndrome even though this patient had few noticeable eye symptoms.

en: Cognitive and Achievement Profile of a Child with NF1 Presenting a Novel Variant Using KABC-II and CHC Theory
ja: 新規バリアントを有するNF1児のKABC-IIとCHC理論による認知・習得プロファイル
abs: Background: NF1 causes learning disabilities. Individual variability requires personalized assessment beyond diagnostic labels. Objectives: Profile a child with a novel NF1 variant using KABC-II and CHC theory. Methods: A 13-year-old female with NF1 underwent KABC-II testing; cognitive results were interpreted via CHC theory, a framework mapping intelligence domains. Subsequent genetic testing was performed. Results: Sequencing identified a novel frameshift variant in the NF1 gene [NM_000267.3:c.1344_1350del p.(His448GlnfsTer23)], judged Likely Pathogenic. The CHC Composite was 76 (Gc:77, Gf:82, Gv:72, Glr:87, Gsm:85). Achievement scores were Vocabulary:77, Reading:77, Writing:90, and Mathematics:93. Unlike typical NF1 profiles with 20-50 point language-over-visuospatial (Gc-Gv) gaps, this case showed only a 5-point difference. Mathematics and writing approached population means despite below-average cognition. Discussion: While the variant's pathogenicity (loss-of-function) likely caused overall cognitive reduction, the unique profile with high mathematics/writing scores cannot be explained by genotype alone. This suggests phenotypic modification by environmental factors, such as education and compensatory strategies. This approach applies to other conditions, though single-case findings limit generalizability and necessitate verification through more cases. Conclusions: NF1 profiles are variable. Achievement exceeding cognitive predictions proves genetic vulnerability is compensable with support, highlighting the necessity of personalized assessment.

en: Functional analysis of synonymous and splice-site variants of uncertain significance using Minigene Assay.
ja: ミニジーンアッセイによる意義不明の同義・スプライス部位バリアントの機能解析
abs: Background: Synonymous substitutions and variants distal to exon-intron boundaries (more than 3 bp) may affect splicing, but established guidelines often categorize them as variants of uncertain significance (VUS). Functional validation of these variants is difficult due to inaccessibility of expressed tissues or low gene expression in blood. Therefore, a functional analysis system would be essential to evaluate their splicing aberrations. The aim of this study is to establish a minigene assay using the pSpliceExpress vector that allows for the rapid analysis (within two weeks) of large genomic fragments (from 5 kb to 15 kb). Material and Method : A previously reported and functionally characterized variant in FBN1 (NM_000138.4:c.6354C>T). We cloned the three-exon fragment (the variant-carrying exon and flanking exons) into pSpliceExpress, transfected it into HEK293 cells, and extracted total RNA 48 hours later. Splicing aberrations were evaluated using RT-PCR, electrophoresis, and Sanger sequencing. Result: The c.6354C>T variant in FBN1 was found to disrupt the splice site recognition, resulting in the complete skipping of the target exon, consistent with the previously reported findings of this variant. Conclusion: Minigene assay enables splicing evaluation in challenging cases: difficult tissue sampling or low gene expression in blood. We plan to evaluate multiple VUS in FBN1 using this system, and to validate whether "frozen blood mRNA analysis" could also be a useful method for low-expression genes in blood like FBN1.

en: DYNC1H1-related dyneinopathies: a two case report highlighting the importance of deep phenotyping
ja: DYNC1H1関連ダイニン病：深い表現型解析の重要性を示す2例報告
abs: Introduction DYNC1H1 encodes the heavy chain of cytoplasmic dynein 1, a motor protein essential for retrograde axonal transport and other intracellular trafficking processes. Pathogenic heterozygous variants cause a broad, domain specific spectrum, ranging from CMT disease to neurodevelopmental brain disorders. Case presentation Case1 was a 4-year-old boy with global developmental delay (DD) and bilateral congenital vertical talus; examination showed lower-limb-predominant hypotonia, reduced reflexes, and electrophysiology confirmed axonal neuropathy. He developed febrile status epilepticus and had no meaningful words at age 4. Case 2 was a 15-year-old girl who developed focal epilepsy (FE) at the age of 5; her seizures have remained well controlled, and despite mild intellectual disability (ID) requiring special education, she is independent in daily life with good social skills. Whole-genome sequencing revealed de novo heterozygous variants in DYNC1H1 in both cases: a previously reported CMT type 2O allele in the N-terminal tail domain in Case 1 and a novel variant in the C-terminal AAA+ ATPase motor domain in Case 2. Case 1 additionally carried a de novo variant in ZMYND11, an ID-associated gene. Conclusion These cases highlight the broad phenotypic spectrum of DYNC1H1-related disorders. They also suggest that additional variants, such as ZMYND11, may act as modifiers, emphasizing the need for detailed phenotyping and comprehensive genomic analysis in DYNC1H1-associated disease.

en: A Lynch syndrome case with a partial MSH2 intron 10 deletion discovered by inconsistent results by MLPA analysis
ja: MLPA解析の結果不一致から発見されたMSH2イントロン10部分欠失を有するLynch症候群の1例
abs: Background: Lynch syndrome is a hereditary cancer syndrome caused by germline pathogenic variants in DNA mismatch repair genes. We report a case in which an MSH2 variant was identified after discordant MLPA results. Case: A 49-year-old man was diagnosed with rectal cancer at age 39. His tumor showed MSI-H and loss of MSH2/MSH6 protein expression. His mother had early-onset colorectal and endometrial cancers, and his sister had ovarian and rectal cancers. Genetic testing: MSH2 sequencing detected no pathogenic variant in exons and exon-intron boundaries. MLPA analysis using probe set P003 for MLH1/MSH2 showed a significantly reduced signal in a single probe for MSH2 exon 10. We validated this using another probe set, P248, though no alterations were detected. We then conducted long-range PCR using primers set on exon 10 and 11 and identified a 2705-bp deletion in intron 10 (MSH2:c.1661+8_c.1662-1445del). RT- PCR analysis using total RNA from cultured T cells demonstrated aberrant transcripts: one lacking exon 10, whereas the other harbored a truncated exon 10 lacking 82 bp from its 3' region by activation of a splicing donor within exon 10; both resulted in a frameshift. Discussion: Detection of structural variants by MLPA depends on probe design, and pathogenic variants may be missed when only a single probe mix is used. When MLPA shows a single-probe or single-exon deletion/duplication, or when MMR deficiency is suggested despite negative sequencing and inconclusive MLPA findings, confirmation with another probe mix and structural/RNA analyses should be considered.

en: Long-read sequencing with haplotype phasing resolves complex USH2A structural variants: five cases
ja: ハプロタイプフェージングを伴うロングリードシーケンスで複雑なUSH2A構造多型を解明：5例
abs: USH2A, spanning ~800 kb with 72 exons, is a major cause of Usher syndrome type 2 (USH2). Short-read copy-number variant (CNV) analysis is limited in resolving structural variant (SV) boundaries, allelic phase, and copy-number gains, often leaving cases genetically unsolved. We applied Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing (PromethION P2 Solo, adaptive sampling) with haplotype phasing to five USH2A cases that were undiagnosed or incompletely diagnosed by short-read panel testing. Five distinct and diagnostically challenging SV configurations were resolved: two cases of compound heterozygous deletions that appeared as a single-copy loss or two spatially separated losses on CNV analysis; one homozygous deletion in which haplotype phasing failed to separate alleles, raising suspicion of consanguinity; one family with an apparently autosomal dominant pedigree that was re-interpreted as two independent compound heterozygotes, each carrying a different point variant in trans with the same inherited deletion allele; and one case of a heterozygous tandem duplication in compound heterozygosity with a point variant, identified by breakpoint-spanning split reads and allele-length discrepancy on phased reads. All five cases reached a definitive biallelic USH2A diagnosis. Long-read sequencing with haplotype phasing enables allele-resolved characterization of complex USH2A SVs - including dominant inheritance mimics and cryptic tandem duplications - and substantially complements short-read-based genetic diagnosis of USH2.

en: Very low-level aberrant splicing of RYR2 revealed by Nanopore cDNA amplicon sequencing in a mild case of CPVT
ja: 軽症CPVT例でナノポアcDNAアンプリコンシーケンスにより明らかになったRYR2の極低レベル異常スプライシング
abs: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT) is a potentially lethal inherited arrhythmia characterized by exercise- or emotion-induced ventricular tachyarrhythmias and sudden cardiac arrest. Heterozygous missense or in-frame deletion variants in RYR2 typically cause CPVT through a gain-of-function mechanism. Although RYR2 contains 105 exons, pathogenic variants cluster within four hotspot regions. Exome sequencing identified a novel synonymous RYR2 variant, c.11880G>A p.(Gln3960=), in a 49-year-old woman with CPVT. She had an unusually mild phenotype, only with premature ventricular contractions and no major arrhythmic events. The variant was absent from population databases and was inherited from her asymptomatic 74-year-old mother. This variant affects the last nucleotide of exon 88 within a hotspot region, and exon 88 skipping was predicted. Blood RNA analysis was uninformative, likely owing to low RYR2 expression. A minigene assay followed by repeated subcloning of transcripts from wild-type and mutant constructs also failed to detect a difference. Given the exceptionally mild phenotype, aberrant transcripts were suspected to be present at very low levels. Therefore, nanopore-based deep amplicon sequencing of minigene-derived transcripts was performed, revealing a low but significant increase in exon 88 skipping (1.2% in mutant vs. 0.3% in control transcripts), resulting in an in-frame deletion of 35 amino acids [p.(3925_3960del)] within a hotspot region. The low abundance of aberrant transcripts may explain the reduced penetrance in this family.

en: Neurofibromatosis type 1 associated with transposable element insertions: Two case reports
ja: トランスポゾン挿入に関連する神経線維腫症1型：2例報告
abs: Background: Transposable elements (TEs) are a type of mobile genetic element that play important roles in gene regulation and transcription. TE insertions into coding or regulatory regions can result in various genetic disorders. Although a molecular diagnosis can be confirmed in the vast majority of patients with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), 5% of cases remain genetically unresolved. Here, we report two cases of NF1 resulting from transposable element insertions in NF1. Case 1: A 11-month-old boy exhibiting multiple cafe-au-lait spots (CALS), suggesting NF1 in infancy. He had no family history of NF1 and no clinical manifestations other than CALS. Case 2: A 16-year-old girl clinically diagnosed with NF1 based on the presence of CALS and an optic pathway glioma. She had no family history and cutaneous or plexiform neurofibromas. Targeted analysis of NF1 and SPRED1 using next generation sequencing (NGS) and MLPA were performed for both cases. NGS analysis indicated soft-clipped alignments suggestive of transposable element insertions in exon 25 and exon 13, respectively. Discussion: To date, TE insertions have been reported to account for 0.4% of pathogenic variants in NF1 and may explain approximately 10% of NF1 cases unresolved by conventional molecular analysis. However, hybrid capture-based NGS approaches have limited sensitivity for soft-clipped reads, which restricts the detection of TE insertions. Conclusion: Analysis of TE insertions using soft-clipped reads contributes to early diagnosis of NF1, and further investigation is warranted to improve sensitivity.

en: Genotype-Dependent Full-Field Stimulus Test Thresholds in Inherited Retinal Dystrophies
ja: 遺伝性網膜ジストロフィーにおける遺伝型依存的な全視野刺激閾値検査
abs: Background Inherited retinal dystrophies (IRDs) are a major cause of blindness. Voretigene neparvovec (Luxturna) and PrismGuide highlight recent advances in IRD care. The full field stimulus test (FST) was a primary endpoint in the RPE65 gene therapy trial (Fujinami et al., 2025), but genotype specific luminance threshold profiles remain unclear. We evaluated FST thresholds in IRD patients with night blindness. Methods Patients with night blindness were selected from 130 patients (234 eyes) who underwent FST. After 45 minutes of dark adaptation, colour FST used blue, red, and white stimuli (Diagnosys ColorDome) following the ISCEV/IPS guideline. Controls were 40 eyes from 20 healthy subjects. Results We analysed 123 eyes from 62 IRD patients; most had retinitis pigmentosa. Median age at onset was 10.0 years (0 to 70), median age at examination was 48.0 years (0 to 83), and median visual acuity was 0.80 logMAR. Median blue, red, and white FST thresholds were minus 3.7, minus 2.5, and minus 3.5 log10 cd s per square metre, respectively, compared with minus 7.7, minus 5.3, and minus 7.1 in controls. Eighteen causative genes were identified, most commonly EYS, RPE65, and RPGR. Thresholds were higher in disease associated with RPE65 and lower in disease associated with PRPH2. Conclusions FST provides a practical measure of visual sensitivity in IRDs. IRD patients showed markedly elevated luminance thresholds and genotype specific patterns. These findings support FST as a quantitative outcome measure for clinical assessment and therapeutic trials.

en: Factors associated with the uptake of genetic testing among relatives of individuals with hereditary tumour syndromes.
ja: 遺伝性腫瘍症候群患者の血縁者における遺伝学的検査受検に関連する因子
abs: Background and Objectives: Cascade testing (CT), based on the pathogenic variant identified in a proband, can guide health management among relatives. However, many relatives do not receive genetic information, genetic counseling, or genetic testing, limiting opportunities for cancer prevention and surveillance. This study investigated factors associated with genetic testing uptake among relatives. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed the medical records of 48 probands with hereditary tumor syndromes who underwent genetic counseling at our institution. Clinical information, pedigrees, and CT implementation among relatives were collected. The primary outcome was uptake of genetic testing among relatives. Univariate analyses were performed to evaluate associations between testing uptake and characteristics of relatives. Results: A total of 387 relatives (first-, second-, and third-degree relatives) were included, and 33 (8.7%) underwent genetic testing. Testing uptake was significantly associated with female sex (11.7% vs. 5.5%), first-degree versus second-/third-degree relatives (17.8% vs. 2.7%), relationship to the proband (children 23.3%, siblings 14.1%, parents 17.8%), attendance at the proband's genetic counseling session (44.4% vs. 6.0%), and a personal history of cancer (24.1% vs. 6.2%) (all p<0.05). Conclusions: The CT uptake rate among first-degree relatives was 17.8%. Degree of kinship and characteristics of relatives were associated with CT uptake. Further multivariable analyses accounting for familial clustering are needed to identify independent factors.

en: De Novo Genome Assembly of a Rare Disease Trio Using HiFi Long-Read Sequencing
ja: HiFiロングリードシーケンスを用いた希少疾患トリオのde novoゲノムアセンブリ
abs: Background: The genetic etiology of many rare diseases remains unresolved due to the limitations of short-read sequencing in detecting complex genomic variants. Long-read technologies offer a promising path toward resolving complex genomic rearrangements at single-nucleotide resolution. Here we report a phased, haplotype-resolved de novo genome assembly for a female patient with an undiagnosed rare disease. Methods and results: The proband was sequenced using PacBio HiFi long-read technology (coverage 32.5×, read N50 17.4 kb), and parental Illumina short-read sequencing data were used to generate parental k-mer databases for trio-based assembly with Hifiasm. The resulting assembly represents a fully phased, diploid genome in which each haplotype is anchored to either the maternal or paternal origin. Assembly contiguity, completeness, and base-level accuracy were assessed using gfastats and yak. Contig N50 was 55 Mb, total assembly length was 3.03 Gb, the number of contigs was 707, and the QV score was 60, all consistent with published HiFi-based human genome assemblies of comparable quality. These assemblies constitute a high-quality genomic resource for downstream variant discovery. Comprehensive SV calling and identification of candidate de novo SVs underlying the proband's phenotype are ongoing and will be reported in a future study. Conclusion: This work demonstrates the utility of long-read, trio-based assembly as a foundation for unbiased variant discovery in rare disease genomics.

en: Multi-omics analysis of molecular responses to diphenylarsinic acid (DPAA) exposure in the primate brain
ja: 霊長類脳におけるジフェニルアルシン酸（DPAA）曝露への分子応答のマルチオミクス解析
abs: Diphenylarsinic acid (DPAA), an organoarsenic compound associated with neurological abnormalities, has been reported to induce neurobehavioral dysfunction; however, the molecular basis of its neurotoxicity remains incompletely understood. In this study, we performed an integrated multi-omics analysis to characterize molecular responses to DPAA exposure in the primate brain. Brain tissues from 30 control and DPAA-exposed cynomolgus monkeys were collected from the medial temporal lobe (MTL), cerebellum (Cb), lateral temporal lobe, and occipital lobe, across multiple exposure durations (5, 29, 170, and 339 days). Whole-genome sequencing (WGS), RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), and DNA methylation (DNAm) profiling using the Infinium MethylationEPIC array were performed. WGS analysis revealed no substantial increase in genomic mutation burden following DPAA exposure. In contrast, RNA-seq and DNAm analyses identified region- and time-dependent molecular alterations. Transcriptional changes were particularly prominent in the MTL at early stages and in the Cb at later stages. Limited overlap between differentially expressed and methylated genes suggested partially independent regulatory responses. These findings suggest that DPAA-induced neurotoxicity is associated primarily with transcriptional and epigenetic alterations rather than direct genomic changes.

en: A novel single-amino-acid insertion in SDHB found in a patient with metastatic paraganglioma
ja: 転移性傍神経節腫患者で見出された新規SDHB単一アミノ酸挿入
abs: [Background] SDHB, located on 1p36.13, encodes a subunit of succinate dehydrogenase and acts as a tumor suppressor gene. SDHB-related paragangliomas (PGLs) are associated with early onset and metastasis. [Case] A man in his 50s with metastatic PGL was referred for debulking surgery prior to 177Lu-DOTATATE therapy. He had no relevant medical or family history. He underwent resection of a retroperitoneal PGL in his 20s, and later developed metastases to the liver and bone. CVD chemotherapy was partially effective but discontinued due to neuropathy, and 131I-MIBG therapy was ineffective. Preoperative plasma normetanephrine was markedly elevated. After metyrosine pretreatment, the liver tumor was removed. SDHB immunostaining was negative. [Genetic analyses] Targeted sequencing of 28 PGL-related genes identified a novel germline SDHB variant, c.685_687dup, p.(Glu229dup). Variant allele frequency was higher in tumor than in blood DNA (76% vs 45%). Array-CGH revealed a somatic 1p deletion. [Discussion] Arg230, adjacent to Glu229, is a known mutation hotspot, where disruption of the ionic bond with Asp224 destabilizes SDHB. The p.(Glu229dup) variant may similarly impair protein function. Although in-frame indels are often difficult to interpret, somatic loss of the SDHB wild-type allele and loss of SDHB immunoreactivity supports pathogenicity in this case. [Conclusion] We identified a novel SDHB in-frame insertion in metastatic PGL. Integration of tumor immunohistochemistry and genomics is valuable for variant interpretation.

en: A Case of Fertility Treatment Resulting in a Childbirth in a Woman with Periodontal Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome
ja: 歯周型Ehlers-Danlos症候群女性の不妊治療により出産に至った1例
abs: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome has 13 subtypes and is associated with severe complications during pregnancy. However, there have been no previous reports of pregnancy and perinatal outcomes of cases of periodontal Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (pEDS). The patient was 34 years old, para 0, and she had no family history suggestive of pEDS. Previously, symptoms such as tooth loss and slow-healing skin wounds were present. Three years previously, genetic testing (complement deficiency gene testing) was submitted, and a missense mutation (c.1013G>A) was detected in the C1R gene. Although this variant has not previously been reported, an amino acid substitution at the same position (p.Cys338Tyr) has been established as a cause of autosomal dominant pEDS. Since this position is essential for CCP1 domain formation in the C1R gene, it was considered likely to have pathogenic significance, leading to a diagnosis of pEDS. The patient and her partner wanted to have children and underwent genetic counseling. They understood that there were many unknown risks associated with pregnancy and childbirth but still wished to undergo infertility treatment. Pregnancy was achieved through assisted reproductive technology. She was hospitalized for preterm labor from 28 to 36 weeks of pregnancy. At 38 weeks, vacuum extraction was performed because of fetal distress. The postpartum course was uneventful, and there were no major problems with wound healing after delivery. This case provides clinically important information regarding pregnancy management and perinatal outcomes in women with pEDS who wish pregnancy.

en: Genotype-dependent dynamics of surgery-induced reactive and regenerative bone formation in a mouse model of mcEDS
ja: mcEDSモデルマウスにおける手術誘発性反応性・再生性骨形成の遺伝型依存的動態
abs: Musculocontractural Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (mcEDS) is caused by dermatan sulfate (DS) deficiency due to pathogenic variants in CHST14 or DSE. Patients with mcEDS develop progressive skeletal deformities; however, the role of DS deficiency in skeletal pathophysiology remains unclear. Chst14-deficient mice (Chst14-/- ), an animal model of mcEDS, exhibit progressive spinal deformity and impaired bone architecture (Takahashi et al., Glycobiology, accepted). To investigate the role of DS deficiency in bone repair and regeneration, a 0.8-mm drill-hole defect was created in the femur of Chst14-/- and wild-type (WT) mice. Bone repair was evaluated on days 0, 3, 7, 10, 14, 21, and 28. Bone closure was longitudinally monitored by micro-CT, while harvested femurs were used for macroscopic analysis and assessment of cortical bone volume and mineral density. No apparent difference in drill-hole closure was observed between the groups. Reactive bone formation was observed in all groups; however, the reactive bulge disappeared by day 28 only in Chst14-/- with drill-hole defects. Micro-CT analyses of cortical bone volume and mineral density around the defect suggested that WT mice showed sustained reactive bone formation followed by remodeling, whereas Chst14-/-exhibited altered timing and reduced persistence of these responses. These findings suggest that DS deficiency impairs maintenance of reactive bone formation and alters the balance between bone formation and remodeling.

en: Craniofacial analysis using the musculocontractural Ehlers-Danlos syndrome model mouse
ja: 筋拘縮型Ehlers-Danlos症候群モデルマウスを用いた頭蓋顔面解析
abs: Musculocontractural Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (mcEDS) is a systemic dermatan sulfate (DS) deficiency caused by pathogenic variants in the CHST14 or DSE genes. It is characterized by multiple malformations and progressive fragility-related manifestations. Craniofacial features include large fontanelle, down slanting palpebral fissures, hypertelorism, microretrognathia, and brachycephaly in early childhood; and asymmetry and mandibular protrusion from adolescence. The aim of this study was to explore the development of craniofacial features of mcEDS e through a mouse model for the disorder. Chst14 gene-deleted mice (Chst14 -/- ) and wild-type mice (WT) were used; and craniofacial radiographs and photographs were obtained and analyzed at 8 and 52 weeks of age. Radiographs showed that the occipital-to-frontal length was significantly shorter in Chst14 -/- mice than WT mice at both ages, and that the mandibular body length was significantly shorter in Chst14 -/- mice than WT mice at 52 weeks. Photographs showed no significant difference in facial symmetricity, facial width ratio, or interpupillary distance to facial length ratio between Chst14 -/- mice and WT mice at both ages. Chst14 -/- exhibited congenital occipital hypoplasia and delayed mandibular growth, representing some overlaps with features in mcEDS. DS deficiency is suggested to affect craniofacial morphogenesis beginning in the fetal period and persisting after birth.

en: A case of perforated descending colon diverticulitis in a patient with osteogenesis imperfecta
ja: 骨形成不全症患者における下行結腸憩室炎穿孔の1例
abs: Background: Osteogenesis imperfecta is a congenital disorder characterized by bone fragility, short stature, and scoliosis. We report a case of perforated descending colon diverticulitis treated with emergency surgery in a patient with osteogenesis imperfecta. Case Presentation: A 50-year-old man with osteogenesis imperfecta was referred to our hospital for suspected gastrointestinal perforation. He had a history of conservative treatment for descending colon diverticulitis. One week before admission, he developed left upper abdominal pain. Physical examination revealed abdominal tenderness with muscular guarding and rebound tenderness. Abdominal computed tomography showed fluid collection with free air around the descending colon. Perforated descending colon diverticulitis with generalized peritonitis was diagnosed, and emergency surgery was performed. Despite severe scoliosis and abdominal deformity, left hemicolectomy, transverse colostomy, and sigmoid mucous fistula creation were successfully performed. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 20. Conclusion: Severe scoliosis and truncal deformity associated with osteogenesis imperfecta may complicate abdominal surgery and perioperative management. As long-term survival of patients with congenital disorders improves, appropriate management of adult-onset gastrointestinal diseases will become increasingly important.

en: Identifying technically challenging short-read NGS regions using standard materials and simulation data
ja: 標準物質とシミュレーションデータを用いたショートリードNGSの技術的困難領域の同定
abs: Introduction: Analytical validation is essential when introducing clinical laboratory tests, including genetic testing. Following the introduction of a D006-4 reimbursed multi-gene panel test in 2024, we conducted analytical validation of an NGS-based genetic test and identified genomic regions that are difficult to analyze using short-read NGS(SR-NGS). Methods: Target regions comprised coding sequences of 187 genes associated with 43 diseases. Variant calling was performed using the DRAGEN pipeline. Analytical accuracy was evaluated using standard DNA samples purchased from NIST and simulation data with variants for all CDS. Results: Using both standard materials and simulation data, technically challenging regions were identified in SELENON, NEB, and COL6A1 in the muscle weakness group, and in TTN and GBA1 in the cardiomyopathy group. In SELENON, difficulty was due to lack of capture probes, whereas in the other genes, sequence-specific characteristics caused instability in variant detection. Discussion: Standard materials enabled platform benchmarking, whereas simulation data allowed comprehensive evaluation of variant detection when variants were present. The combined use of these approaches enabled multifaceted assessment of technically challenging SR-NGS regions. Conclusion: Rare disease genetic testing is primarily performed as laboratory-developed tests. Even with limited clinical specimens are unavailable, an analytical validation framework within individual laboratories is required. The approach presented here provides a practical method to meet this requirement.

en: A case of Genitopatellar syndrome with complex craniosynostosis
ja: 複雑な頭蓋縫合早期癒合を伴うGenitopatellar症候群の1例
abs: Background: Loss-of-function variants in KAT6B are associated with Say-Barber-Biesecker-Young-Simpson syndrome (SBBYSS) and Genitopatellar syndrome (GPS). Isolated sagittal craniosynostosis has been described in only two of more than 150 reported cases of KAT6B-related disorders, leaving the association with KAT6B unclear. Case: The patient was a boy who presented with iris hypopigmentation, micrognathia, laryngomalacia, cryptorchidism, micropenis and developmental delay. At 7 months of age, he was referred for further evaluation of his clinical features. Whole exome sequencing identified a pathogenic nonsense variant c.3718G>T (p.Glu1240Ter) in KAT6B, which is consistent with the diagnosis of GPS. At the age of 4 years, he exhibited marked bitemporal narrowing and ridging of the coronal sutures, suggesting the presence of craniosynostosis. Subsequently, cranial CT revealed complex craniosynostosis. Discussion: A recent study has demonstrated premature ossification and accelerated osteoblast differentiation in Kat6B null mice. The present case may provide further insight into the association between craniosynostosis and KAT6B, highlighting the importance of clinical evaluation for craniosynostosis in KAT6B-related disorders.

en: Novel de novo COPB2 variants cause neurodevelopmental disorder with pyramidal and extrapyramidal features
ja: 新規de novo COPB2バリアントは錐体路・錐体外路症状を伴う神経発達症を引き起こす
abs: Coatopathies are a heterogeneous group of congenital genetic disorders caused by mutations in coat proteins and their associated factors, which are involved in intracellular vesicle transport. Among them, coatomer protein complex I (COPI) is responsible for retrograde trafficking from the Golgi apparatus to the endoplasmic reticulum. COPB2 encodes a component of COPI, and pathogenic variants in COPB2 have been reported to be associated with primary microcephaly in an autosomal recessive manner and childhood- or juvenile-onset osteoporosis with developmental delay in an autosomal dominant manner. In this study, we report three unrelated individuals with novel de novo COPB2 (NM_004766.3) variants identified by exome sequencing: c.893_894inv p.(Lys298Thr), c.1186T>A p.(Trp396Arg), and c.2318G>A p.(Trp773*). cDNA analysis using patient-derived lymphoblastoid cell lines confirmed that c.893_894inv caused skipping of exon 8, leading to a premature termination codon. Clinical features of the three individuals included dystonia, pyramidal signs, spasticity, abnormal muscle tone, developmental delay, dental malocclusion, and variable skeletal features. Our findings expand the phenotypic spectrum of COPB2-related disorder and emphasize the importance of COPI functions in neuronal and skeletal development.

en: Analysis of the Deleted Region and a Diabetes-Associated Autoimmunity Locus in 22q11.2DS with Type 1 Diabetes
ja: 1型糖尿病を伴う22q11.2欠失症候群における欠失領域と糖尿病関連自己免疫座位の解析
abs: Introduction: 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22q11.2DS) predisposes to autoimmunity, but type 1 diabetes (T1D) is rare despite islet autoantibody positivity. A previous study suggested that an autoimmunity locus within the standard 3-Mb 22q11.2 deletion may modify T1D susceptibility. We report a child with 22q11.2DS and T1D whose deleted range was examined by array CGH. Case report: A 2-year-9-month-old boy presented with polydipsia, polyuria, and decreased activity. Hyperglycemia, elevated HbA1c, urinary ketones, low fasting serum C-peptide, and positivity for anti-GAD, IA-2, and ZnT8 antibodies led to a diagnosis of acute-onset type 1A diabetes with diabetic ketoacidosis. Short stature, atrial septal defect, speech delay, and characteristic facial features suggested 22q11.2DS, and FISH confirmed a 22q11.2 deletion. Array CGH revealed an approximately 2.81-Mb heterozygous deletion at 22q11.21. This corresponded to the common standard 3-Mb deletion and included the autoimmunity locus suggested to modify T1D susceptibility. Discussion: Although deletion of this locus has been proposed to protect against T1D, this patient developed despite carrying the standard 3-Mb deletion. This suggests that loss of this locus does not fully prevent T1D, and that additional factors such as HLA-related background and multiple islet autoantibody positivity may contribute to diabetes development in 22q11.2DS. Conclusion: This case suggests that deletion of the T1D-related autoimmunity locus alone cannot fully explain T1D development and provides insight into autoimmune diabetes in 22q11.2DS.

en: Sibling Cases of Isolated Asymptomatic Proteinuria without Megaloblastic Anemia Caused by Novel Homozygous AMN Variants
ja: 新規ホモ接合AMNバリアントによる巨赤芽球性貧血を伴わない孤立性無症候性蛋白尿の同胞例
abs: Introduction:AMN encodes amnionless, a protein involved in vitamin B12 absorption and proximal tubular protein reabsorption. Biallelic AMN variants cause Imerslund-Grasbeck syndrome type 2, typically with megaloblastic anemia and low-molecular-weight proteinuria. Isolated asymptomatic proteinuria without megaloblastic anemia has been reported in only one prior case. AMN has not been routinely included among the analyzed genes in previous genetic studies of proteinuria. Case Description: We report two Japanese brothers, aged 12 and 8 years, with isolated asymptomatic proteinuria detected by urinary screening. Their urinary protein/creatinine ratios were 0.7 and 0.5 g/gCr. Neither had anemia, impaired kidney function, or extrarenal manifestations. Urinary α-1-microglobulin was mildly elevated only in the elder brother. Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel homozygous AMN variant, c.750T>G, p.Cys250Trp, in both siblings; both parents were heterozygous. The variant was extremely rare and unreported. In silico tools predicted deleterious effects, and Missense3D structural analysis classified it as damaging. Serum vitamin B12 levels were low in both siblings, consistent with the expected phenotype. It was classified as Likely Pathogenic based on ACMG/AMP criteria with ClinGen recommendations. Discussion: This sibling pair suggests that AMN-associated disease can present as isolated asymptomatic proteinuria with subclinical vitamin B12 deficiency but without anemia. These findings support including AMN in genetic analysis with unexplained isolated asymptomatic proteinuria.

en: Non-neoplastic Chromosomal Findings Incidentally Detected during Chromosome Analysis for Hematologic Malignancies
ja: 血液腫瘍の染色体検査で偶発的に検出された非腫瘍性染色体所見
abs: Background: Chromosome testing is important for diagnosing hematologic malignancies. However, in addition to abnormalities originating from neoplastic clones, non-neoplastic chromosomal abnormalities, including constitutional chromosomal abnormalities, age-related changes, findings originating from transplant donors, and polymorphic findings, may also be detected. Materials and Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 5099 lymph node and bone marrow chromosome tests performed for the diagnosis of hematologic malignancies between January 2016 and December 2025, including repeated examinations in the same patients. We investigated the frequency, distribution, clinical significance, and challenges associated with the interpretation of non-neoplastic chromosomal findings. Results: Non-neoplastic chromosomal findings were identified in 49 cases. These included sex chromosome abnormalities (n=1), chromosomal abnormalities suspected to be constitutional or representative of non-neoplastic mosaicism (n=1), age-related Y chromosome loss (n=15), chromosomal abnormalities thought to be donor-derived following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (n=2), inv(9)(p12q13) (n=29), and both inv(1)(p13q21) and inv(9) (p12q13) (n=1). Discussion: When interpreting these findings, it is necessary to distinguish them from neoplastic abnormalities and to comprehensively consider constitutional background, aging, transplantation history, and polymorphic findings. These findings demonstrate practical issues in the explanation of test results and information management.

en: Familial Persistent Fetal Vasculature Associated with Balanced t(4;7)(p15.3;q36): A Possible Position Effect
ja: 均衡型t(4;7)(p15.3;q36)に関連した家族性胎児血管遺残：位置効果の可能性
abs: Background: Persistent fetal vasculature (PFV), formerly persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous (PHPV), is a congenital ocular disorder caused by failed regression of the fetal hyaloid vasculature. Most cases are sporadic, and familial PFV is rare. Case Presentation: Here, we report PFV-related findings across three generations. The proband was a 35-year-old man diagnosed with PFV of the left eye. He had bilateral microcornea, a mature cataract, and total retinal detachment. Vitreoretinal surgery failed to achieve retinal reattachment, resulting in left-eye loss of vision. G-banding revealed a balanced reciprocal translocation, 46,XY,t(4;7)(p15.3;q36), which was confirmed by FISH. His mother was also diagnosed with PFV. His sister had multiple congenital anomalies involving the heart, limbs, and proptosis, and died at 16 months of age. His daughter was diagnosed with PFV and was found to have microphthalmia, exotropia, and coloboma. Chromosomal microarray analysis revealed a terminal deletion of 4p16.1-p16.3 and a terminal duplication of 7q36.3, both confirmed by subtelomeric FISH. Discussion: Given that the proband carried a balanced translocation, a pathogenic mechanism other than simple gene dosage imbalance is suggested. A position effect associated with the chromosomal rearrangement may have altered the regulation of developmental genes within the 7q36 region, including SHH, a key regulator of ocular and systemic development. Conclusion: Familial PFV associated with t(4;7)(p15.3;q36) suggests a possible position effect involving 7q36 genes in disease pathogenesis.

en: A familial supernumerary der(15) resulting from 3:1 segregation of t(11;15)(q23.3;q12)
ja: t(11;15)(q23.3;q12)の3:1分離による家族性過剰der(15)
abs: Background: Three-to-one segregation in balanced reciprocal translocation carriers may result in a supernumerary derivative chromosome and partial trisomy. We report a patient with a supernumerary der(15) derived from a familial balanced translocation t(11;15)(q23.3;q12). Case Presentation: The patient was a boy with severe developmental delay, congenital heart defects, pharyngeal stenosis, laryngomalacia, hearing loss, and cerebral white matter abnormalities on brain MRI. Chromosome analysis revealed 47,XY,+der(15)t(11;15)(q23.3;q12). His mother carried a balanced reciprocal translocation, 46,XX,t(11;15) (q23.3;q12). Chromosomal microarray analysis demonstrated a 17.7 Mb duplication of 11q23.3-qter and a 7.3 Mb duplication of 15q11.1-q12, consistent with a supernumerary der(15) generated through 3:1 segregation. Discussion: The maternal uncle was also a carrier of the same translocation, and his child reportedly had severe developmental delay with a similar chromosomal imbalance, suggesting recurrence of unbalanced segregation within the family. The proband exhibited severe neurodevelopmental impairment, feeding difficulties, airway abnormalities, epilepsy and white matter abnormalities, overlapping with features of Emanuel syndrome. However, the underlying chromosomal rearrangement differed from the recurrent der(22) associated with t(11;22). Familial supernumerary der(15) resulting from 3:1 segregation of t(11;15)(q23.3;q12) appears extremely rare. This family broadens the phenotypic spectrum associated with partial trisomy of distal 11q and proximal 15q.

en: Chromosomal aberration analysis of healthy individuals aged 19 to 23 detected by 3-color FISH.
ja: 3色FISHで検出した19〜23歳健常者の染色体異常解析
abs: Exchange-type chromosomal aberrations (CAs) in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) are useful for retrospective dosimetry and follow-up studies of over-exposed patients after radiation accidents. The dicentric chromosome frequency ranges from 0 to 0.001 in occupationally non-exposed healthy donors at any age, whereas the background translocation frequency increases with age or uncertain factors [1]. The objective of this pilot study was to investigate individual differences in CAs. To this end, chromosomal analysis was performed using the three-color FISH method with chromosomes 1, 2 and 4 paints, combined with the modified FPG staining [2] on a group of ten healthy donors aged 19 to 23 (non-smokers). The selection of this age group was done by the practical considerations of obtaining informed consent and minimizing the influence of acquired factors. More than 1000 metaphases per donor were analyzed to examine cell kinetics and CAs. As a result, the frequency of 2nd metaphase (M2) ranged from 2.9% to 17.0%. Notethat even M3 and M4 metaphases were observed in some donors. The dicentric frequency of M1 detected by DAPI-stain ranged from 0 to 0.001. The mean translocation frequency of M1 per 100 cell equivalent was 0.59 (95%CI, [0.80, 0.38]). The results give rise to a number of intriguing questions, including those concerning inter-individual differences in subpopulations of PBMCs and responses to reagent, and reconsideration of protocols for dosimetry. [1] IAEA: Cytogenetic Dosimetry, pp. 90-94, IAEA, Vienna, 2011. [2] Miho Akiyama et al., Cytologia 89: 1-8, 2024.

en: Allele-specific DNA methylation profiles of X-chromosome genes detected by long-read sequencing
ja: ロングリードシーケンスで検出したX染色体遺伝子のアレル特異的DNAメチル化プロファイル
abs: [Background] X chromosome contains genes subject to X chromosome inactivation (XCI) (S), escape genes (E) and genes on pseudoautosomal region 1 (PAR1) expressed from both X chromosomes, and variable escape genes (VE). A DNA methylation index of CpGs in the promoter of genes (MI) is elevated in inactive X of S and inversely correlated with gene expression. Although XCI occurs independently of parental origin, comprehensive analysis of parent-of-origin allele-specific MI (ASM) analysis remains limited. [Objective] To clarify ASM profiles of X chromosomal genes. [Methods] We analyzed four individuals with a 46,XX karyotype, and two individuals each with 46,XY, 45,X, and 47,XXY karyotypes. Promoter regions were defined based on ENCODE candidate cis-regulatory elements, and the mean MI was evaluated using Long-read sequencing (LRS). Genes were classified as S, VE, and E and genes on PAR1. We evaluated MI differences (>=0.25) among cases with different karyotypes, and examined δMI (maternal allele - paternal allele) for S in four 46,XX cases. [Results] Most S showed karyotypes-dependent MI. For ASM, the median δMI (minimum, maximum) across S was -0.13 (-0.41, 0.07), -0.02 (-0.26, 0.22), -0.02 (-0.23, 0.19), and -0.68 (-0.85, 0.17) in four 46,XX cases, respectively. [Discussion]δMI varied among S in female individuals, suggesting gene-specific MI on inactive X. XCI effects may be gene-specific, although validation by expression analysis is needed. [Conclusion] We established an ASM analysis system for X chromosome using LRS. The effect of XCI on DNA methylation may be gene-specific.

en: Long-read methylation profiling beyond 11p15.5 canonical imprinting regions in Beckwith- Wiedemann syndrome
ja: Beckwith-Wiedemann症候群における11p15.5の既知インプリンティング領域を超えたロングリードメチル化解析
abs: Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome (BWS) is an imprinting disorder primarily caused by epigenetic alterations at chromosome 11p15.5. Conventional diagnostic approaches for imprinting disorders rely on locus-specific assays and have limited ability to evaluate haplotype-resolved methylation patterns. We applied long-read nanopore sequencing to profile genome-wide DNA methylation patterns in individuals with BWS (n = 10) and controls. Using 5-methylcytosine basecalling, haplotype phasing, and DSS (Dispersion Shrinkage for Sequencing data), we evaluated haplotype-resolved methylation patterns across 48 known imprinted differentially methylated regions (DMRs). At 11p15.5, methylation patterns consistent with established BWS subtypes were observed in all cases: loss of methylation at KCNQ1OT1:TSS-DMR (n = 6), gain of methylation at H19/IGF2:IG- DMR (n = 2), and mosaic paternal uniparental disomy (patUPD) (n = 2). In patUPD cases, phasing across KCNQ1OT1:TSS-DMR or H19/ IGF2:IG-DMR could not be achieved. However, Integrative Genomics Viewer visualization demonstrated skewed methylation read distributions consistent with mosaic patUPD. Among individuals with loss of methylation at KCNQ1OT1:TSS-DMR, additional hypomethylation affecting 2-13 imprinted DMRs per sample was identified, supporting multi-locus imprinting disturbance in a part of BWS patients. These findings suggest that epigenetic abnormalities in BWS extend beyond canonical imprinting regions and demonstrate the utility of haplotype-resolved long-read methylation analysis.

en: Gene-Level m6A Profiling Suggests Decay-Biased mRNA Regulation in Human Trophoblast Stem Cells
ja: 遺伝子レベルのm6Aプロファイリングはヒト栄養膜幹細胞における分解寄りのmRNA制御を示唆する
abs: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) regulates post-transcriptional gene expression via mRNA stability and translation. In human trophoblast stem cells (hTSCs), METTL3 is highly expressed and required for maintenance, while m6A profiles change upon differentiation. However, it remains unclear whether m6A modification mainly contributes to mRNA stabilization or degradation in hTSCs. In this study, we detected m6A modification signals in hTSCs at single-base resolution by Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) and calculated gene-level m6A density scores. We also estimated changes in mRNA stability under DOX-inducible METTL3 depletion using a public Actinomycin D chase RNA-seq dataset of hEPSC-derived TSCs (GSE280039), and integrated these data with DRS-derived m6A density scores. Representative candidate genes were validated using METTL3 inhibitor STM2457, GLORI, ActD chase qPCR, and RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP)-qPCR. Integrated analysis showed that m6A -rich genes tended to exhibit prolonged stability after METTL3 depletion, suggesting direct m6A -mediated decay. Genes destabilized after METTL3 depletion showed limited m6A signals, suggesting indirect regulation. In DLX3, a representative m6A -regulated candidate, GLORI confirmed STM2457-induced reduction of m6A modification on DLX3 mRNA, and ActD chase qPCR showed prolongation of mRNA half-life. RIP-qPCR further confirmed YTHDF1/2 binding to the 3'UTR m6A -enriched region of DLX3 mRNA. Although mRNA fate regulation by m6A is considered highly context-dependent, our findings suggest a bias toward mRNA decay in hTSCs.

en: Real-World Validation of Oxford Nanopore-Based Methylation Classification for Brain Tumors
ja: 脳腫瘍に対するOxford Nanoporeベースのメチル化分類の実臨床での検証
abs: DNA methylation profiling has become an essential component of modern brain tumor diagnosis and is increasingly incorporated into integrated molecular classification schemes. Although array-based methylation classifiers are widely used in clinical practice, they require additional laboratory workflows and often involve prolonged turnaround times. Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) sequencing provides a unique opportunity to simultaneously generate genomic and methylation information from a single assay, potentially streamlining molecular diagnostics. In this study, we evaluated the performance of MethyLYZR for methylation-based classification of brain tumors using ONT sequencing data. A total of 19 brain specimens were analyzed, representing a diverse cohort of CNS tumors, including gliomas, medulloblastomas, ependymomas, meningiomas, germ cell tumors, craniopharyngiomas, and other brain lesions. Pathology diagnoses, DFKZ classifications, and NIH classifications were available for a subset of samples. All specimens underwent ONT sequencing with modified-base detection enabled and were analyzed using MethyLYZR. MethyLYZR predictions were compared with available pathology diagnoses, integrated diagnoses, DFKZ classifications, and NIH classifications. Classification confidence, concordance, and sequencing depth requirements were assessed. MethyLYZR successfully classified 10 samples from 19 samples with 53% concordance to pathological e diagnoses. Furthermore, the real-time nature of nanopore sequencing enabled rapid generation of diagnostic predictions. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of performing brain tumor classification directly from ONT-derived methylation profiles and highlight the potential of MethyLYZR as a rapid and cost-effective approach for integrated molecular diagnostics in neuro-oncology.

en: Integration of blood-based biomarkers and genetic variants identifies intervention-responsive individuals with MCI
ja: 血液バイオマーカーと遺伝的バリアントの統合により介入反応性のMCI者を同定
abs: Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) is a high-risk condition for dementia, and multidomain interventions may delay cognitive decline in older adults with MCI. However, responses vary substantially among individuals. We previously conducted the Japan-Multimodal Intervention Trial for the Prevention of Dementia (J-MINT), a multicenter randomized controlled trial evaluating a multidomain intervention in older adults with MCI. Results from the J-MINT suggested that greater cognitive benefits may be achieved in individuals with specific biological profiles. To identify individuals most likely to benefit from the multidomain intervention, we measured blood-based biomarkers (BBMs) in 269 J-MINT participants. Overall cognitive improvement did not differ significantly between the intervention and control groups. However, hierarchical clustering analysis identified a subgroup characterized by elevated glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) levels and multiple biomarker abnormalities, which showed a significant benefit from the intervention. This subgroup was characterized by four associated genetic variants. Furthermore, a predictive model integrating the four associated variants with clinical variables to identify intervention-responsive individuals achieved a mean area under the curve (AUC) of 0.887 (95% confidence interval, 0.866-0.904). These findings suggest that integrating BBMs and genomic information may help identify individuals with MCI who are responsive to interventions and support the development of personalized prevention strategies for dementia.

en: Genome-wide Association Study of Social Isolation in the Tohoku Medical Megabank Community- Based Cohort Study
abs: Social isolation is increasingly recognized as a public health concern, yet its genetic basis remains poorly understood. We conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) to identify genetic variants associated with social isolation in Japanese adults. We analyzed 63,497 participants from the Tohoku Medical Megabank Community-Based Cohort Study. Social isolation was assessed using the 6-item Lubben Social Network Scale (LSNS-6) and dichotomized with established cutoffs for the total score and family and friend subscales (<12 and <6, respectively). GWASs were performed using generalized linear mixed models adjusted for age, sex, 10 genetic principal components, and genotyping batch. Summary statistics stratified by study site and recruitment route were combined by sample-size-weighted meta-analysis. Social isolation was observed in 25.8%, 14.8%, and 34.1% for the total scale, family subscale, and friend subscale, respectively. Two loci reached genome-wide significance: rs10736933 near ACADSB/HMX3 for the total scale (P = 4.9 × 10-8) and rs1778366 near LINC02315/LRFN5 for the friend subscale (P = 1.1 × 10-8). The family subscale had no significant locus; the top variant was rs780848113 near LMOD1/TIMM17A (P = 4.6 × 10-7). Heritability estimates were 4.0%, 2.4%, and 3.8%, respectively. This GWAS of LSNS-6-defined binary social isolation identified loci associated with overall and friend-related social isolation in Japanese adults. The findings suggest that genetic associations with social isolation may differ by LSNS-6 domain.

en: Sex differences in transcript-level gene expression and differential isoform usage in healthy human cell lines
abs: Aim Biological sex differences such as variations in serum oestrogen levels are well known. However, sex differences in gene expression at the cellular level remain incompletely understood. We investigated whether sex differences exist in gene-level and transcript-level expression. Methods We performed the analysis using RNA-seq data from lymphoblastoid cell lines derived from healthy individuals. Differential expression analysis at the gene and transcript levels was performed using the Subio Platform. Isoform switching analysis was performed using IsoformSwitchAnalyzeR. Results Gene-level analysis identified 186 genes with ≥ 2-fold sex-biased expression. These genes comprised 570 transcripts, among which 164 showed differential expression at both gene and transcript levels, whereas 406 showed no differential expression at either level. Transcript-level analysis identified 1,700 differentially expressed transcripts, including 1,536 detected exclusively at the transcript level. Isoform switching analysis identified 43 genes with significant changes in isoform usage. Conclusion Transcript-level analysis detected sex differences not identified by gene-level analysis. Isoform switching occurred independently of overall gene expression changes, suggesting additional regulatory mechanisms. These findings highlight the importance of transcript-level analysis for understanding sex-associated differences in gene regulation and potential disease susceptibility.

en: Transcriptome-based endotyping of eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis using nasal brushing samples
abs: Background: Eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis (ECRS) is a clinically heterogeneous disorder that is frequently severe and resistant to conventional treatment. We have previously demonstrated that nasal brushing, a minimally invasive technique, could elucidate the pathophysiology of ECRS. In this study, we aimed to validate these findings in an expanded cohort. Methods: Nasal brushing specimens were collected from the ethmoidal mucosa in the middle meatus. Bulk RNA sequencing was performed on samples from 41 patients with ECRS and 11 controls to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Hierarchical clustering of the 41 patients with ECRS was performed using the top 100 DEGs. In addition, CIBERSORTx was used to infer cellular composition from bulk RNA-seq data. Results: RNA-seq analysis of nasal brushing samples identified 1,225 DEGs between ECRS patients and controls, including 1,019 upregulated and 206 downregulated genes. Hierarchical clustering based on the top 100 DEGs classified ECRS patients into three distinct transcriptomic clusters. Cluster 1 was associated with a significantly lower postoperative recurrence rate than clusters 2 and 3. Cell-type deconvolution analysis indicated that nasal brushing samples comprised epithelial cells as well as diverse immune cell populations, including NK cells, macrophages, and mast cells. Conclusion: Minimally invasive nasal brushing combined with transcriptomic profiling provides a useful approach for molecular endotyping of ECRS and may help predict clinical outcomes, including postoperative recurrence.

en: Ancient Jomon Blood Group Genotypes Illuminate the Evolutionary History of Red Blood Cell Antigens
abs: Blood type systems, determined by antigen variation on red blood cells, are widely used genetic markers, including the ABO, RHCE and MNS systems. However, blood group variation in the Jomon, a Neolithic population representing a basal lineage of East Asians, remains poorly characterized beyond limited data from Hokkaido and a small number of systems. In this study, we analyzed blood group-associated variants and inferred genotypes using previously published whole-genome sequencing data from 18 ancient Jomon individuals sampled across the Japanese archipelago (Hokkaido, Honshu, Shikoku, and Kyushu). While ABO variation showed little differentiation from present-day East Asians, Jomon individuals exhibited distinctive allele patterns in several systems, including RHCE*E, GYPB*S, and FUT1*01.02. These findings highlight the distinct red blood cell antigen variation in the Jomon and underscore the value of inferring blood group genotypes from ancient genomes for understanding human population history, as well as the evolutionary dynamics of immune-related genetic variation.

en: Association Study of Sensory-Cognitive Phenotypes and SNPs toward Personalized Healthcares
abs: Taste and olfactory preferences represent complex polygenic traits influenced by sensory, metabolic, and neurobiological determinants. Although associations between specific SNPs and diseases via sensory traits are reported in some studies, their molecular basis requires further elucidation for clinical application. This study examines correlations between SNPs and sensory-cognitive phenotypes to establish a foundation for future studies on personalized healthcare. A total of 108 completed questionnaires were collected from participants aged 20 years or older. Phenotypic data including aroma discrimination, taste perception, and overall preference were collected using two contrasting wine styles to emphasize distinct sensory characteristics as evaluation metrics. Salivary genetic data regarding taste, olfaction, and alcohol metabolism were statistically analyzed against questionnaire-based phenotypic responses. This study was approved by the ethics committees of the Institute of Medical Science, The University of Tokyo and A. D. A. M. Innovations Co. Associations between SNPs and wine-related phenotypes, such as aroma discrimination and taste perception, were analyzed. This pilot study was conducted to identify candidate SNPs and estimate sample sizes for future validation studies. Despite limitations such as a small sample size and subjective questionnaire bias, we plan to expand targeted SNPs and cases. We aim to contribute to improve quality of life through preventive personalized healthcare.

en: Founder Effect of IVS4+919G>A Variant in Fabry Disease in Japan: A Historical Population Diffusion Perspective
abs: More than 800 GLA mutations causing Fabry disease are known, but founder effects due to single gene variant have been reported in Taiwan (IVS4+919G>A). The first report of this variant in Japan was by Ishii S et al (2002). Inoue T et al. (2013) identified Fabry disease patients with pathogenic variants, including this variant, in a pilot study of newborn screening in Fukuoka City and its vicinity in Japan. Based on these reports, we hypothesized that the presence of the variant in Japan (especially Kyushu) is related to historical population mobility. The terms "Minato" (Port) and "Tojin-machi" (Chinese settlements) provide evidence of inflows into Japan through trade across the East China Sea (such as Japanese pirates and Japan-Ming trade). "To" in "Tojin-machi" is a place name that has existed in the inner part of Kyushu, and it suggests that a group with the same variant expanded inland via the "Highways". Liang KH et al. (2020) analyzed the haplotype and reported that the variant originated from a single ancestor and occurred in China more than 800 years ago. It may also imply that Japanese patients share the same haplotype. Yoshida S et al. (2020) reported patients with this variant in Fabry high-risk screening in Japan, demonstrating a geographical distribution that extends beyond Kyushu. This study analyzed trade connections and the geographic distribution of the variant using place names as indicators, examining the historical movements of population and considering the role of "Ports" as hubs for maritime transportation and "Highways" as routes for land transport.

en: Exploring balancing selection in the human genome through trans-species polymorphisms
abs: Balancing selection is an evolutionary process that maintains multiple allelic variants in a population over long periods of time. Such long-term maintenance of variation can contribute to adaptation and may be particularly important in genomic regions related to immune response and host-pathogen interactions. This study aimed to identify candidate regions in the human genome that may have been shaped by balancing selection. To detect such regions, we focused on trans-species polymorphisms (TSPs), which are genetic variants shared between humans and closely related primates. Because humans and other great apes diverged millions of years ago, shared polymorphisms may reflect ancient variation that has persisted across species. We compared human population genomic data with genomic data from non-human primates to search for TSP candidates. The analysis identified regions consistent with long-term balancing selection. Some candidates were located near genes related to immune function, including pathways potentially involved in pathogen recognition, inflammation, and host defense. Others were found near genes associated with neurological function, sensory perception, and other physiological traits. These results suggest that balancing selection may affect functions beyond immune response alone. By combining evidence from shared polymorphisms and patterns of variation within human populations, this study narrows down candidate regions for balancing selection and provides a basis for understanding how ancient genetic variation contributed to present-day human diversity.

en: Population-scale analysis of predicted loss-of-function variants in the TMM 100K whole-genome resource
abs: Population-scale whole-genome sequencing (WGS) resources are essential for understanding the impact of rare functional variants on human phenotypes. The Tohoku Medical Megabank (TMM) Project has performed WGS on ~100,000 Japanese individuals and constructed a reference panel of ~61,000 unrelated individuals. Here, we characterized predicted loss-of-function (pLoF) variants and examined their population-level features in the Japanese population. Variant annotation was performed using Variant Effect Predictor and LOFTEE to identify high-confidence pLoF variants, including stop-gained, frameshift, and essential splice-site variants. In the ~61K reference panel, we identified ~157,000 autosomal pLoF variants, >99% of which were rare (minor allele frequency <1%). Comparison with gnomAD showed fewer observed pLoF variants than in global populations but similar numbers to East Asian datasets, reflecting population-specific variation patterns. The per-individual pLoF burden was consistent with previous large-scale sequencing studies, averaging ~220 pLoF variants per individual. Gene-level pLoF counts were generally concordant with gnomAD, although several genes, including MUC family genes and clonal hematopoiesis-associated genes such as DNMT3A and TET2, showed notable deviations. Most identified pLoF variants were absent from ClinVar, indicating substantial unexplored functional variation in the Japanese population. These results provide a large-scale reference for pLoF variation in the Japanese population and support future disease genetics studies.

en: Germline Testing Uptake after Mismatch Repair Immunohistochemistry in Endometrial Cancer Patients at Our Institution
abs: Lynch syndrome (LS) is a hereditary cancer syndrome caused by pathogenic variants in DNA mismatch repair (MMR) genes, and endometrial cancer is a major LS-associated tumor. Although insurance coverage for MMR immunohistochemistry (MMR-IHC) has recently expanded in Japan, uptake of subsequent germline testing remains low. This study evaluated germline testing uptake after MMR- IHC in endometrial cancer patients at our institution. We retrospectively reviewed endometrial cancer patients who underwent MMR-IHC after February 2025. At our institution, MMR-IHC is recommended for surgical cases with advanced disease, high-risk histology, or a family history of LS-related cancers. We assessed MMR abnormality patterns, germline testing uptake, and results. Among 41 surgical cases, seven underwent MMR-IHC. Five showed deficient MMR, but only two proceeded to germline testing. Three declined testing because it was not covered by insurance. Patients who accepted testing were influenced by family history of aggressive LS-related tumors or concern for their adult children. Among patients with MSH2 loss, one had a pathogenic germline variant and one declined testing. Among those with MLH1/PMS2 loss, one tested negative and two declined testing. In conclusion, germline testing uptake was low. Financial burden and the absence of a strong family history may reduce acceptance. Because LS-related endometrial cancer may not show the classic family history seen in colorectal cancer, greater awareness and broader screening strategies may be needed in Japan.

en: The factors affecting the surveillance of HBOC-associated cancers and the genetic testing for at-risk relatives
abs: Background: The detection of hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome (HBOC) has increased with companion diagnostics and comprehensive genomic profiling. Although surveillance of the probands for HBOC-associated cancers and genetic testing of at risk-relatives are recommended after the genetic confirmation of the probands, they are not always performed. We evaluated factors affecting their implementations. Methods: Fifteen patients diagnosed as HBOC at our institution between January 2024 and December 2025 (BRACAnalysis, MyChoice, or CGP) were analyzed. We assessed the impact of the probands' disease status at the genetic confirmation of HBOC and the genetic counseling on the surveillance rates for HBOC-associated cancers and the genetic testing rates of at-risk relatives with chi square test. Results: The surveillance of the probands for HBOC-associated cancers was performed in 5/8 patients with stable disease and 0/7 with unstable disease, that was statistically significant. The genetic testing of HBOC for at-risk relatives was performed in 1/8 stable cases and 4/7 unstable cases with a trend toward higher testing when the proband's disease was unstable. However, the genetic counseling of the probands did not influence the surveillance rates of the probands for HBOC-associated cancers and the genetic testing rates of HBOC for at-risk relatives. Conclusion: At HBOC diagnosis, the probands' disease status rather than the genetic counseling was associated with implementation of the surveillance for HBOC-associated cancers and the genetic testing of at-risk relatives.

en: Risk-reducing surgery patterns and clinical predictors in BRCA1/2 carriers with prior breast cancer
abs: [Background] Risk-reducing mastectomy (RRM) and risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy (RRSO) for BRCA1/2 pathogenic variant carriers became insurance-covered in Japan in 2020. Factors associated with risk-reducing surgery selection in HBOC patients with prior breast cancer remain unclear. [Methods] Among 59 HBOC patients with prior breast cancer diagnosed since April 2020, 38 who underwent risk-reducing surgery were analyzed. Patients were classified into RRM alone (n=6), RRM+RRSO (n=16), and RRSO alone (n=16). Primary analysis compared patients undergoing RRM (n=22) with those undergoing RRSO alone (n=16). Factors included age at HBOC diagnosis, timing of BRCA testing, BRCA1/2 status, breast cancer subtype, family history, reproductive history, neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC), and contralateral RRM (CRRM). [Results] Median age at HBOC diagnosis was 41.2, 43.8, and 55.5 years across the three groups. Preoperative BRCA testing rates were 100%, 68.8%, and 43.8%, respectively, and were significantly higher in the RRM group than in the RRSO-alone group (77.3% vs. 43.8%; p=0.047). Non-luminal subtype and NAC use were more frequent in the RRM group. CRRM was concurrently performed in 68.2% of RRM cases. No significant differences were observed in BRCA1/2 status, family history, or reproductive history. [Conclusion] Preoperative BRCA testing was significantly associated with RRM selection. Earlier genetic diagnosis during breast cancer treatment may facilitate consideration of prophylactic breast surgery and contribute to individualized risk-reduction strategies.

en: Reconstruction of disease understanding during life stage transitions for female carriers of Barth syndrome
abs: Background: Barth syndrome(BS) is an X-linked disorder caused by pathogenic TAFAZZIN variants, characterized by multisystem manifestations requiring medical care from infancy. We report two genetic counseling(GC) sessions for a female carrier and her mother, conducted five years apart, which facilitated disease understanding tailored to life-stage and family context. Case: A woman in her twenties was identified as a carrier following her brothers' diagnoses of BS, leading to referral of her and her mother to our GC clinic. At the initial GC, she struggled to comprehend the implications of her carrier status, and ongoing GC opportunities were assured. Five years later, as she entered a relationship with a prospective marriage partner, she requested a second GC with her mother to better understand and explain the condition to her partner. GC addressed disease course, inheritance, and the importance of early intervention. Her mother had initially expressed negative feelings toward genetic testing and family disclosure, but following the second GC, both adopted a positive perspective, recognizing its value for the next generation. Discussion: The client's awareness of her carrier status was initially limited, but her informational needs evolved with life-stage transitions. These GC appeared most effective when aligned with psychosocial circumstances and stages of acceptance, offering support for mother and daughter. For female carriers of X-linked disorders, GC should be regarded as a continuing process that reframes genetic information and supports adaptation across life stages.

en: Genetic counseling for two couples who decided to continue pregnancy after a prenatal diagnosis of trisomy 21
abs: Introduction: We report two couples who, following positive maternal serum screening (MSS) or NIPT results, had a diagnosis of fetal trisomy 21 (T21) by amniocentesis and decided to continue their pregnancies. We discuss their conflicts in decision-making and the role of continuous genetic counseling (GC). Case 1: A 43-year-old woman (G2P1) had a positive MSS. Amniocentesis confirmed T21, and the couple was referred for GC. She had thought of continuation of pregnancy but had hesitation considering social trends in Japan that most decided termination after definitive diagnosis. We provided information on expected welfare support for the baby and discussed possible psychological burden of termination. She decided to continue the pregnancy, realizing the reality of raising the child and the psychological burden of termination unbearable for her. Case 2: A 38-year-old woman (G3P0, 2 miscarriages) underwent NIPT. Despite her pre-test intention to continue the pregnancy regardless of the result, her anxiety escalated hearing the positive result. Through GC, we provided information and discussed. After confirmation of the diagnosis by amniocentesis, she decided to continue the pregnancy. Discussion: : Prior to screening, both couples agreed that they would unlikely consider termination. However, the definitive diagnosis triggered their hesitation, driven by anxieties about rearing the baby with T21 and confronting negative social trends. These experiences highlight the critical role in GC of information on welfare support for the baby and realization of termination process.

en: The Role of Certified Genetic Counselors for Families with Hereditary Tumor Syndromes Diagnosed during Childhood
abs: Background: Familial genetic counseling has increased as hereditary tumor syndromes are increasingly identified in pediatric cancer patients through paired tumor panel sequencing. While genetic counseling (GC) highlights medical benefits such as surveillance and risk-reducing surgery, Certified Genetic Counselors (CGCs) must also address concerns, stress, and conflicts related to familial cancer predisposition as well as the cancer treatment of the proband. We evaluated the roles of CGCs and optimal support models. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed two families with pediatric cancer patients diagnosed with hereditary tumor syndromes in whom pathogenic variants in BRCA2 and TP53 were identified through paired tumor panel sequencing. CGCs supported these families, who experienced difficulties in decision-making, psychosocial distress, and complex family dynamics. We analyzed their clinical courses, psychological responses, and multidisciplinary interventions. Results: Decision-making support helped families understand genetic issues, including testing of at-risk relatives such as siblings of the proband and management of unaffected variant carriers. This support facilitated decisions consistent with family values. However, conflicts and anxiety persisted after standard GC sessions, indicating the need for ongoing support and interdisciplinary collaboration with pediatric oncologists and geneticists. Conclusion: CGCs should establish a seamless multidisciplinary framework between clinical genetics and oncology departments to address persistent psychosocial vulnerabilities.

en: Clinical Features and Genetic Counseling in Three Patients with Wiedemann-Steiner Syndrome
abs: Background: Wiedemann-Steiner syndrome (WSS) is a rare autosomal dominant disorder characterized by short stature, developmental delay, hypertrichosis, and distinctive facial features, caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in KMT2A. Objective: To report the clinical and genetic features of three patients with WSS and discuss important findings for clinical diagnosis and genetic counseling. Patients: We report three female patients with WSS (age at diagnosis: Cases 1 and 2, 6 years; Case 3, 15 years). Common findings included developmental delay, short stature, hypertrichosis, growth hormone deficiency, and characteristic facial features with down-slanting and narrow palpebral fissures. In addition, Case 2 had avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder, and Case 3 had cervical vertebral fusion anomalies.
