Trio whole-exome sequencing identified heterozygous pathogenic KMT2A variants in all patients (Case 1: c.676delC, p.Thr225fs; Case 2: c.8806_8809del, p.Val2936* ; Case 3: c.5251A>T, p.Lys1751*). The variants in Cases 1 and 3 occurred de novo, whereas the mother of Case 2 showed mosaicism for the variant. Discussion/ Conclusion: In addition to short stature and developmental delay, hypertrichosis, and characteristic facial features are important clues for the clinical diagnosis of WSS; however, diagnosis based on clinical findings may be difficult because of the nonspecific manifestations. Trio whole-exome sequencing is therefore useful for establishing the diagnosis. The parental mosaicism in Case 2 highlights an important consideration for genetic counseling.

en: Current Status and Challenges of a Preconception Care System for Patients with Hereditary Diseases
abs: Background Our department launched a preconception care clinic in February 2024 for women with medical or hereditary conditions who have concerns regarding future pregnancy and childbirth. However, utilization of preconception care among patients with hereditary diseases remains unclear. Methods We retrospectively reviewed patients managed and delivered at our institution between February 2024 and February 2025. We evaluated the implementation of preconception care and genetic counseling among patients with hereditary diseases or hereditary risk pregnancies. Results During the study period, 33 patients attended the preconception care clinic. Only two sought counseling because of hereditary diseases: one with familial adenomatous polyposis and one with Marfan syndrome. During the same period, eight pregnancies complicated by hereditary diseases and five with hereditary fetal risk were managed. Among these 13 cases, six underwent genetic counseling, but none had received preconception care before pregnancy. In six cases, genetic counseling was initiated only after hereditary risks became apparent during pregnancy. Discussion Despite the presence of hereditary diseases and hereditary risk pregnancies, preconception care utilization was limited. Genetic counseling was frequently initiated after conception, reducing opportunities for reproductive decision-making and maternal risk assessment before pregnancy. These findings highlight the need to improve awareness of preconception care and its role in genetic medicine among both healthcare providers and the public.

en: Current Status of Prenatal Genetic Counseling and Prenatal Testing at Our Center
abs: At our center, prenatal genetic counseling is provided by a multidisciplinary team, including clinical geneticists, through two outpatient clinics per week. Referral indications include advanced maternal age, suspected fetal abnormalities on ultrasound, a previous child with congenital anomalies, and concerns regarding medication exposure during pregnancy. Between 2021 and 2025, a total of 1,570 prenatal genetic counseling sessions were conducted. Following counseling, prenatal testing included 1,103 non-invasive prenatal tests (NIPT), 110 maternal serum screening tests, and 67 amniocenteses (overlapping cases included). Approximately 70% of patients chose NIPT. Among NIPTs performed at our center, 14 were positive and 4 were inconclusive. Of the 14 positive cases, 3 resulted in miscarriage or stillbirth and 11 underwent termination of pregnancy after confirmatory testing. Among the 4 inconclusive cases, 3 were negative on repeat testing, while 1 was diagnosed with a chromosomal abnormality by amniocentesis and subsequently miscarried. Our center is a certified core facility within the national NIPT program and a regional perinatal medical center. Referrals of NIPT-positive patients from affiliated institutions have increased in recent years. We provide comprehensive counseling and decision-making support for patients with positive NIPT results, fetal abnormalities, or suspected genetic disorders. As NIPT use expands, demand for specialized prenatal genetic counseling continues to increase, highlighting the important role of certified NIPT centers in regional prenatal care.

en: PGT-M genetic counseling in a family harboring the mitochondrial m.8363G>A variant
abs: Background: The mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) variant m.8363G>A in MT-TK, encoding mitochondrial tRNA-Lys, is associated with Leigh syndrome, MERRF-like features, cardiomyopathy, and hearing loss. Although higher mutant loads have been linked to disease, a reliable heteroplasmy level (HL) threshold for predicting severity has not been established. We report a family with m.8363G>A who sought genetic counseling (GC) regarding preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic disorders (PGT-M). Case presentation: The proband developed recurrent vomiting and developmental delay at 5 months. At 8 months, dysphagia and lactic acidosis emerged, followed by death from heart failure. Brain MRI showed bilateral basal ganglia abnormalities, and homoplasmic m.8363G>A in blood confirmed Leigh syndrome. The proband's mother had a blood HL of 64% and remained asymptomatic. She and her partner, residing in the United States, visited our university hospital for GC regarding PGT-M in Japanese. We discussed uncertainty in genotype-phenotype correlation and limitations of PGT-M. The mother preferred male embryos to avoid passing on a similar emotional burden. The couple ultimately chose to pursue PGT-M in the United States. Discussion: PGT-M for mtDNA disorders aims to reduce severe disease risk by selecting embryos with low HL; however, phenotype prediction remains difficult because of the mitochondrial bottleneck and tissue-specific heteroplasmy. This case highlights the complexity of reproductive decision-making for mtDNA disorders and the importance of GC under prognostic uncertainty.

en: HBOC Identified as a Secondary Finding in HemeSight Gene Panel Test for Breast Malignant Lymphoma: A Case Report
abs: Introduction: Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) is increasingly used for hematologic malignancies and may reveal hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes as secondary findings, requiring appropriate genetic counseling (GC). Case: The proband was a 47-year-old woman who received a HemeSight genetic panel test to investigate the genetic background of the breast diffuse large B-cell lymphoma . She had been diagnosed with colorectal cancer in their forties., and her mother had died of breast cancer in her 30s. The analysis identified a pathogenic variant in the BRCA2 gene (c.8504C>A, p.Ser2835Ter; variant allele frequency, 44%) as a secondary finding, raising suspicion of HBOC syndrome. Using peripheral blood, we performed BRACAnalysis and confirmed the result. Discussion: Primary breast lymphoma is extremely rare, accounting for less than 0.5% of all malignant breast tumors. To our knowledge, no primary breast lymphoma directly linked to a germline BRCA2 (gBRCA2) pathogenic variant has been reported before. However, the report from overseas have demonstrated an association between gBRCA2 pathogenic variants and non-Hodgkin lymphoma in CAYA generation. This is an atypical case of HBOC, and the proband has two young daughters. Although evidence regarding risks of the future tumor event is limited, ongoing genetic counseling with careful consideration of the timing and approach to sharing genetic information with children, together with longitudinal support through a multidisciplinary team, may be useful for at-risk relatives.

en: Current Status and Challenges of Genetic Counseling for MSI-High Cases at Our Institution
abs: [Background] Microsatellite instability (MSI) testing is an important biomarker for determining eligibility for immune checkpoint inhibitors. MSI-H may also indicate Lynch syndrome and prompt consideration of genetic counseling (GC) and genetic testing. However, referral of MSI-H cases to genetic services varies among institutions. [Objective] To evaluate GC implementation for MSI-H cases at our institution and identify operational challenges through a physician questionnaire survey. [Methods] We retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent MSI testing at our institution between January 2020 and December 2025. Clinical characteristics, GC, and additional testing were assessed. A questionnaire was administered to physicians who had ordered MSI testing regarding GC referral, awareness of GC, and collaboration with the genetics department. [Results] Among 879 patients who underwent MSI testing, 97 were MSI-H. GC was performed in 13 cases, and genetic testing for Lynch syndrome in 4. Awareness of genetics department notifications was reported by 37.5% of physicians; all had experience offering GC. Reasons for not offering GC included patient age and poor general condition. Reasons patients declined GC included low interest in hereditary cancer, cost concerns, and poor health. [Discussion] Despite widespread use of MSI testing, referral of MSI-H cases to genetic services remained limited at our institution. Both physician-and patient-related factors appeared to contribute. More effective strategies are needed to facilitate referral of MSI-H cases to genetic services.

en: A Multi-Axis Cell-State Framework for Decoding Tumor Microenvironment Heterogeneity and Immunotherapy Response
cat: 優秀演題賞（ポスター）候補
abs: The tumor microenvironment (TME) influences cancer progression and immunotherapy response. Traditional bulk RNA–seq with deconvolution methods provides only averaged immune compositions, failing to capture distinct immune states. Ecotypes, representing functional immune ecosystems, remain poorly characterized in clinical significance. To address this, we introduce Deep Semi–NMF, a multi– layered non–negative matrix factorization approach that uncovers hierarchical immune patterns. Applying this to samples across 16 cancer types from TCGA, we identified diverse immune cell states with deeper layers capturing metabolic reprogramming and cytotoxic activity. These states were mapped to ecotypes, and some specific ecotypes correlated with improved survival, while others contributed to immune suppression and tumor immune evasion. Ecotype classification enables patient stratification based on immune landscape, offering applications in predicting immunotherapy response. By refining immune cell state resolution and linking ecotypes to clinical outcomes, this study advances precision tumor immunophenotyping and personalized cancer immunotherapy.

en: Division state identifies dynamic genetic regulation during T-cell activation and immune disease-linked gene programmes
cat: 優秀演題賞（ポスター）候補
abs: A major challenge in human genetics is to connect disease risk variants to the cellular functions they perturb. Variants associated with immune-mediated disease (IMD) have implicated T-cell activation as a disease-causal process; however, it remains elusive whether these variants act on pathways initiating cell division, driving effector differentiation, or maintaining proliferative capacity. Activated T-cells comprise mixtures of cells after different numbers of divisions, obscuring genetic effects that act at specific stages of this process. Here, we generate a division-resolved single-cell atlas of 112,454 CD4+ T-cells, showing that 34.4% of genes exhibit division-dependent regulation. We develop CellDivider, a deep learning model that infers proliferative state from single-cell transcriptomes (r=0.881), enabling cohort-level analysis of proliferation phenotypes. Single-cell dynamic eQTL models incorporating division state, inferred in 655,349 T-cells from 119 individuals, reveal regulatory effects that are missed when the heterogeneity is ignored. Finally, we resolve gene-expression programmes that govern distinct stages of T-cell activation and proliferation. Polygenic IMD risk preferentially converges on early activation and differentiation modules, rather than on proliferative capacity itself. Consistently, division-resolved analysis of the pleiotropic immune risk gene RPS26 localises its genetic effects to early division states, providing mechanistic insight. Our findings illustrate how resolving dynamic cellular consequences sharpens variant-to-function inference.

en: Genome-wide association study of blood cell traits in a Japanese general population cohort
cat: 優秀演題賞（ポスター）候補
abs: Blood cell parameters are highly polygenic quantitative traits influenced by genetic and environmental factors. Large-scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS), particularly in European cohorts, have identified thousands of loci associated with haematological phenotypes, highlighting strong genetic contributions to inter-individual variation. However, fewer studies have examined these traits in East Asian populations. We performed GWAS for multiple blood cell traits in ~55,000 individuals from a Japanese general population cohort using REGENIE, a generalised linear mixed model based on whole-genome regression that accounts for population structure and relatedness. Models were adjusted for age, sex, smoking status, and four principal components of genetic ancestry. We identified multiple genome-wide significant loci across red blood cell traits, haemoglobin, haematocrit, and red cell indices (MCV, MCH, MCHC), many consistent with known haematological loci. To assess combined genetic effects, polygenic risk scores (PRS) were constructed and tested for association with each trait. PRS showed significant associations across all phenotypes, although explained variance was modest (change in R2 < 1% in most traits). These results demonstrate that blood cell traits in Japanese individuals are strongly polygenic and largely consistent with global genetic architecture. Overall, our study highlights the importance of identifying genetic loci underlying baseline variation in blood cell traits.

en: Reclassification of a PRKAR1A Splice-Site variant of uncertain significance in Carney complex
cat: 優秀演題賞（ポスター）候補
abs: Background: Carney complex (CNC) is a rare autosomal dominant disorder characterized by myxomas, pigmented skin lesions, and endocrine tumors. Loss-of-function variants in PRKAR1A are a major cause of CNC. We functionally evaluated a PRKAR1A splice-site variant initially classified as a variant of uncertain significance (VUS) in a patient clinically diagnosed with CNC. Case: A 31-year-old woman presented with Cushing`s syndrome due to primary pigmented nodular adrenal, and bilateral breast myxomas, leading to a clinical diagnosis of CNC. Genetic testing identified a splice-site variant in PRKAR1A (NM_002734.5:c.177+3A>G). Although absent from population databases and meeting PM2_Supporting, the variant remained a VUS because its effect on splicing was unclear. Functional analysis: cDNA analysis revealed two aberrant transcripts: a 10-bp deletion at the 3` end of exon 2 and a 28-bp insertion derived from intron 2, both causing frameshifts. These splicing abnormalities were recapitulated in the minigene assay. qPCR demonstrated that wild-type PRKAR1A transcript levels were reduced to approximately 50% of control levels. Cycloheximide treatment increased the levels of the two aberrant transcripts identified by cDNA analysis, indicating that both transcripts undergo nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD). Conclusion: This variant induces abnormal splicing and subsequent NMD, consistent with a loss-of-function mechanism. These findings supported the application of PVS1, leading to reclassification of this VUS as pathogenic.

en: Establishment of a Runx2 missense mouse model of cleidocranial dysplasia and identification of a novel dental phenotype
cat: 優秀演題賞（ポスター）候補
abs: The causative gene for cleidocranial dysplasia (CCD), Runt-related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2), encodes a transcription factor with a conserved Runt homology domain (RHD) that mediates DNA binding and heterodimerization. Human patients with CCD exhibit clavicular and cranial malformations, along with dental abnormalities such as prolonged retention of deciduous teeth, delayed eruption of permanent teeth, and multiple supernumerary teeth, resulting from RUNX2 haploinsufficiency. In Runx2-null heterozygous mice, skeletal abnormalities are also observed, whereas the dental phenotype is limited to mild delayed tooth eruption. Loss of intramembranous ossification in Runx2-null homozygous mice demonstrated that Runx2 is a key transcription factor for osteogenesis. In this study, we generated Runx2 p.R232Q mutant mice using Platinum TALENs and a single-stranded oligonucleotide, corresponding to the human RUNX2 p.R225Q mutation, a missense mutation of the RHD where point mutations are frequently reported. We characterized the Runx2 missense protein in vivo and demonstrated that intramembranous bone formation is abolished in homozygous mutant mice. In heterozygous mutants, we identified not only skeletal abnormalities characteristic of CCD patients but also a novel dental phenotype in which small tooth-root-like structures were observed at the furcation of the three roots of the maxillary first molar. These findings establish a missense Runx2 mouse model of CCD that recapitulates key disease features and reveal a previously unrecognized role in tooth root morphogenesis.

en: Aberrant transcripts of BRCA1/BRCA2 in T cells of breast cancer patients without pathogenic variant by BRACAnalysis
cat: 優秀演題賞（ポスター）候補
abs: <Background> Genetic testing of BRCA1/BRCA2 genes, such as BRACAnalysis has become available in Japan as being covered by a national insurance system. Though, highly suspected as HBOC, some patients receive testing reports with genetic result of VUS even no alterations. We performed further analysis to explorer possible alterations in BRCA1/BRCA2. <Patients> Patient #1 suffered from metachronous bilateral breast cancer at ages 45 and 71. Her father developed pancreatic cancer at 82 y.o.. BRACAnalysis reported exon 1 duplication with a pathogenicity classification of VUS. Patient #2 suffered from right breast cancer at age of 45. She has a condensed family history of 7 members of breast cancer. Multigene panel testing showed no pathogenic variant in 31 hereditary tumor related genes. <Methods> We conducted RNA sequence using cultured T cells of these 2 patients. <Results> Patient #1. We confirmed the duplication of fragment including the exon 1 of BRCA1 by MLPA and long-read whole genome sequence. We detect aberrant transcripts coded by intron 1 of BRCA11. Further RT-PCR analysis demonstrated that this transcript was anti-sense one. Patient #2. We detected an activation of reported cryptic exon with 64 bp coded by intron 20 of BRCA2. This resulted in truncation of BRCA2 (p.Glu2878Valfs*22). <Discussion> For those patients of highly suspected as HBOC with VUS, inconclusive, or even no alterations, long-read whole genome sequencing and RNA sequence analysis may be an informative alternate to explore the pathogenic variants in BRCA1/BRCA2 genes.

en: Secondary BRCA2 Findings in Pediatric Exome Sequencing: Clinical and Ethical Challenges in Cascade Testing
cat: 優秀演題賞（ポスター）候補
abs: A pediatric patient with continuous fever underwent clinical exome sequencing for diagnostic evaluation. Besides the primary disease-associated variant, a pathogenic BRCA2 variant (rs886040788) was incidentally identified as a secondary finding. BRCA2 is included in the ACMG secondary findings list for hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome (HBOC). However, since HBOC usually manifests in adulthood, predictive testing should generally be deferred in childhood. This case raised several practical and ethical challenges. First, although confirmatory testing is required in Japan for insured HBOC surveillance, the pediatric proband was not an appropriate target. Second, no apparent family history suggestive of HBOC had been recognized in this case, complicating family risk communication. Third, the clinical benefit was expected to apply mainly to adult relatives, such as parents, rather than to the child. In this context, the focus of genetic counseling shifted from patient-centered disclosure to family-oriented risk communication and cascade testing. Consideration was given to how secondary findings identified in pediatric genomic testing should be communicated with parents, how adult relatives should be approached for confirmatory testing and surveillance, and how current insurance systems may not adequately accommodate secondary findings from comprehensive analysis. This case highlights the growing need for practical frameworks integrating pediatric ethics, future autonomy, secondary findings management, and family-based preventive care in the genomic medicine era.

en: Epidemiology of Mortality and Stillbirths in Down Syndrome Using Japanese Vital Statistics
cat: 優秀演題賞（ポスター）候補
abs: Objective: Life expectancy among individuals with Down syndrome (DS) has increased substantially; however, recent trends in mortality and stillbirths remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to describe the status, temporal trends, and age-at-death patterns of deaths and stillbirths associated with DS. Methods: We conducted a descriptive epidemiological analysis using nationwide vital statistics data. Annual numbers of deaths and stillbirths, age at death, mortality rates, and temporal trends were evaluated from 2013 to 2024. Results: A total of 3,404 deaths and 166 stillbirths associated with DS were identified during the study period. The median age at death was 57 years, with a maximum age of 91 years. Deaths were concentrated in adulthood, particularly among individuals aged 50 years or older. In contrast, the annual number of stillbirths fluctuated over time. The mortality rate per 100,000 total births approximately doubled during the study period. An increase in mortality rates was observed between 2021 and 2022, which may have been partly attributable to a decline in total births. Discussion: Taken together with previous reports, these findings suggest that individuals with DS may be transitioning from a phase of rapidly increasing life expectancy to a new stage characterized by sustained longevity and a plateau in survival gains. There is an increasing need to establish comprehensive support systems for adults with DS. Future planning should consider both mortality trends and changes in birth prevalence to optimize lifelong care for individuals with DS.
